stories.title: Assam floods have now killed 66 people and affected 6.5 lakh more, as Union Minister Sonowal calls the situation 'extremely critical'
stories.what_happened: Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal visited flood relief camps in Sivasagar district and described the situation as 'extremely critical,' as Assam's flood death toll for the season reached 66 and more than 6.5 lakh people across six districts remain affected. The state is running 274 relief camps and distribution centres, currently sheltering close to 19,000 displaced people, with the National and State Disaster Response Forces (NDRF/SDRF) continuing rescue and relief operations alongside the Centre.
key_points: Death toll from this year's Assam floods has reached 66
Over 6.5 lakh (650,000) people affected across six districts
Sivasagar is worst-hit, with roughly 3 lakh people impacted
274 relief camps are housing nearly 19,000 displaced people; NDRF/SDRF running rescues

depth.background: Assam faces destructive monsoon flooding most years, as the Brahmaputra river and its tributaries swell with heavy rain and overflow their banks across the state's low-lying districts. This year's flood season has been especially severe, compounding an already-active monsoon that has also triggered fresh IMD (India Meteorological Department) rain alerts elsewhere in the country this week.

stories.title: Chamika Karunaratne's 72* off 34 fires Galle Gallants to the top of the Lanka Premier League table
stories.what_happened: Galle Gallants posted 220 for 6, powered by an unbeaten 72 off 34 balls from Chamika Karunaratne, with useful contributions from Sam Harper, Nurul Hasan, Charith Asalanka and Sahan Arachchige. Dambulla Sixers got a promising start from Niroshan Dickwella in the chase but collapsed once wickets started falling, never mounting a serious threat beyond the powerplay, and Galle Gallants moved to the top of the table with eight points.
key_points: Galle Gallants posted 220/6, driven by Karunaratne's unbeaten 72 off just 34 balls
Dambulla Sixers fell well short in the chase after early wickets triggered a collapse
Win takes Galle Gallants clear at the top of the LPL points table with eight points
This is a separate, later match to the Jaffna-Kandy game already in the feed today

depth.background: The Lanka Premier League (LPL) is Sri Lanka's franchise T20 tournament, now in its group stage with teams playing for a spot in the playoffs. Galle Gallants and Dambulla Sixers had already met once this LPL season, when Dambulla won comfortably — making this a rematch with the earlier result at stake.

stories.title: Manchester Super Giants thrash Birmingham Phoenix by 87 runs in The Hundred
stories.what_happened: Manchester Super Giants posted 187 for 5 from their 100 balls and then bowled out Birmingham Phoenix for just 100, winning by 87 runs in the competition's 7th match of the men's season.
key_points: Manchester Super Giants posted 187/5 in their 100 balls
Birmingham Phoenix collapsed to just 100 all out in reply
87-run margin is one of the more lopsided results of this year's Hundred
Result strengthens Super Giants' position in the men's competition table

depth.background: The Hundred is England's short-form, 100-balls-per-side cricket competition, running men's and women's tournaments side by side each summer as a faster, more broadcast-friendly alternative to T20. Manchester Super Giants and Birmingham Phoenix are two of the eight men's franchises competing this season.

stories.title: 'How the hell did I end up here?' — Verstappen stunned by his own damaged-car podium as Red Bull says it never gave him a car to attack with
stories.what_happened: After qualifying poorly and picking up car damage during the Hungarian Grand Prix, Max Verstappen finished 2nd — a result he said left him baffled, telling reporters 'I don't understand how we are second' and 'How the hell did I end up here?' Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies backed up Verstappen's surprise, saying the team 'never managed to give Max... a car they could attack with' this weekend and that the car's behaviour was unlike stronger recent races such as Spa or Austria.
key_points: Verstappen said he was 'still shocked' by finishing 2nd after a poor qualifying and race damage
He called it 'a bit of an over-performance compared to what we expected'
Team boss Laurent Mekies said Red Bull 'never managed to give Max... a car he could attack with'
Mekies said this weekend's car behaviour was completely different from stronger races like Spa or Austria

depth.background: Red Bull has struggled with inconsistent car performance across the 2026 season, sometimes competitive and sometimes off the pace from one race to the next, making it hard for the team and Verstappen to predict results race to race. Laurent Mekies, who now leads Red Bull's F1 team, has been managing the team through this stretch of unpredictable form.

stories.title: Toto Wolff launches a 'Teletubbies' rant at rival teams over a blue-flag failure that nearly cost Antonelli the Hungarian GP podium
stories.what_happened: A system fault during the Hungarian Grand Prix meant the automatic blue-flag light panels stopped working, so backmarkers could only be warned manually — and several didn't react in time, holding up Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli as he tried to catch Max Verstappen for 2nd place in the closing laps while defending from Lewis Hamilton behind him. Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff blasted rival teams afterwards, saying it was 'disgraceful' that 'some of the Teletubbies engineers... sitting on the pit walls' failed to tell their drivers what was happening, adding that lapped cars 'defending is just not acceptable.'
key_points: A light-panel system fault meant blue flags could only be shown manually to backmarkers
Antonelli was held up by slow lapped cars while chasing Verstappen for 2nd late in the race
Wolff called rival teams' pit-wall engineers 'Teletubbies' for not warning drivers in time
Antonelli still held on for 3rd, extending his championship lead to 50 points

depth.background: Blue flags are shown to backmarkers (cars a lap or more behind) to tell them to let faster, competing cars past without a fight. Normally this is triggered automatically by trackside light panels, which teams and drivers rely on to know when to yield.

stories.title: West Indies build a commanding 303/7 at lunch on Day 2 of the Pakistan Test
stories.what_happened: Resuming Day 2 from an overnight 194 for 3, West Indies added 109 runs in the first session to reach 303 for 7 by lunch, in 96 overs, despite losing four more wickets along the way. Shai Hope remained unbeaten on 89, anchoring the innings, while lower-order batter Shamar Joseph provided late fireworks with 23 not out off just 12 balls, hitting four boundaries and a six. Pakistan's Aamer Jamal was the most successful bowler in the session, taking a wicket for 81 runs.
key_points: West Indies resumed Day 2 at 194/3 and reached 303/7 by the lunch break
Shai Hope anchored the innings with an unbeaten 89
Shamar Joseph blazed 23 off just 12 balls with four fours and a six
It's a big recovery from a rain-hit 23/1 at the same stage on Day 1

depth.background: West Indies and Pakistan are playing the first Test of their series at the Brian Lara Stadium in Tarouba, Trinidad — a brand-new Test venue. Day 1 was badly disrupted by rain and tight bowling from Pakistan's Mohammad Abbas, which restricted West Indies to just 23 for 1 at the close.

thread.previously: We reported that rain and disciplined bowling from Mohammad Abbas had restricted West Indies to just 23 for 1 at the close of a truncated Day 1.
thread.changed: West Indies have recovered strongly on Day 2, reaching 303 for 7 by lunch on the back of Shai Hope's unbeaten 89 and a late blitz from Shamar Joseph.

prev_ref.title: Rain and Mohammad Abbas restrict West Indies to 23/1 on Day 1 of the Pakistan Test at a brand-new venue

stories.title: Max Verstappen wins the Hungarian Grand Prix after starting only 10th on the grid
stories.what_happened: Verstappen carved through the field at the Hungaroring to win the Hungarian Grand Prix from 10th on the grid, his 8th win of the 2026 season and the 28th of his career. Lewis Hamilton brought his Ferrari home 2nd, with Mercedes' George Russell 3rd. Over team radio after the chequered flag, a stunned Verstappen said: "Amazing result. Who would have thought when we woke up that we were going to win the race."
key_points: Verstappen won from 10th on the grid — his 8th win of the season
Lando Norris had taken pole, with Hamilton and Antonelli both hit by grid penalties
Hamilton finished 2nd for Ferrari, Russell 3rd for Mercedes
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc lost a likely strong result to a strategy call

depth.background: Saturday's qualifying at the Hungaroring in Budapest was chaotic: Lando Norris took pole for McLaren by just 0.012 seconds over Lewis Hamilton, before stewards handed grid penalties to both Hamilton and championship leader Kimi Antonelli for separate incidents, reshuffling Sunday's starting order. Red Bull's Max Verstappen — this season's most successful driver by wins — had a poor qualifying and lined up well back in 10th, a rare off-day for the team.

stories.title: Verstappen's Red Bull exit clause is now live after a below-top-2 Hungarian GP
stories.what_happened: Verstappen finished the Hungarian Grand Prix — the summer-break-defining race — well outside the championship's top two, confirming what had looked likely for weeks: he can now exercise his contractual release clause any time between August and October to leave Red Bull for 2027, rather than seeing out a long-term deal.
key_points: Verstappen sits P7, ~113 points off championship leader Antonelli
Hungarian GP was the exact reference race written into his contract
He can now activate the release clause between August and October
Aston Martin, boosted by Adrian Newey and a new Honda deal, is seen as the leading suitor

depth.background: Red Bull reportedly wrote a release clause into Verstappen's contract because of his long-running unease with F1's overhauled 2026 technical regulations, which he has compared unfavorably to 'Mario Kart' racing. The clause was designed as a pressure valve given that discomfort, with Aston Martin — now allied with car designer Adrian Newey and a new exclusive Honda engine deal — widely seen as his most likely destination if he leaves.

thread.previously: Max Verstappen's Red Bull contract includes a release clause letting him leave for 2027 if he isn't ranked in the championship's top two by the time F1 reaches its summer break, with the Hungarian Grand Prix serving as the key reference race.
thread.changed: The Hungarian GP — the actual reference race — has now been run. Verstappen sits seventh in the standings, roughly 113 points behind runaway leader Kimi Antonelli, comfortably outside the top two. That confirms the clause is now active, and he can formally choose to trigger it any time between August and October.

prev_ref.title: Verstappen can now trigger an exit clause to leave Red Bull for 2027 — if he's not top-2 by August

stories.title: India complete a 3-0 T20I sweep of Zimbabwe as Sooryavanshi wins Player of the Series
stories.what_happened: India posted 192 for 5 batting first, with Sooryavanshi top-scoring with 81 off 49 balls, before bowling Zimbabwe out for 157 for 7 to win by 35 runs and complete a 3-0 series sweep. Sooryavanshi, who scored 151 runs across the series, was named Player of the Series as well as Player of the Match for the decider.
key_points: India beat Zimbabwe by 35 runs to win the 3rd T20I and the series 3-0
Teenager Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hit 81 off 49 balls, his best T20I score
Sooryavanshi finished with 151 series runs and won Player of the Series
It's Shreyas Iyer's first series win since taking over as India's T20I captain

depth.background: India toured Zimbabwe for a three-match T20I series under new captain Shreyas Iyer, with the series offering a testing ground for fringe players, including 18-year-old opener Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, before India's next major assignments. India had already won the first two matches of the series heading into this decider.

stories.title: Jaffna Kings crush Kandy Royals by 93 runs in the Lanka Premier League
stories.what_happened: Jaffna Kings beat Kandy Royals by 93 runs in Match 13 of the 2026 Lanka Premier League at the Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium. Jaffna posted 199/4 from their 20 overs before bowling Kandy out for 106 in 18.2 overs. Kamil Mishara was named Player of the Match.
key_points: Jaffna Kings posted 199/4 in their 20 overs at Rangiri Dambulla
Kandy Royals were bowled out for just 106 in 18.2 overs
Kamil Mishara named Player of the Match
Result keeps Jaffna Kings among the LPL 2026 pace-setters

depth.background: The Lanka Premier League (LPL) is Sri Lanka's franchise Twenty20 tournament, running alongside similar leagues elsewhere (India's IPL, the Caribbean's CPL) that give international and local players a short, high-intensity domestic season outside their national team commitments.

stories.title: F1 heads into its summer break with 17 drivers out of contract and the Norris-Piastri title fight wide open
stories.what_happened: F1 heads into its summer break (starting July 27, with no race until the Dutch Grand Prix on August 23) with 17 of the grid's driver contracts expiring at the end of 2026 — all but five drivers are unsigned for 2027. Max Verstappen's Red Bull contract contains an exit clause that has now become active after the team failed to keep him inside the top two in the championship, adding fresh uncertainty to the sport's biggest storyline.
key_points: F1's summer break officially begins July 27, running until the Dutch GP on August 23
Only five drivers — Verstappen, Norris, Piastri, Leclerc and Gasly — have deals beyond this season
Max Verstappen's Red Bull exit clause is now active after a below-top-2 result run
The next month of driver-market speculation could reshape multiple teams' 2027 lineups

depth.background: Formula 1 contracts for the following season are typically negotiated and announced through the middle of the current year, and the summer break — a mandated shutdown of race-team factories — has traditionally been when driver moves get finalized, because there are no races to distract from the negotiations.

stories.title: Mirabai Chanu scripts history with a third straight Commonwealth Games weightlifting gold
stories.what_happened: Chanu won India's first gold medal of the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games in the women's 48kg weightlifting final, lifting a combined 190kg — a new Games record — to secure the title. She set a Commonwealth record of 85kg in the snatch and a Games record of 105kg in the clean and jerk. It is her third consecutive individual Commonwealth Games gold in the same weight category.
key_points: Chanu wins the women's 48kg gold with a Games-record 190kg total lift
She set a Commonwealth record 85kg snatch and a Games-record 105kg clean and jerk
It's her third consecutive individual Commonwealth Games gold medal
Only India's Vinesh Phogat has managed three straight individual CWG golds before her

depth.background: Saikhom Mirabai Chanu, an Olympic medallist weightlifter from Manipur, carried India's flag at the Commonwealth Games 2026 opening ceremony in Glasgow. She had already won consecutive Commonwealth Games golds in the women's 48kg category at the two previous editions, making this event a bid for a rare 'three-peat' — winning the same individual event at three straight Games, something very few athletes from any country manage because of the toll repeated peak performances take across years.

stories.title: Piastri's Hungarian GP heartbreak: gearbox failure ends his race while leading, as Norris wins and Antonelli extends his F1 title lead
stories.what_happened: Oscar Piastri lost the race lead early after tangling with backmarker Carlos Sainz's Williams, then was forced to retire on lap 56 with a gearbox failure while running second — a bitter result after leading much of the race. Teammate Lando Norris held on to win from pole, 15 seconds clear of Max Verstappen, with Antonelli completing the podium in third. Lewis Hamilton crossed fourth but was demoted to fifth after a 5-second penalty for speeding in the pit lane.
key_points: Oscar Piastri retired on lap 56 with a gearbox failure while running second
An earlier clash with Carlos Sainz's Williams had already cost him the lead
Teammate Lando Norris converted pole into his first win of the season
Kimi Antonelli's podium stretches his championship lead to 50 points over Hamilton

depth.background: McLaren has been the class of the field for much of the 2026 Formula 1 season, but the Hungarian Grand Prix — the last race before F1's summer break — turned into a story of what could have been for one of its two drivers. Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes' rising star, arrived at Hungaroring already holding the championship lead, chasing a feat no driver has managed since 1950: winning the title on home soil.

stories.title: India chase a clean sweep as the series-deciding 3rd T20I in Harare gets underway
stories.what_happened: The third and final T20I between Zimbabwe and India begins today in Harare. With the series already won 2-0, India are playing for a clean sweep (3-0) rather than the series itself, while Zimbabwe look to avoid a whitewash and salvage some pride on home soil.
key_points: India already lead the 3-match T20I series 2-0
3rd and final T20I starts today in Harare
A win would complete a clean sweep of the series
India's 2nd T20I win came by 90 runs, with Ishan Kishan named Player of the Match

depth.background: India toured Zimbabwe with a fringe/second-string squad, giving newer players a chance to press their case for a fuller national recall. India won the first T20I by 7 wickets and the second by 90 runs, already sealing the series with a match to spare.

stories.title: India's Commonwealth Games Day 3: lawn bowls pair wins, boxer advances, but swimmers miss the final
stories.what_happened: On Day 3 (July 26), India's women's lawn bowls pair of Rupa Rani Tirkey and Pinky Singh won their sectional match against Namibia. In boxing, Sachin Siwach moved a step closer to a medal in the men's 60kg category. But in the pool, swimmers Dhakshan Shashikumar and Aryan Nehra failed to qualify for the men's 400m freestyle final, while the men's 4x200m freestyle relay team was still to swim its heats later in the day.
key_points: Rupa Rani Tirkey and Pinky Singh win women's pairs lawn bowls vs Namibia
Boxer Sachin Siwach moves a step closer to a medal in men's 60kg
Dhakshan Shashikumar and Aryan Nehra fail to make the men's 400m freestyle final
Men's 4x200m freestyle relay heats still to come later in the day

depth.background: India arrived at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games with two bronze medals already banked — including one from Lovlina Borgohain's boxing bye into the semifinals — and is chasing a broader medal push across boxing, gymnastics, swimming and lawn bowls through the Games' first week.

stories.title: PM Modi marks 26th Kargil Vijay Diwas in his 136th Mann Ki Baat address
stories.what_happened: In the 136th episode of Mann Ki Baat, PM Modi paid tribute to the soldiers who fought in the 1999 Kargil War, calling their valour a lasting source of national pride, on the 26th anniversary of India's victory. He also used the address to spotlight the 'Catch The Rain' rainwater-harvesting campaign running since early July, the 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' tree-plantation drive, a plastic-recycling 'Waste to Wealth' initiative from Sitamarhi in Bihar, and India's growing defence exports — citing a recent BrahMos and Astra missile agreement with Indonesia. Separately, a large tribute march with over a thousand participants — veterans, martyrs' families, and youth — was held in Drass, Ladakh, near the original Kargil battle sites.
key_points: July 26 marks 26 years since India's 1999 Kargil War victory
Modi paid tribute to soldiers in his monthly Mann Ki Baat radio address
He also highlighted rainwater harvesting, tree plantation, and a Bihar recycling project
A tribute march (Padyatra) was held in Drass, Ladakh, near the old battle sites

depth.background: Mann Ki Baat ('from the heart') is PM Modi's monthly radio address, running since 2014, where he talks directly to citizens about social initiatives and national moments — this was its 136th episode. Kargil Vijay Diwas marks India's victory in the 1999 Kargil War, fought in the high-altitude Kargil district of Ladakh after Pakistani forces and militants crossed the Line of Control; it's observed every July 26.

stories.title: Spain declares its first-ever national wildfire emergency as evacuations pass 300,000
stories.what_happened: Spain's government declared its first-ever national emergency over a wildfire after two large blazes near the capital merged into one and a third fire threatened to join them, burning roughly 15,000 hectares across the Madrid and Ávila regions. Regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso called it the worst fire in the region's history. Combined evacuations across France and Spain have now climbed past 300,000 people, up from about 250,000 a day earlier, with roughly 60,000 evacuated from villages west of Madrid alone. A separate, smaller blaze near Valencia killed one elderly man. High winds are fanning the flames in both countries.
key_points: Spain invokes a national emergency for a wildfire for the first time ever
Three blazes near Madrid have merged into one 'worst fire in the region's history'
Combined France-Spain evacuations now top 300,000, up from ~250,000 yesterday
Italy, Greece, Netherlands and Portugal are flying in extra water-bomber aircraft

depth.background: Southwestern Europe has been locked in a weeks-long, climate-change-intensified heatwave that has left forests around Madrid and southwestern France tinder-dry. Wildfires broke out over the weekend and, as of yesterday, had already forced roughly 250,000 people from their homes across France and Spain. A 'national emergency' in Spain is a rarely-used legal step: it lets the central government in Madrid take over powers that normally sit with Spain's semi-autonomous regions, and it has only been invoked once before (during a countrywide blackout in 2025).

thread.previously: We reported that wildfires fueled by a weeks-long heatwave had forced over 250,000 evacuations across southwestern France and central Spain.
thread.changed: The crisis has escalated sharply: Spain has now declared its first-ever national wildfire emergency after blazes merged near Madrid, and combined evacuations have passed 300,000.

prev_ref.title: Wildfires force over 250,000 evacuations across southwestern France and central Spain

stories.title: New UK PM Andy Burnham vows to stand up to Trump, rules out early election
stories.what_happened: In comments reported by the BBC, Burnham said he would defend British national interests and 'call out' US President Trump if required, even while describing an earlier exchange with him as 'really warm.' He also told the BBC he has no plans to call an early general election before the one already due in 2029, saying voters don't want one and that his focus is on stabilizing the country.
key_points: Burnham says he'll 'call out' Trump if needed on UK interests
Calls an earlier Trump exchange 'really warm' but won't be pushed around
Rules out an early general election before 2029
Comes a week after becoming the UK's 7th PM in a decade

depth.background: Britain has churned through prime ministers at a historic rate. Keir Starmer resigned in June 2026 after support for him collapsed inside the Labour Party following a disastrous set of local election results. Andy Burnham, the high-profile mayor of Greater Manchester and a leading 'soft left' Labour voice, was chosen as his successor and was sworn in on July 20, 2026, becoming the UK's 7th prime minister in just 10 years — the fastest leadership turnover Britain has seen in nearly two centuries.

stories.title: A new depression is brewing in the Bay of Bengal — Andhra Pradesh put on alert as it may intensify within 24 hours
stories.what_happened: The India Meteorological Department and Andhra Pradesh's State Disaster Management Authority say a depression that formed over the northwest Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a 'deep depression' within the next 24 hours. It's forecast to track toward the coast between Paradip (Odisha) and Sagar Island (West Bengal) by Monday, but north coastal Andhra Pradesh is already being warned of strong winds (55-65 kmph) and rough seas as its outer bands arrive. The IMD's Amaravati office has issued a three-day heavy-rain warning for the state.
key_points: A depression over the northwest Bay of Bengal could strengthen into a deep depression within 24 hours
It's expected to track toward the coast near Paradip (Odisha) and Sagar Island (West Bengal) around Monday
North coastal Andhra Pradesh is bracing for winds up to 65 kmph and rough seas
Fishermen have been told to stay off the sea until further notice

depth.background: This is a separate weather system from the extreme-rain system already battering Maharashtra and central India, and from the flooding in Assam — India's monsoon season regularly spins up multiple low-pressure systems over the Bay of Bengal at once, each capable of dumping heavy rain hundreds of kilometres from where it forms. Coastal Andhra Pradesh is especially exposed because it faces the Bay of Bengal directly and has a long, low-lying coastline.

stories.title: Kerala cyber police arrest two Delhi men over a fake 'ministerial berth for ₹3 crore' scam targeting an MLA and two MPs
stories.what_happened: Kozhikode cyber police arrested two Delhi residents in connection with the scam, bringing them to Kerala after tracing the fraud network beyond the SIM card's registered owner. Police believe the group used caller-spoofing technology and 'mule' bank accounts — accounts opened in someone else's name to receive and quickly move stolen or fraudulent money — to hide their real identities while trying to extort politicians.
key_points: Callers impersonated the private secretary of Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra
Demanded ₹3 crore from Kerala MLA Vidya Balakrishnan for a ministerial post
Same number contacted MPs Shafi Parambil and Dean Kuriakose
Two Delhi residents arrested; police suspect caller-ID spoofing and mule bank accounts

depth.background: This scam surfaced in mid-July when Elathur MLA K Vidya Balakrishnan got a WhatsApp call from someone claiming to work for Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra's office, offering to arrange her a ministerial post in exchange for ₹3 crore (about $360,000). She grew suspicious and verified with Vadra's actual office, then filed a police complaint. The same caller reportedly used the same number to approach two sitting MPs with similar offers. Investigators initially traced the SIM card to a Delhi daily-wage worker who denied involvement, saying he'd lost his phone months earlier — suggesting the real fraudsters were using a stolen or bought identity to mask themselves.

stories.title: India's Test squad for Sri Lanka to be named by Tuesday — Jadeja set to return, Bumrah still under watch
stories.what_happened: BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia confirmed India's squad for its upcoming two-Test tour of Sri Lanka will be announced by Tuesday, July 28. Ravindra Jadeja is set to return to the Test side, while pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah's availability remains under close watch after he skipped a decisive ODI against England with left-knee swelling; a source close to the team says the three-week gap before the series gives him time to recover. Washington Sundar and Sai Sudharsan are also on the fitness watch-list. The tour opens with the first Test in Galle on August 15, followed by Colombo.
key_points: BCCI secretary confirms the squad will be announced by Tuesday, July 28
Ravindra Jadeja set to return as India's first-choice Test spinner
Jasprit Bumrah's left-knee fitness remains the biggest selection question
Washington Sundar and Sai Sudharsan also carry fitness question marks
First Test starts in Galle on August 15, second in Colombo

depth.background: India's Test team has been managing a string of fitness concerns among its fast bowlers and key all-rounders through a packed international calendar. Ravindra Jadeja, a senior all-rounder and India's most trusted Test spinner, was rested for a recent one-off Test and left out of the ODI series in England to manage his workload after a long IPL season.

stories.title: IMD issues red alerts for Himachal, Uttarakhand and J&K as a fresh monsoon surge hits North India
stories.what_happened: The IMD's Sunday morning bulletin put Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh under red alerts for extremely heavy rainfall over the next 24 hours, with Delhi-NCR on orange alert for heavy rain, thunderstorms and gusty winds up to 40 kmph. The bulletin describes the southwest monsoon as newly reinvigorated and active across North India.
key_points: Red alerts for extremely heavy rain in Himachal, Uttarakhand, J&K and Ladakh
Delhi-NCR under an orange alert with thunderstorms and 30-40 kmph winds
Hilly regions face a real risk of landslides and flash floods
Comes as monsoon rains have already killed dozens and displaced hundreds of thousands elsewhere in India this month

depth.background: India's southwest monsoon — the seasonal wind pattern that brings most of the country's annual rainfall between June and September — has been unusually intense this year, already causing deadly floods and landslides in Assam, Jammu & Kashmir, and other states earlier in July. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) grades rainfall risk with a color code: yellow (watch), orange (be prepared), red (take action, most severe).

stories.title: IMD issues red alert for extreme rain across Maharashtra and Central India as monsoon intensifies
stories.what_happened: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a red alert — its highest warning level — for Pune's Ghatmatha region and warned of extremely heavy rain across central Maharashtra and Odisha, with orange alerts for Raigad and Ratnagiri districts. Separately, IMD forecast widespread rain, thunderstorms and gusty winds of 40–60 km/h across North India, including Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu & Kashmir.
key_points: Red alert (highest level) for Pune's Ghatmatha region
Orange alerts for Raigad and Ratnagiri districts
Central Maharashtra and Odisha warned of extremely heavy rain
Delhi, UP, Bihar, Himachal and Uttarakhand also under thunderstorm/wind alerts

depth.background: India's southwest monsoon delivers most of the country's annual rainfall between June and September and typically peaks in intensity through July. This year an unusually active monsoon trough has already caused deadly, prolonged flooding in Assam, where the death toll stands at 66, and is now swinging its focus toward central and western India.

stories.title: Typhoon Noul slams into southern China, forcing 340,000 evacuations and grounding Hong Kong flights
stories.what_happened: Typhoon Noul made landfall at around 3:50am local time on Sunday near Huidong county in Huizhou, Guangdong province, with maximum sustained winds of about 162 km/h (101 mph) — the strongest typhoon to hit China so far this year. It forced the relocation of more than 340,000 people in Guangdong, while Hong Kong's airport cancelled roughly 350 flights and the city halted train services for the day. At least nine people were injured in Hong Kong as gale-force winds swept the territory.
key_points: Strongest typhoon to hit China so far this year
340,000+ people evacuated in Guangdong province
About 350 Hong Kong flights cancelled, trains halted for the day
Landfall winds of roughly 162 km/h near Huizhou

depth.background: Typhoon season in the western Pacific typically peaks from July through October, and southern China's Guangdong province — along with neighbouring Hong Kong — sits directly in the usual storm track. Typhoons are the same kind of storm as Atlantic hurricanes; only the name changes by ocean basin.

stories.title: LPG cylinder blast kills four workers at an Assam iron-casting unit; CM announces compensation
stories.what_happened: A suspected LPG cylinder explosion tore through a shared compound housing Kade Global Infrastructure LLP and IRID Casting Works LLP in Pangram, under Udharbond police station in Assam's Cachar district, killing four workers on Sunday. Preliminary investigation points to a cylinder engaged in casting work as the cause. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma announced ₹5 lakh (500,000 rupees) in compensation for each victim's family and warned that industrial negligence would not be tolerated. Four people, including the factory manager, have been detained, and the Assistant Labour Commissioner will separately investigate workplace safety conditions.
key_points: Blast hit a shared factory compound in Cachar district's Udharbond area
An LPG cylinder used in the casting process is the suspected cause
CM Himanta Biswa Sarma announces ₹5 lakh compensation per victim's family
Factory manager among four people detained as safety-lapse probe begins

depth.background: Small and mid-sized manufacturing units in India, especially in the metal-casting and foundry trade, often rely on LPG (liquefied petroleum gas) cylinders for the intense heat their processes need. Industrial safety enforcement in such units varies widely by state, and cylinder-related accidents remain a recurring cause of workplace deaths in India.

stories.title: Israeli settlers torch two West Bank mosques and daub 'revenge' graffiti after a soldier's killing; Israel raids Nablus overnight
stories.what_happened: In the early hours of Sunday, Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian villages in the West Bank, setting fire to two mosques and spray-painting 'Revenge Benayahu' on walls — a reference to Benayahu Mellet, a 32-year-old Israeli reserve soldier killed in a shooting near the Palestinian village of Tal earlier in the week. Separately, Israeli soldiers stormed the city of Nablus overnight, detaining about 40 Palestinians, including a woman and former prisoners.
key_points: Settlers set fire to two mosques in Palestinian villages before dawn Sunday
Graffiti referenced Benayahu Mellet, an Israeli reservist killed in a shooting near Tal village
Separately, Israeli troops raided Nablus overnight and detained about 40 Palestinians
Comes as settler attacks now account for over half of Palestinian injuries in the West Bank this year

depth.background: The occupied West Bank is home to roughly 500,000 Israeli settlers living alongside about 3 million Palestinians, under Israeli military administration. Settler violence against Palestinian communities — arson, property damage, physical attacks — has been rising for years and often goes unpunished; rights groups and the UN say it has surged further since the Gaza war began in October 2023. Israeli military raids on Palestinian towns, aimed at suspected militants, are a near-daily occurrence and often result in mass detentions.

stories.title: Scientists find a biological "tipping point" that decides whether Alzheimer's plaques actually turn into dementia
stories.what_happened: Researchers analyzed brain tissue from older adults with and without cognitive decline, plus a rare group: cognitively sharp centenarians who had amyloid plaques in their brains but never developed dementia. Using detailed cell-mapping techniques, they found microglia — the brain's resident clean-up/immune cells — pass through two distinct states: first, an inflammatory response triggered by amyloid plaques; later, in people who go on to develop dementia, a switch into a second, "antigen-presenting" state that shows up alongside tau tangle buildup and real memory loss. The healthy centenarians' microglia reached the first state but never made the second switch.
key_points: Brain immune cells (microglia) pass through two distinct stages on the way to Alzheimer's-linked memory loss
Study compared brains of people with dementia, without it, and rare cognitively-sharp centenarians who had plaques but no symptoms
The healthy centenarians' immune cells stopped at stage one and never flipped into stage two
Stage two is the one that lines up with tau tangles and actual cognitive decline — giving researchers a concrete target

depth.background: Alzheimer's disease involves two hallmark buildups in the brain over decades: sticky "amyloid" protein plaques outside brain cells, and tangled "tau" protein fibers inside neurons. Doctors have long known some people carry heavy amyloid buildup and never develop dementia, but why some brains cross into symptomatic decline and others don't has been unclear. A team from Belgium's VIB and KU Leuven, the UK Dementia Research Institute, and biotech Muna Therapeutics set out to find the switch, publishing their findings in the journal Nature Medicine.

stories.title: Massive fire guts four shops in Maharashtra's Washim in the early hours
stories.what_happened: A massive fire broke out at four shops in Washim in the early hours of Sunday, July 26. The blaze spread rapidly, engulfing the shops within minutes and sending thick smoke into the surrounding area. Fire tenders were dispatched immediately and firefighting operations were underway as of the latest reports, with the cause of the fire not yet determined.
key_points: Fire broke out at four shops in Washim, Maharashtra, early Sunday morning
Flames spread quickly, sending thick smoke into the air
Fire crews were dispatched and are working to douse the blaze
Cause of the fire has not yet been established

depth.background: Washim is a district town in eastern Maharashtra. Shop and market fires are a recurring hazard across small-town India during the humid monsoon months, often linked to short-circuits or unattended electrical wiring in densely packed commercial strips, though the exact cause here is still unconfirmed.

stories.title: US exempts 2,231 Taiwanese products from its new round of tariffs
stories.what_happened: US trade authorities confirmed that 2,231 categories of Taiwanese goods will be exempted from the newest round of tariffs, which hit around 60 countries this week. The exemptions implement the trade agreement Taiwan and the US signed earlier this year and follow an existing Section 232 tariff relief package finalized in May.
key_points: Washington carves out 2,231 Taiwanese product lines from fresh tariffs
Comes after the US imposed new duties on roughly 60 trading partners
Builds on a January 2026 deal tying tariff relief to Taiwanese investment in the US
Semiconductors are the product category investors care about most

depth.background: Since early 2026, the US has been rolling out a new wave of tariffs — import taxes — on dozens of countries as part of a broader trade-policy reset. Taiwan negotiated a side deal in January in which it agreed to help fund up to $250 billion in US semiconductor, energy, and AI manufacturing capacity in exchange for lower tariff rates, since Taiwan makes the advanced chips that power almost every modern device.

stories.title: India gets hit with a 10% US tariff — lower than China's — as trade talks continue
stories.what_happened: The Trump administration announced new tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on imports from 60 trading partners, including India, taking effect this week. India's rate came in at 10% — lower than the 12.5% level floated in June, and lower than China's rate — and excludes sensitive categories like generic pharmaceuticals, smartphones, steel, aluminium and auto parts. India's government said on Saturday it would keep engaging with Washington to finalize a full bilateral trade agreement, including on issues like textiles.
key_points: The Trump administration imposed fresh tariffs of 10%–12.5% on goods from 60 trading partners, including India, over claims those countries failed to curb imports made with forced labour
India's 10% rate is lower than China's 12.5%, and excludes key exports like generic medicines, smartphones, steel, aluminium and auto parts
India says it will keep negotiating a full bilateral trade agreement with the US despite the new tariff

depth.background: The US and India have been negotiating a broader trade deal through much of 2026, aiming to expand market access and cut trade barriers between the two countries. Even as those talks continue, the Trump administration has been rolling out new tariffs — taxes on imported goods — across dozens of countries, officially citing concerns about forced-labour-linked supply chains, but also using them as broader trade leverage.

stories.title: Gaza's Health Ministry says nine more Palestinians killed in 24 hours, as ceasefire violations keep piling up nine months in
stories.what_happened: Gaza's Health Ministry said Israeli fire killed at least seven Palestinians and contributed to two further deaths from previously sustained wounds over the past 24 hours, with 36 more people injured; Turkish wire service Anadolu Agency reported the cumulative Gaza death toll has now passed 73,300. Rescue crews said some of the wounded remained hard to reach because of access restrictions. Israel's military has generally said its post-ceasefire Gaza operations target militants, weapons caches and infrastructure it considers a threat, rather than commenting on each individual strike.
key_points: Gaza's Health Ministry says hospitals received nine bodies in the past 24 hours — seven newly killed, two who died of earlier wounds
36 more people were reported injured in the same window
The Israel-Hamas ceasefire that began October 10, 2025 formally still holds, but strikes have continued through it
Israel says operations target militants and weapons sites; Gaza's authorities call the pattern a running violation of the truce

depth.background: A ceasefire took effect in Gaza on October 10, 2025, ending the deadliest phase of a two-year war that had by then killed more than 70,000 Palestinians according to Gaza's Health Ministry — the territory's Hamas-run health authority, whose casualty figures are nonetheless the primary source used by the UN and most international news organizations for lack of independent access to Gaza. The deal was meant to end major combat and open the door to reconstruction and further negotiations, but both sides have accused each other of violations essentially every week since.

stories.title: Chickenpox tears through Gaza's displacement camps — 9,300 cases in two weeks
stories.what_happened: Health workers report roughly 9,300 chickenpox cases across more than 130 health facilities in Gaza in just the past two weeks, according to reporting confirmed by multiple outlets including Euronews and Arab News. Chickenpox is a highly contagious virus that causes an itchy, blistering rash and fever — usually mild in healthy, vaccinated children, but it spreads fast in crowded, unhygienic conditions and can be more dangerous for malnourished or unvaccinated kids.
key_points: About 9,300 chickenpox cases logged in just two weeks across 130+ clinics
Doctors say the real number is almost certainly higher
Overcrowded tents with no clean water make isolating the sick impossible
Worst hit area is Khan Yunis in southern Gaza

depth.background: Gaza's population has been squeezed into crowded tent camps for the better part of two years of war, with hospitals and clinics damaged and medicine and staff in short supply. Many children born during the war missed routine vaccinations, leaving a generation with weaker defenses against diseases that are normally minor and easily prevented.

stories.title: US Cyclospora outbreak tied to Taco Bell lettuce grows to nearly 2,000 cases across 9 states
stories.what_happened: The CDC's latest update, published today, puts the outbreak at 1,947 confirmed cases across Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania and West Virginia, with at least 98 people hospitalized and no deaths reported. Investigators traced the source to iceberg lettuce grown by Taylor Farms de Mexico, which moved through Taco Bell's supply chain. The company issued a nationwide recall of its central-Mexico iceberg lettuce on July 17. Illness onset dates range from June 22 to July 20, meaning the outbreak has been quietly growing for over a month.
key_points: 1,947 confirmed cases across 9 US states, 98 hospitalized
Traced to Taylor Farms de Mexico iceberg lettuce used by Taco Bell
Supplier recalled all central-Mexico iceberg lettuce on July 17
Illnesses started as early as June 22, still climbing

depth.background: Cyclospora cayetanensis is a microscopic parasite that spreads through food or water contaminated with human waste — usually irrigation water tainted by leaking sewage, or field workers without proper sanitation. It's not spread person-to-person. The US has had smaller outbreaks before, usually linked to imported produce like cilantro or basil, but this one has grown unusually large and is centered on a major fast-food chain's supply chain.

stories.title: Malaysia confirms Sepang's F1 return — as a stand-in 'Bahrain Grand Prix' on October 3-4
stories.what_happened: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim confirmed that Sepang International Circuit will host a Formula 1 race weekend on October 3-4, 2026 — but it will run as the 'Bahrain Grand Prix' rather than a Malaysian GP, effectively relocating Bahrain's cancelled race rather than creating a new standalone Malaysian event. It ends a wait that began when Anwar said an announcement was coming 'this Sunday.'
key_points: Sepang International Circuit confirmed to host a new October 3-4 race weekend
The race will run as the 'Bahrain Grand Prix' — Bahrain's own race was cancelled by Middle East conflict
It's Sepang's first F1 race since 2017, when the Malaysian GP was discontinued
Announcement made by Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim, as promised, on Sunday

depth.background: Sepang hosted the Malaysian Grand Prix from 1999 to 2017, when F1 dropped it from the calendar over falling attendance and rising hosting costs. This year, F1's 2026 calendar lost the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix after they were cancelled due to the Iran-linked conflict in the Middle East, leaving F1 needing to fill race weekends and honor sponsor and broadcast commitments tied to those races.

thread.previously: Malaysia's PM said a formal Sepang F1 return announcement was coming that Sunday.
thread.changed: The announcement has been made: Sepang will host a race October 3-4, run as the Bahrain Grand Prix.

prev_ref.title: Malaysia's PM says a formal Sepang F1 return announcement is coming this Sunday

stories.title: Bangladesh names its 15-man Test squad for a historic first tour of Australia in 23 years, with uncapped Musfik Hasan in for the injured Nahid Rana
stories.what_happened: The BCB announced its 15-man squad today, led by Najmul Hossain Shanto. Uncapped pacer Musfik Hasan — who has had national call-ups before, in 2023 and 2024, without playing a Test — was picked to help cover the gap left by Rana. Litton Das will sit out the first Test but is expected to be fit for the second. The team departs for Australia on August 1, plays a three-day warm-up match in Darwin from August 6-8, then the first Test starts August 13 in Darwin, with the second in Mackay from August 22.
key_points: The BCB picked a 15-man squad, led by Najmul Hossain Shanto, for the two-Test series in Australia
Uncapped fast bowler Musfik Hasan gets the nod after Nahid Rana's side-strain injury ruled him out
Wicketkeeper-batter Litton Das will miss the first Test but is expected back for the second
It's Bangladesh's first Test series in Australia in 23 years — no player in this squad has ever played a Test on Australian soil

depth.background: Bangladesh has historically struggled touring Australia, where extra pace and bounce expose weaknesses that don't show up as much at home. That challenge got harder yesterday when Nahid Rana — Bangladesh's fastest bowler and best suited to Australian conditions — was ruled out for six to eight weeks with a Grade 2 side strain, forcing selectors to scramble for a replacement just before the squad's scheduled departure.

thread.previously: Bangladesh's premier fast bowler Nahid Rana was ruled out of the two-Test series in Australia after a Grade 2 left side strain, with the Bangladesh Cricket Board confirming a six-to-eight-week recovery timeline just before the squad's scheduled departure.
thread.changed: The BCB has now named the full 15-man squad, calling up uncapped pacer Musfik Hasan to help cover the gap left by Rana, and confirming Litton Das will also miss the series opener before returning for the second Test.

prev_ref.title: Bangladesh loses fast bowler Nahid Rana for the Australia Tests to a side strain

stories.title: Woman critically hurt in Delhi's 'Chalo Sansad' protest crackdown taken off ventilator, now conscious and stable
stories.what_happened: RML Hospital says the injured 21-year-old woman was successfully taken off ventilator support and is now breathing unaided, conscious, and responding appropriately to doctors, though she remains under close observation in intensive care. Hospital authorities also had to step in to knock down social-media rumours that she had died, confirming she is alive and stable.
key_points: 21-year-old protester injured in the July 20 CJP march-on-Parliament crackdown
Taken off ventilator support and breathing on her own after nearly 72 hours
She is now conscious and responding to doctors at Delhi's RML Hospital
Hospital had to publicly deny social-media rumours she had died

depth.background: The 'Chalo Sansad' (March to Parliament) protest was staged by the Gen-Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) movement, demanding accountability for leaked exam papers and, more broadly, action on youth unemployment. On July 20, police action against the marchers left more than 100 protesters needing hospital treatment, including a 21-year-old woman who suffered critical injuries and was placed on ventilator support at Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital.

thread.previously: We reported that Education Minister Pradhan had resigned, Modi addressed students directly for the first time, and fresh government-CJP talks were underway over deeper youth-unemployment demands.
thread.changed: The human cost of the movement's most violent day — the July 20 police crackdown during the Chalo Sansad march — is now clearer: a critically injured 21-year-old protester has been taken off ventilator support and is recovering, after hospital officials had to publicly deny rumours she had died.

prev_ref.title: Modi faces fresh pressure as Gen-Z 'Cockroach' protest leaders hold another round of talks with the government

stories.title: AIADMK chief Palaniswami meets PM Modi in Tiruchirapalli, papering over a power-sharing rift ahead of Tamil Nadu's 2026 election
stories.what_happened: Palaniswami met Modi in Tiruchirapalli, rearranging his own statewide tour to make time for it. The meeting follows visible strain in the AIADMK-BJP alliance: AIADMK has publicly said it expects to form a majority government on its own in 2026, while senior BJP figures, including Union Home Minister Amit Shah, have said any resulting government would be a coalition with the BJP playing an integral role.
key_points: AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami (EPS) met PM Modi during Modi's Tamil Nadu visit
EPS rearranged his own state campaign schedule to fit in the meeting
Comes amid public friction: AIADMK says it will win a majority on its own; BJP leaders say it'll be a coalition with BJP central to it
Meeting happened in Tiruchirapalli, where Modi is staying ahead of events marking 1,000 years since Chola emperor Rajendra I's northern military campaign

depth.background: Tamil Nadu goes to the polls in 2026, and the AIADMK — one of the state's two dominant regional parties alongside the ruling DMK — is contesting in alliance with the BJP. AIADMK governed Tamil Nadu for years under J. Jayalalithaa before splitting into rival factions after her death; Palaniswami has since consolidated control of the party and is positioning it as the main challenger to the DMK.

stories.title: India stalls at 10th on the Commonwealth Games medal table as boxers and gymnasts keep hopes alive
stories.what_happened: Through three days of competition, India sits 10th on the Glasgow 2026 medal table with a single confirmed medal - a bronze won by Jhandu Kumar in men's heavyweight para powerlifting. In boxing, Sachin Siwach beat Canada's Keoma Al-Ahmadieh on a split decision to reach the round of 16, while Jadumani Singh also stayed alive in his bracket. In gymnastics, the women's team narrowly missed a team medal, but Pratishta Samanta moved into the top three of the vault standings after her subdivision, keeping her in contention for an individual final.
key_points: Only 1 confirmed medal after 3 days: Jhandu Kumar's bronze in para powerlifting
Boxer Sachin Siwach advances to the round of 16 with a split-decision win
Gymnast Pratishta Samanta cracks the top 3 in vault, chasing an individual final
Lovlina Borgohain already guaranteed at least a medal via a bye to the semifinal

depth.background: India entered the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games hoping to build on a strong showing at the 2022 edition. Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu opened the campaign chasing a third straight gold, and two-time champion boxer Lovlina Borgohain was seen as one of India's surest medal bets, drawing a bye straight into her semifinal.

stories.title: Assam flood death toll climbs to 66 as fresh deaths hit Sivasagar and Charaideo
stories.what_happened: The Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA) says the flood death toll has risen to 66 — 65 classified as general flood-related deaths and one as an urban-flood death — after four more people died in the past day, three in Sivasagar district and one in Charaideo. More than 6.5 lakh people are now affected across 10 districts, and the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) are carrying out rescue and relief work alongside the state government.
key_points: Death toll rises to 66, up from 61 a day earlier
Four more deaths reported in the last 24 hours — three in Sivasagar, one in Charaideo
Over 6.5 lakh (650,000) people now affected across 10 districts
NDRF and SDRF continue rescue and relief operations

depth.background: Assam is hit by severe monsoon flooding most years as the Brahmaputra river and its tributaries swell, but this year's floods have been unusually deadly and widespread, already affecting hundreds of thousands of people and drawing in national disaster-response teams alongside the state's own machinery.

thread.previously: Assam's flood toll had jumped to 61, with 14 deaths in a single day and over 700,000 people affected.
thread.changed: The toll has risen further to 66 after four more deaths in the last 24 hours, while the affected population is now reported at over 6.5 lakh (650,000) across 10 districts.

prev_ref.title: Assam's flood toll jumps to 61 — 14 people died in a single day as 700,000+ are now affected

stories.title: Mexican rookie Noel León wins his first Formula 2 Feature Race at the Hungaroring
stories.what_happened: León won Sunday's F2 Feature Race at the Hungaroring, the same Budapest circuit hosting the Hungarian Grand Prix. It's his first Feature Race win of the season, having already taken Sprint Race wins earlier this year in Montreal and Monaco — the Montreal win made him the first Mexican driver to win an F2 race in the modern era.
key_points: León, a 21-year-old rookie for Campos Racing, took his maiden F2 Feature Race win at Budapest's Hungaroring
It adds to two earlier Sprint Race wins this season, in Montreal and Monaco
A Feature Race is F2's longer, higher-points race — a bigger scalp than a Sprint win
Comes the same race weekend Lando Norris won the main Hungarian Grand Prix

depth.background: Formula 2 is the main feeder series directly below Formula 1 — most current F1 grid drivers competed in it (or its predecessor, GP2) before graduating up. Each F2 race weekend runs two races: a shorter Sprint Race and a longer, higher-points Feature Race. León, from Monterrey, Mexico, worked his way up through US and European junior single-seater categories before joining Campos Racing for his F2 rookie season this year.

stories.title: Berlin names 21-year-old Islamist extremist as suspect in fatal Pride attack, launches manhunt
stories.what_happened: Berlin police have identified the suspect as a 21-year-old man, named in reports as Abdul B., who is already known to authorities as part of the city's Islamist extremist scene and was released from a juvenile detention centre only in May 2026. Officers describe him as slim, about 1.9 metres tall, with black hair, wearing a black hoodie and white trousers at the time of the attack. Germany's elite counter-terrorism unit GSG 9, along with helicopters and other aerial surveillance, is now involved in the manhunt. Police have not confirmed a motive and are warning the public not to approach him.
key_points: Suspect named as a 21-year-old known to Berlin's Islamist extremist scene
He had been released from a juvenile detention centre only in May 2026
Elite counter-terrorism unit GSG 9 and aerial units are now hunting him
Motive still not officially confirmed; public warned not to approach him

depth.background: Christopher Street Day (CSD) is Germany's version of Pride, named after the New York street where the 1969 Stonewall uprising began; Berlin's is one of Europe's largest. On Saturday night a van drove into the crowd celebrating in the central Tiergarten park, killing a woman and injuring 16 people, eight seriously. The driver fled on foot, and for hours German authorities gave few details on who they were looking for.

thread.previously: A white van plowed into the crowd at Berlin's Christopher Street Day (Pride) celebration in Tiergarten park on Saturday night, killing one woman and injuring 16 people, eight seriously. The driver fled the scene and no motive was given.
thread.changed: Police have now named the suspect as a 21-year-old known to Berlin's Islamist extremist scene who was released from juvenile detention just two months earlier. He remains at large as GSG 9 and aerial units search for him; a motive is still not officially confirmed.

prev_ref.title: Van rams into crowd at Berlin's Pride celebration, killing one and injuring 16

stories.title: Sudan's army seizes the town of Bara, easing pressure on a besieged regional capital, as a US-brokered truce push continues
stories.what_happened: Sudan's army captured the town of Bara, less than 50km from Al Obeid, loosening the RSF's grip on the besieged city — a notable battlefield gain given Kordofan is now the war's central front. At the same time, the army is demanding the RSF completely withdraw from the cities it holds as its price for accepting a US-proposed 90-day truce meant to open the door to a lasting ceasefire.
key_points: Army captured Bara, under 50km from besieged Al Obeid in North Kordofan
Kordofan is now the war's main front after the army lost all of Darfur last year
Army wants the rival RSF to fully withdraw from captured cities before any truce
The US has proposed a 90-day truce meant to lead toward a permanent ceasefire
War has displaced 13+ million people; ~5 million face emergency-level hunger

depth.background: Sudan's civil war, which began in 2023, pits the national army against the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) for control of the country. The RSF swept through the western Darfur region last year, capturing its main city El Fasher, which pushed the fighting east into the Kordofan region — where the army has been trying to break an RSF siege of Al Obeid, North Kordofan's capital and a key army stronghold.

stories.title: France mobilizes the military and shortens the Tour de France finale as wildfires force 250,000+ evacuations
stories.what_happened: Wildfires burning across France and Spain have displaced more than 250,000 people combined, with France's government mobilizing the military to reinforce firefighters and emergency crews. Race organizers shortened the Tour de France's final stage from a 133km route starting in Thoiry to an 89km circuit confined to Paris, after officials reassigned part of the race's police security detail to wildfire response instead. The race itself continued, but with the shorter route and a smaller security footprint.
key_points: Nearly 200,000 evacuated in France, roughly 60,000 more near Madrid in Spain
France called in the military to help fight the fires and protect towns
Tour de France's final stage cut from 133km to 89km — about a third shorter
Race security officers were reassigned from the route to wildfire response instead

depth.background: A prolonged heatwave and weeks of dry conditions have turned much of France and Spain into a tinderbox this July, on top of the national wildfire emergency Spain already declared this week. The Tour de France, cycling's biggest race and one of the most-watched sporting events in the world, was in its final days, building to a traditional finish in Paris.

stories.title: F1's summer-break countdown: 17 drivers are out of contract for 2027 — and Alonso's own career decision is now due
stories.what_happened: Heading into F1's summer break (which follows the Hungarian Grand Prix), only five drivers — Max Verstappen, Lando Norris, Oscar Piastri, Charles Leclerc and Pierre Gasly — have contracts confirmed into 2027. Seventeen others, including seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton and veteran Fernando Alonso, are out of contract at the end of 2026, setting up a major reshuffling of the grid. Alonso is expected to make his own call — race on or retire — during the break, based partly on whether Aston Martin's new upgrades (unveiled this weekend in Hungary) close the gap to the front. Mercedes, meanwhile, still hasn't decided between George Russell and Kimi Antonelli for its two 2027 seats.
key_points: Only 5 drivers (Verstappen, Norris, Piastri, Leclerc, Gasly) have deals confirmed into 2027
17 drivers, including Hamilton and Alonso, are out of contract after 2026
Fernando Alonso, 45, is expected to decide his future during the upcoming summer break
Mercedes still hasn't confirmed either seat for 2027, with Russell and Antonelli competing for both

depth.background: Formula 1 drivers typically sign multi-year deals, and clusters of contracts expiring at the same time create what the paddock calls 'silly season' — a scramble of rumours, moves and announcements as teams and drivers sort out who races where next. 2026 is one of those years: new technical rules reshuffled which teams are competitive, which in turn has reshuffled who wants to move. Fernando Alonso, a two-time world champion now in the twilight of a 25-year career, has said his Aston Martin future — and possibly his F1 career — hinges on whether the team's 2026 upgrades finally make the car competitive.

stories.title: Ferrari admits it was 'our mistake' as Hamilton apologises for his reaction to a costly Hungarian GP penalty
stories.what_happened: During Saturday's Hungarian Grand Prix qualifying, Hamilton was on a slow in-lap when McLaren's Oscar Piastri came up behind him on a quick lap. Ferrari's radio warning came late, and Hamilton unintentionally blocked Piastri at Turn 1. The stewards handed Hamilton a three-place grid penalty, dropping him from a provisional 2nd to 5th on the grid. Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur publicly took the blame, saying the team warned Hamilton 'far too late.' Hamilton, visibly frustrated after qualifying, later apologised to the team during the pre-race drivers' parade for his reaction in the moment.
key_points: Hamilton impeded McLaren's Piastri in Q3 after a delayed radio warning from Ferrari
The FIA dropped Hamilton three places on the grid, from 2nd to 5th
Team boss Fred Vasseur says Ferrari told Hamilton 'far too late' that Piastri was coming
Hamilton apologised during the drivers' parade for his post-qualifying 'attitude'

depth.background: Lewis Hamilton joined Ferrari for the 2026 season as a seven-time world champion looking to add a first title with the Italian team. In qualifying, drivers must stay out of the way of rivals on a fast 'push lap' — if a driver is spotted by their team on a slow lap, the radio is supposed to warn them in time to move aside. A driver who blocks another gets penalised by race stewards even if it wasn't intentional, because F1's rules hold the team responsible for keeping their driver informed.

stories.title: Russia bombards Kyiv with ballistic missiles overnight, killing at least 7 across Ukraine
stories.what_happened: Russia struck Ukraine overnight with one guided X-59/69 missile, seven Iskander ballistic missiles and 136 long-range attack drones. Ukrainian air defenses intercepted the guided missile, five of the seven ballistic missiles, and 104 of the drones — but a residential building in Kyiv was hit, igniting fires. Regional authorities reported at least 7 civilians killed and 58 injured nationwide over the past 24 hours, including one person killed and twelve hurt in a separate daytime drone strike on Kharkiv. Russia also reported casualties from Ukrainian strikes, including on a Russian-held area.
key_points: Russia fired ballistic missiles and over 130 drones at Ukraine overnight
At least 7 civilians killed and 58 wounded across the country in the past day
A residential building in Kyiv was struck; a Kharkiv drone strike killed one more
Kazakhstan's president calls for the war to be frozen and talks to resume

depth.background: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, launched in February 2022, has continued despite periodic diplomatic efforts, including talks based on the original 2022 Istanbul framework. Overnight long-range strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities — mixing ballistic missiles with cheap, mass-produced Shahed-type drones — have become Russia's routine tactic to wear down Ukrainian air defenses and civilian morale, even as both sides periodically report troop and civilian losses from ongoing frontline and drone warfare.

stories.title: Drone strike kills civilians, including children, at a Sea of Azov holiday camp — each side blames the other
stories.what_happened: An overnight drone attack hit a holiday-camp area of Kyrylivka, a resort town on the Sea of Azov in Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia region. Russian-appointed regional governor Yevgeny Balitsky said 11 to 12 people were killed, including four or five children, with about 19 more wounded. Russian authorities and state media blamed Ukraine for the strike. Ukraine had not issued a public response to the accusation as of publication.
key_points: Overnight strike hit a resort area in Kyrylivka, a Russian-occupied town on the Sea of Azov
Russian-installed officials say 11-12 dead including 4-5 children, ~19 wounded
Russia blames Ukraine; Kyiv has not yet responded to the accusation
Comes the same week Russia struck a Kyiv arms exhibition, killing 10

depth.background: This stretch of Ukraine's Azov Sea coast, near the city of Melitopol, has been under Russian occupation since 2022. Russia has resettled and marketed it as a domestic beach holiday destination, so it is often full of civilian tourists rather than military personnel. Both sides in this war now regularly use long-range drones and missiles to hit targets far from the front line, and both have been accused of strikes that killed civilians.

stories.title: Verstappen fitted with a fresh Honda engine for the Hungarian GP after a hidden crack turns up
stories.what_happened: A closer physical inspection on Saturday evening found a crack in a structural area of the engine that Honda said it hadn't seen before, prompting an overnight swap to a new power unit for Sunday's race. Because this is only the third engine Verstappen has used this season — within F1's per-driver allocation before penalties apply — he faces no grid penalty and keeps his third-place starting spot.
key_points: Honda found a crack while re-checking the engine from Verstappen's Silverstone crash
Red Bull swapped in a new power unit on Saturday night
No grid penalty — it's only his third engine this season, within the allowed limit
A fourth unit later this year would trigger a 10-place grid drop

depth.background: Verstappen wrecked his car in a heavy, high-speed crash with Lewis Hamilton at the British Grand Prix at Silverstone. Honda sent that power unit back to its Sakura facility in Japan for inspection, and initial checks said it was fine — Verstappen used it again through Hungarian GP qualifying.

stories.title: West Indies claw back from 23/1 to 194/3 as Hodge's unbeaten 83 steadies a rain-hit Day 1 vs Pakistan
stories.what_happened: West Indies slipped to 23/1 early in the day as Pakistan's bowlers, led by Mohammad Abbas, made early inroads, with rain repeatedly stopping play. Kavem Hodge and Shai Hope then put together an unbroken partnership to steady the innings, with Hodge finishing the rain-shortened day unbeaten on 83 off 181 balls. West Indies closed play at 194 for 3.
key_points: West Indies were reduced to 23/1 early after choosing to bat first
Kavem Hodge (83 not out) and Shai Hope (37 not out) rebuilt with an unbroken stand
Rain repeatedly interrupted play at the new-look Brian Lara Stadium, Tarouba
West Indies closed Day 1 on 194/3 in the series-opening Test

depth.background: This is the first of a multi-match Test series between West Indies and Pakistan, being played at the Brian Lara Stadium in Tarouba, Trinidad — a venue that has recently been redeveloped. West Indies won the toss and chose to bat first, but early results were shaky.

thread.previously: We reported West Indies slipped to 23/1 early on Day 1, with rain and Mohammad Abbas causing early trouble at the redeveloped Tarouba venue.
thread.changed: West Indies recovered through an unbroken Hodge-Hope partnership to close the rain-hit day at a much healthier 194/3, with Hodge unbeaten on 83.
