stories.title: Trump quietly halts nightly US strikes on Iran, breaking a 13-day streak
stories.what_happened: US Central Command did not announce any new overnight strikes on Iran for the first time since the campaign began nearly two weeks ago. Trump directed the military not to conduct new strikes on Friday, breaking the daily-attack pattern. Iran also reported no new strikes on American targets overnight.
key_points: US skipped a night of strikes on Iran for the first time in nearly two weeks
Trump personally ordered the pause on Friday, officials say
No new Iranian strikes on US targets were reported either
Houthi attacks on Saudi oil sites kept a separate front open

depth.background: On June 27, a US-brokered ceasefire between Israel/the US and Iran collapsed, and the US began nightly bombing runs on Iranian targets that ran for 13 straight days. At least four US service members and dozens of Iranians have been killed since. Trump had recently floated a 'massive attack' but also said negotiations might make it unnecessary.

thread.previously: We reported Trump was floating that a bigger attack on Iran might not be necessary and was considering negotiations, even as US strikes hit a 13th consecutive night.
thread.changed: That talk turned into action: the US skipped a night of strikes entirely for the first time since the campaign began, and Iran didn't retaliate either — though officials caution it may not last.

prev_ref.title: Trump says a 'massive attack' on Iran 'may not be necessary,' floats negotiations as US strikes hit a 13th straight night

stories.title: Houthis hit back at two Saudi Aramco oil sites, setting a refinery ablaze as Brent tops $100
stories.what_happened: In the early hours of Saturday, Houthi forces fired a barrage of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco-linked sites in the Red Sea towns of Jazan and Yanbu. A Houthi military spokesperson said it was retaliation for the Saudi strike on Hodeidah and Kamaran Island. NASA's satellite fire-monitoring system detected an abnormal temperature spike at Jazan around 4:17am local time, and residents filmed a fire burning at the refinery. At least five explosions were reported in Jazan; nearby commercial flights were diverted.
key_points: Dozens of missiles and drones hit Aramco facilities in Jazan and Yanbu
Fire breaks out at the Jazan refinery, one of Saudi's newest, 400,000 barrels/day
Yanbu is Saudi Arabia's main working oil-export route now that Hormuz is blocked
Brent crude jumped back above $100 a barrel on the news

depth.background: Since a US-Israel campaign against Iran began earlier this year, Iran-aligned Houthi rebels in Yemen have been attacking ships and infrastructure to pressure the Gulf states that back the US position. Saudi Arabia struck the Houthi-held port of Hodeidah in Yemen days ago, hitting back after Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping. The Strait of Hormuz — the narrow chokepoint at the mouth of the Gulf that a large share of the world's oil passes through — has already been effectively closed by the fighting, so Yanbu, Saudi Arabia's Red Sea export terminal, has become one of the last ways Saudi oil reaches world markets.

thread.previously: We reported Saudi Arabia struck the Houthi-held port of Hodeidah in Yemen, retaliating for Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping.
thread.changed: The Houthis have now hit back directly at Saudi soil, striking Aramco facilities in Jazan and Yanbu, setting a refinery on fire and pushing Brent crude back above $100 a barrel.

prev_ref.title: Saudi Arabia strikes Houthi-held Hodeidah, opening a new front as it hits back for Red Sea attacks

stories.title: Iran rejects Trump's claim it's 'getting more serious' about talks — a general says Tehran would welcome a US ground invasion
stories.what_happened: Speaking Friday, Trump said the US and Iran remain in contact and that he believes Iran is 'getting more serious' about a negotiated end to the war. An Iranian military official identified by state media as General Asadi publicly rejected that characterization, saying Iran's fight is a 'war of attrition' with no end date, and adding Iran hopes American ground forces put themselves in a position where Iran 'can engage them on the ground.' Trump separately told reporters the US military is 'locked and loaded' for a heavier attack if Iran doesn't return to serious talks.
key_points: Trump said Friday the US and Iran are still talking and Tehran is 'getting more serious'
An Iranian general publicly dismissed that, saying Iran's war is 'one that will not end'
The same general said Iran wants US ground troops to 'find themselves in a position where we can engage them'
No new US strikes were reported Friday night, after 13 consecutive nights of bombing

depth.background: The US, Israel and Iran agreed a memorandum of understanding weeks ago meant to open 60 days of talks toward a wider peace deal covering Iran's nuclear program and the Strait of Hormuz. That truce collapsed, and the US has since bombed targets inside Iran for 13 straight nights. Trump has said he could end the war either 'diplomatically or militarily,' and has floated both continued talks and a bigger strike.

stories.title: DRC's Ebola outbreak becomes the fastest-spreading ever recorded — deaths pass 1,300
stories.what_happened: The death toll from DRC's current Ebola outbreak has surged past 1,300, with confirmed cases topping 3,000 as of this weekend — a more than 40% jump in just five days, according to Al Jazeera and UN reporting. A public health official described the virus as 'spreading like a wildfire.' Neighboring Uganda has also confirmed cases, and isolated imported cases have turned up as far away as France and the United States.
key_points: Confirmed cases have climbed past 3,000; deaths have surpassed 1,300
Cases rose more than 40% in just five days
WHO says the virus is 'spreading like a wildfire'
Most new infections can't be traced to a known source, making containment harder

depth.background: Ebola is a severe viral disease first identified near the Ebola River in what is now the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) in 1976; it causes fever, severe bleeding, and organ failure, and has killed a large share of those infected in past outbreaks. The DRC has battled more Ebola outbreaks than any other country, but health officials say this one — declared earlier this year — is spreading faster than any previous outbreak on record.

stories.title: Anahat Singh, 18, becomes the first Indian ever to win the World Junior Squash title
stories.what_happened: Anahat Singh won the girls' singles final at the 2026 World Squash Junior Championships in Niagara-on-the-Lake, Canada, beating Egypt's Ruqayya Salem in straight games (11-3, 11-7, 11-9) on July 25, 2026. It's the first time a non-Egyptian player has won the title since 2010, ending a 15-year run of Egyptian champions. Singh dropped just two games across her entire six-match run to the title. Prime Minister Narendra Modi publicly congratulated her.
key_points: Beat Egypt's Ruqayya Salem 11-3, 11-7, 11-9 in the final in Canada
Ends Egypt's 15-year grip on the girls' singles title
First non-Egyptian champion since an American won it in 2010
Dropped only two games across her whole six-match campaign

depth.background: Squash is a fast indoor racket sport played in a four-walled court; the World Junior Championships are the sport's top under-19 event, and Egypt has dominated the girls' singles title for the better part of two decades thanks to its deep youth squash pipeline. Anahat Singh is an 18-year-old Indian player who has been rising through junior and senior ranks for several years and was already a national talking point after past regional junior titles.

stories.title: Sarnath, where the Buddha gave his first sermon, is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site
stories.what_happened: UNESCO's World Heritage Committee formally inscribed the 'Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath' on the World Heritage List during its 48th session in Busan, South Korea, on July 25, 2026. The listing covers the Deer Park area, including the Dhamek Stupa (a large dome-shaped Buddhist shrine) and the Dharmarajika and Chaukhandi Stupas. It is India's 45th UNESCO World Heritage Site, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi publicly welcomed the news.
key_points: UNESCO's World Heritage Committee inscribed Sarnath on July 25 at its Busan, South Korea session
It's India's 45th World Heritage site
The nomination had waited 28 years for approval
Site includes the Dhamek Stupa, Dharmarajika Stupa, and Chaukhandi Stupa near Varanasi

depth.background: Sarnath, near Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh, is one of Buddhism's four holiest sites — it's where, over 2,500 years ago, the Buddha is believed to have delivered his first sermon after attaining enlightenment, setting out the core teachings that became Buddhism. UNESCO's World Heritage List recognizes places of outstanding cultural or natural value to humanity; getting on it brings global recognition, tourism potential, and stronger legal protection against damage or unchecked development. India first nominated Sarnath decades ago.

sources.name: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

stories.title: Verstappen can now trigger an exit clause to leave Red Bull for 2027 — if he's not top-2 by August
stories.what_happened: Verstappen's contract includes an exit clause letting him leave Red Bull for another team in 2027, but only if he's outside the top two positions in the Drivers' Championship when the sport's summer break begins in August. Kimi Antonelli currently leads the championship with 204 points, with Lewis Hamilton second and George Russell third — meaning Verstappen, who has struggled with Red Bull's 2026 car, is not currently inside the top two and would be eligible to trigger the clause. He would have a three-month window, from August to October, to make the move official. His manager says the Verstappen camp wants to decide quickly, possibly before the break even starts.
key_points: Verstappen is signed through 2028, but his contract has a release clause
It activates if he's outside the top 2 in the championship at the start of August's summer break
He'd get a 3-month window (August–October) to use it
His manager says a decision could come 'possibly even before the summer break'

depth.background: Verstappen signed a seven-season extension with Red Bull running to 2028 — an unusually long deal in F1, where top drivers typically sign 2-3 year contracts. He reportedly had 'longstanding apprehension' about the sweeping new technical rules introduced for 2026, and got Red Bull to agree to a specific escape route in case the new-rules car wasn't competitive.

stories.title: OpenAI fully launches GPT-5.6 Sol after a month-long US government security review
stories.what_happened: OpenAI said this weekend it has now fully released GPT-5.6 Sol, its most capable model yet, after the US government's review pushed the launch back about a month from its original July 9 preview. Access is still limited to roughly 20 vetted organizations while a broader public rollout is prepared 'in the coming weeks.' On the 'Agents' Last Exam' benchmark, a test of long, professional, multi-step tasks across 55 fields, Sol scored 53.6, more than 13 points ahead of the closest rival model from Anthropic.
key_points: OpenAI's most advanced model, delayed a month at Washington's request
A new executive order lets the government preview 'frontier' AI models first
Sol beats rival models on complex reasoning and coding benchmarks
Public rollout still limited to about 20 vetted partners for now

depth.background: OpenAI first previewed the GPT-5.6 family on July 9, 2026 - three tiers called Sol (flagship), Terra (mid-tier), and Luna (fast and cheap). Weeks earlier, on June 2, President Trump signed an executive order letting AI companies voluntarily give the US government up to 30 days of early access to any 'frontier' model before it reaches the public, so officials can check for national-security risks like cyberattack or bioweapon misuse. OpenAI ran Sol through that window before releasing it more widely.

stories.title: Israel locks down northern West Bank and raids a village after a deadly settler-Palestinian shootout
stories.what_happened: On Friday, a group of Israeli settlers entered a restricted area near the Palestinian village of Tal, close to Nablus, for what officials called an unauthorized, uncoordinated hike. Clashes broke out with local residents, and in the gunfire that followed, four Palestinians and two Israeli soldiers were killed. Accounts differ: Palestinian officials say settlers provoked the confrontation by trying to attack villagers; Israel's military first described the civilians involved as unarmed hikers, then acknowledged some were armed and said both sides had opened fire before troops intervened. In response, Israel reinforced troops, imposed a curfew across large parts of the northern West Bank, postponed soldiers' leave, and on Saturday carried out a large-scale raid on a village near Nablus, capturing two people linked to the shooting. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also ordered military demolitions, new movement restrictions on Palestinians in the area, and moves to legalize outposts that are currently illegal even under Israeli law.
key_points: 4 Palestinians and 2 Israeli soldiers killed Friday near the village of Tal, close to Nablus
Israeli settlers were on an 'unauthorized' hike into a restricted area when clashes broke out
Israel imposed a curfew, reinforced troops, and raided a nearby village, capturing two suspects
Netanyahu ordered demolitions, new movement restrictions on Palestinians, and moved to legalize illegal outposts

depth.background: The West Bank is Palestinian territory that Israel has militarily occupied since 1967; roughly 500,000 Israeli settlers now live there in communities most of the world considers illegal under international law, alongside about 3 million Palestinians. Friction between settlers and Palestinian villagers over land and access is constant, and 'unauthorized hikes' by settlers into Palestinian-controlled or restricted areas have repeatedly been the spark for deadly clashes in recent years.

stories.title: Critical, unpatched security flaw in Alibaba's Fastjson is being actively exploited — no fix exists yet
stories.what_happened: Security researchers at FearsOff discovered a critical vulnerability in Fastjson, tracked as CVE-2026-16723, that lets an attacker send a specially crafted piece of JSON data to a vulnerable application and run their own code on it — no password or login required. Fastjson's maintainers published an advisory on July 21. Security firm ThreatBook confirmed real-world attacks starting July 22. As of the latest reporting on July 25, Alibaba had not released a fix, and the attack works even when standard safety settings that normally block similar bugs are turned on.
key_points: CVE-2026-16723, severity 9.0 out of 10 — critical
Affects Fastjson 1.2.68 through 1.2.83, widely used in enterprise Java apps
Attackers can run code with no login needed, no patch available yet
Active attacks confirmed since July 22, mostly against US firms

depth.background: Fastjson is a free code library, maintained by Chinese tech giant Alibaba, that lets Java programs read and write JSON data (a common format for exchanging information between computer systems). Because it's fast and free, it got embedded into huge numbers of enterprise applications built on Java and Spring Boot — the same programming stack used by banks, hospitals, retailers and many other large organizations worldwide.

stories.title: First death confirmed as Spain and France wildfires grow to 25,000 hectares; Germany sends aid
stories.what_happened: Authorities in Manises, Spain confirmed the fires' first fatality. Fire officials say roughly 30 separate blazes are burning simultaneously across southwestern France's Gironde and Landes regions, with the total burned area now near 25,000 hectares. Around 50,000 people remain affected in the wider Madrid region alone. Germany has sent an A400 military transport plane, helicopters and rescue personnel to reinforce French firefighting crews.
key_points: One person confirmed dead in Manises, Spain
Fires have burned roughly 25,000 hectares so far — nearly the size of a mid-sized city
About 30 separate fires are still burning across southwestern France
Germany is sending helicopters, a military transport plane and rescuers to help French firefighters

depth.background: Spain and France are in the grip of an unusually intense, record-breaking wildfire season, driven by a prolonged heatwave and tinder-dry vegetation across southern Europe. Officials in both countries had already evacuated more than 250,000 people, and Spain had declared its first-ever national wildfire emergency. Fires like this spread fastest when high heat, low humidity, and strong wind combine — exactly the conditions much of the Iberian Peninsula and southwestern France have seen this month.

thread.previously: Wildfires had forced over 250,000 evacuations across southwestern France and central Spain, and Spain declared its first-ever national wildfire emergency as the fire season hit a record.
thread.changed: The fires have now claimed their first confirmed death, grown to roughly 25,000 hectares, and Germany has sent military aircraft and rescue crews to reinforce French firefighters.

stories.title: Bearman is routing Ocon at Haas — and it's shaping the team's 2027 driver call
stories.what_happened: Through the first 10 rounds of the 2026 season, Bearman has beaten Ocon 11-3 in qualifying head-to-heads and out-scored him 18 championship points to 3. Bearman himself has cautioned it hasn't always been a fair fight, citing parts-supply inconsistency that has affected both cars at times. Haas's team boss has already said an inconsistent car is clouding a clean read on Ocon's case as the team weighs its 2027 driver lineup.
key_points: Bearman leads Ocon 11-3 in qualifying head-to-heads through 10 rounds
Bearman has out-scored Ocon 18 championship points to 3 this season
Bearman says the fight 'hasn't always been fair' due to Haas's inconsistent parts supply
Haas is weighing its 2027 lineup with Ocon's seat now in question

depth.background: Haas signed Esteban Ocon, a race-winning former Alpine and Mercedes-backed driver, alongside rookie Oliver Bearman, pairing an experienced hand with a highly-rated young talent from Ferrari's junior program. How that pairing performs directly affects who Haas keeps for 2027, since a struggling teammate makes it harder to judge whether the car or the driver is the problem.

thread.previously: Haas's boss said an inconsistent car was clouding a clean read on Ocon's case as the team weighed its 2027 driver lineup.
thread.changed: New season-long numbers show Bearman leading Ocon 11-3 in qualifying and 18-3 in points, sharpening the case Haas has to weigh.

prev_ref.title: Haas boss says an inconsistent car is clouding Ocon's case, as the team weighs its 2027 driver lineup

stories.title: Wildfires force over 250,000 evacuations across southwestern France and central Spain
stories.what_happened: French authorities ordered new evacuations of towns in Gironde, including Bordeaux suburbs Le Haillan, Eysines and Mérignac, as a wildfire that has already burned roughly 32,700 hectares (about three times the area of Paris) and destroyed 140 homes pushed toward the city. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said more than 200,000 people have now been evacuated from the Gironde and Landes regions, calling the fire 'unprecedented' because it has grown large enough to generate its own winds. Across the border, Spain confirmed its first wildfire fatality as a blaze near Madrid burned about 10,000 hectares and a neighboring fire in Ávila province consumed 13,000–15,000 hectares more.
key_points: Bordeaux suburbs ordered to evacuate as the Gironde fire triples in size
Spain confirms its first wildfire death, near Madrid
Over 250,000 people evacuated across both countries combined
Spain's interior ministry says one blaze is 'beyond the capacity of firefighters to contain'

depth.background: Gironde, the wine-and-pine-forest region around Bordeaux, has burned before — a 2022 fire there was one of Europe's worst in decades. This summer's heatwave across southern Europe has left vegetation tinder-dry, and scientists say climate change is making these fires bigger and faster-moving than in the past.

stories.title: Trump confirms Netanyahu's White House sit-down for Tuesday — with fresh intel on Iran's nuclear program
stories.what_happened: President Trump publicly confirmed that Prime Minister Netanyahu will fly to Washington on Monday and meet him at the White House on Tuesday, July 28. Netanyahu will also attend the funeral of Senator Lindsey Graham during the trip. Israeli officials say Netanyahu intends to present Trump with fresh intelligence suggesting Iran is quietly rebuilding its nuclear and military capacity under its wartime leadership.
key_points: Trump says Netanyahu travels to Washington Monday, meets him Tuesday
Netanyahu will also attend Senator Lindsey Graham's funeral
He plans to show Trump intelligence on Iran's nuclear 'recovery' efforts
First in-person Trump-Netanyahu meeting since the Iran war reignited

depth.background: Israel and the US have been coordinating closely since Iran's ceasefire collapsed and US strikes on Iran resumed this month, now stretching past 13 straight nights. A Trump-Netanyahu meeting had been discussed for weeks without a firm date, while both governments weighed how much further to push a war that has already drawn in the Houthis and Saudi Arabia.

thread.previously: We reported Netanyahu was heading to the White House for his first face-to-face with Trump since the Iran war began, without a confirmed date.
thread.changed: Trump has now confirmed the exact timeline — Netanyahu arrives Monday, meets him Tuesday July 28 — and Israeli officials say he'll bring new intelligence on Iran's nuclear recovery efforts.

stories.title: US quietly empties its two biggest Gulf air bases as Iran's retaliatory strikes keep coming
stories.what_happened: Satellite imagery reviewed by open-source analysts shows Al Udeid's aircraft count falling from 17 to just 3 before the base was completely emptied; Al Dhafra has seen a similar drawdown. The moves follow Iranian strikes on Al Udeid, Al Dhafra, Ali Al Salem in Kuwait, and Fifth Fleet-linked sites in Bahrain, as Tehran's retaliation for the US-Iran war expands to hit bases across the Gulf.
key_points: Al Udeid (Qatar) and Al Dhafra (UAE) — the US military's largest Middle East hubs — have been fully evacuated of aircraft
Satellite images show the drawdown happening gradually over recent days
Comes after Iranian strikes hit Al Udeid, Al Dhafra, Ali Al Salem (Kuwait), and Fifth Fleet-linked sites in Bahrain
Iran's retaliation for the wider US-Iran war keeps spreading across the Gulf

depth.background: Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar is the forward headquarters for US Central Command — effectively the nerve center for American air power across the Middle East. Al Dhafra in the UAE hosts US and allied fighter jets and surveillance aircraft. Both became targets as Iran widened its retaliation for the war with the US and Israel, hitting American installations across the Gulf states that host US forces.

thread.previously: Yesterday we reported Iran had fired drones at US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan as its retaliation for the war spread across the Gulf.
thread.changed: The US has now fully evacuated aircraft from its two largest regional hubs, Al Udeid (Qatar) and Al Dhafra (UAE), after strikes hit those bases too — a much bigger step than the drone attacks reported yesterday.

stories.title: US measles cases hit a 35-year high — over 2,300 confirmed as vaccine hesitancy grows
stories.what_happened: The CDC has confirmed 2,318 measles cases across the US so far in 2026 — already above all of 2025's total (2,289 cases, itself a record) and the highest count since 1991, when 9,643 cases were recorded. Officials say 93% of this year's cases are outbreak-linked, and the same share are in people who were not vaccinated. There have been 35 distinct outbreaks so far.
key_points: 2,318 confirmed US measles cases in 2026 — the most since 1991
93% of this year's cases are in unvaccinated people
Kindergarten vaccination rates have slipped to about 92%, below the 95% needed for herd immunity
35 separate outbreaks recorded so far, and cases are still rising

depth.background: Measles was declared eliminated in the US in 2000 thanks to a highly effective two-dose vaccine (MMR) — meaning the disease no longer spread continuously on its own, even though travelers occasionally brought cases in. Rising vaccine hesitancy over the past several years, especially in some states and communities, has been chipping away at the immunity level that kept those imported cases from turning into bigger outbreaks.

stories.title: Government agrees to ₹1 crore compensation and FIR withdrawals as CJP formally calls off its NEET protest
stories.what_happened: Following a third round of talks, the Centre agreed to CJP's core demands: ₹1 crore in compensation for the families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide, and withdrawal of FIRs filed against protesters anywhere in India. CJP's spokesperson said the group is withdrawing its agitation 'in good faith,' with the government due to hand over written commitments by Tuesday and a follow-up round of talks scheduled after four weeks.
key_points: CJP declares it is withdrawing its agitation after the Centre accepted its core demands
Government to pay ₹1 crore compensation to families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide
FIRs against protesters to be withdrawn nationwide
Next round of talks scheduled in four weeks; written commitments promised by Tuesday

depth.background: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has led weeks of protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar over alleged irregularities in the NEET medical entrance exam, including a paper leak and deaths by suicide among affected aspirants. The protests escalated through clashes with police, an internet shutdown near the protest site, and pressure that ultimately led Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign.

stories.title: Mumbai's FDA suspends licences of three well-known restaurants in a widening food-safety crackdown
stories.what_happened: The FDA suspended the food business licences of three well-known Mumbai eateries — Shalimar Restaurant, Noor Mohammadi Hotel, and Rehmania Restaurant — after inspections found serious hygiene violations. Since late May, authorities have inspected 443 hotels, restaurants and dhabas, issued 161 improvement notices, and suspended 56 licences overall. Mumbai's mayor has now directed the civic health department to run ward-level inspections focused on repeat offenders.
key_points: Shalimar, Noor Mohammadi, and Rehmania restaurants lose their licences after hygiene inspections
Part of a statewide drive: 443 eateries inspected since May, 56 licences suspended so far
Mumbai's mayor has ordered ward-by-ward inspections targeting repeat offenders
The same crackdown has also uncovered synthetic/adulterated milk production units

depth.background: Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has been running an intensifying hygiene enforcement drive since May 2026, after complaints and spot checks turned up unsafe food-handling practices at popular eateries and dairy suppliers across the state.

stories.title: Rain and Mohammad Abbas restrict West Indies to 23/1 on Day 1 of the Pakistan Test at a brand-new venue
stories.what_happened: West Indies won the toss and chose to bat first in the series opener at the new Brian Lara Cricket Academy in Tarouba. Rain repeatedly interrupted play, and Pakistan's Mohammad Abbas exploited the seam-friendly conditions to keep West Indies to 23 for 1 at the lunch interval, with more rain threatening the rest of the day's play.
key_points: West Indies win the toss, choose to bat, but close a rain-hit session at 23/1
Mohammad Abbas' seam bowling proves the difference in tough batting conditions
First-ever Test match at Trinidad's new Brian Lara Cricket Academy venue in Tarouba
Part of the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27 cycle

depth.background: Pakistan came into this two-match series against West Indies with Babar Azam newly reinstated as Test captain after Shan Masood was dropped following a poor run of results. The series is part of the ongoing World Test Championship cycle, where results feed into a table deciding who reaches the next WTC final.

stories.title: Sunrisers Leeds hold off Southern Brave by five runs for their first win of the Hundred season
stories.what_happened: Mitchell Marsh (69) and Dan Lawrence (51 not out) hit half-centuries to lift Sunrisers Leeds to 187 for 5. Southern Brave fought back through Tom McKinney (44) and Tristan Stubbs (43 not out) but fell 5 runs short, finishing on 182 for 5, handing Sunrisers Leeds their first win of the season.
key_points: Mitchell Marsh (69) and Dan Lawrence (51*) power Sunrisers Leeds to 187/5
Southern Brave fall 5 runs short, finishing 182/5 in reply
McKinney (44) and Stubbs (43*) kept the chase alive late for Brave
First win of the season for Sunrisers Leeds, at Headingley

depth.background: The Hundred is England's 100-ball franchise cricket tournament, run each summer with eight men's and eight women's teams. Sunrisers Leeds had struggled for form so far this season heading into this match against Southern Brave at Headingley.

stories.title: Sergio Perez reveals he felt 'dizzy' and not fully fit during Hungarian GP qualifying
stories.what_happened: Perez said he felt dizzy and not '100% physically' during Saturday's Hungarian Grand Prix qualifying session, a day after his Cadillac's brake fire scare in final practice. He ended up qualifying last on the grid, 22nd, 3.045 seconds off pole, with teammate Valtteri Bottas just ahead in 21st. Team boss Christian Horner said he hopes Perez can take confidence forward despite the tough weekend, while stressing the car's inconsistency needs to improve.
key_points: Perez says he wasn't '100% physically' during Saturday's qualifying
Comes a day after his Cadillac caught fire and forced a red flag in final practice
He qualified 22nd and last, behind teammate Valtteri Bottas in 21st
Team boss Horner says he hopes Perez can 'take confidence' from the weekend despite the results

depth.background: Sergio Perez joined the new Cadillac F1 team for 2026 after a difficult end to his Red Bull career. His season has been inconsistent, and Friday's Hungarian GP practice saw his car suffer a brake fire that forced him to pull over and brought out a red flag, raising doubts about whether his car would even be fit to qualify.

stories.title: Nvidia and South Korea's SK Group unveil a $500 billion-plus AI buildout — chips, memory, and data centers
stories.what_happened: Nvidia and South Korea's SK Group announced a more than $500 billion initiative spanning AI data centers and next-generation memory, formalized via letters of intent at an AI summit in San Francisco. SK Hynix will supply Nvidia with next-gen HBM4 memory, SK Telecom will build a 2-gigawatt AI data center powered by Nvidia's upcoming Vera Rubin chips (due online in 2027), and Nvidia is separately investing $1 billion in Korean cloud firm Naver. In a related move, Samsung Electronics signed an estimated $200 billion memory-and-foundry agreement with chip designer Broadcom.
key_points: Nvidia and SK Group announced letters of intent worth $500bn+ in AI infrastructure
SK Hynix will secure Nvidia's next-gen memory supply and co-develop HBM4 chips
SK Telecom to build a 2-gigawatt AI data center on Nvidia's Vera Rubin chips, live in 2027
Nvidia is also putting $1bn into Naver, and Samsung struck a related $200bn deal with Broadcom

depth.background: Building a modern AI system needs three things at once: powerful processor chips (Nvidia's specialty), the ultra-fast memory chips that feed data to those processors (called HBM, or High Bandwidth Memory — SK Hynix is a world leader here), and the physical data centers to house it all. As AI models get bigger, all three have become scarce and expensive, so the companies that make them are increasingly locking each other into long-term supply deals rather than competing openly on the spot market. South Korea's SK Group and Samsung are the two dominant global suppliers of this HBM memory.

stories.title: Guyana Amazon Warriors edge Desert Vipers by 2 wickets to stay unbeaten in the Global Super League
stories.what_happened: Guyana Amazon Warriors chased down Desert Vipers' total of 205 for 6, reaching 206 for 8, to win by 2 wickets and stay unbeaten through their first two matches of the tournament. Romario Shepherd's 52 earned him Player of the Match. Desert Vipers, who had also lost their previous match to Lahore Qalandars by 38 runs, remain winless.
key_points: Guyana chased down 206/8 in reply to Desert Vipers' 205/6
A tight 2-wicket win — Guyana's second victory in as many games
Romario Shepherd named Player of the Match for his 52
Desert Vipers now winless after 2 matches

depth.background: The Global Super League is a T20 tournament in Guyana bringing together champion or top teams from five franchise leagues around the world — the Caribbean Premier League, Pakistan Super League, Big Bash League, ILT20, and Major League Cricket — competing for a $1 million prize pool.

thread.previously: We previewed Desert Vipers' bid for their first win of the tournament, against defending champions Guyana Amazon Warriors, who were unbeaten so far.
thread.changed: Guyana won a close chase, 206/8 to Desert Vipers' 205/6, staying unbeaten through two matches while Desert Vipers are now 0-2.

prev_ref.title: Desert Vipers chase their first Global Super League win today against unbeaten defending champions Guyana

stories.title: Barbados prepares mass tribute and state funeral for cricket legend Sir Garfield Sobers on July 29
stories.what_happened: Barbados is finalizing plans for a full state funeral for Sobers on Wednesday, July 29, at 10 a.m. at Kensington Oval — the island's most famous cricket ground. His body will lie in state at Parliament on July 27 and then at Kensington Oval on July 28 so the public can pay respects, before a public thanksgiving service and a private funeral at Coral Ridge Memorial Gardens. Free tickets to attend the Kensington Oval service are being handed out at post offices and government buildings islandwide purely to help organizers estimate the crowd, and condolence books have been placed at multiple sites across Barbados. Prime Minister Mia Mottley has declared a National Day of Mourning, and Barbados's overseas missions are hosting tribute events for the diaspora.
key_points: State funeral set for July 29 at Kensington Oval, Barbados
Body lies in state at Parliament (Jul 27) then Kensington Oval (Jul 28)
Free public tickets being distributed to gauge crowd size
PM Mia Mottley declared a National Day of Mourning

depth.background: Sir Garfield 'Garry' Sobers, widely regarded as cricket's greatest-ever all-rounder, died on July 17, 2026, at his home in Barbados aged 89. He played 93 Tests for the West Indies between 1954 and 1974, scoring 8,032 runs and taking 235 wickets, and as a 21-year-old set what was then the world-record Test score of 365 not out — a mark that stood for 36 years. He also captained the West Indies for seven years and is a Barbadian National Hero.

stories.title: CPL 2026: Trinbago Knight Riders re-sign spinner Usman Tariq, Guyana Amazon Warriors land Glenn Phillips
stories.what_happened: Ahead of CPL 2026, TKR used a Right-to-Match Option to re-sign Pakistani 'mystery spinner' Usman Tariq, who took 20 wickets in 10 matches during their 2025 title run, alongside retaining Sunil Narine, Nicholas Pooran and other key players. Guyana Amazon Warriors (2025 runners-up) signed New Zealand all-rounder Glenn Phillips, who returns to the CPL after a six-year absence, along with Afghanistan's Mohammad Nabi and Rahmanullah Gurbaz, and re-signed veteran South African leg-spinner Imran Tahir as captain. Phillips had missed New Zealand's recent Caribbean ODI series with a side injury suffered while scoring his maiden Test century against England, and his signing signals he's fit again.
key_points: TKR re-signs Pakistan spinner Usman Tariq, their 2025 title-winning top wicket-taker
Guyana Amazon Warriors sign NZ all-rounder Glenn Phillips, returning after 6 years away
CPL 2026 runs Aug 7–Sep 20, now with 7 teams including new side Jamaica Kingsmen
Squads must mix senior West Indies players, overseas stars, and young 'Breakout' talent

depth.background: The Caribbean Premier League (CPL) is the Caribbean's top T20 cricket tournament, drawing international stars alongside West Indies players during the Northern Hemisphere off-season. Ahead of each season, teams retain key players and draft new ones under rules requiring a mix of senior West Indies players, overseas signings, and young 'Breakout' players. Trinbago Knight Riders (TKR), partly owned by Bollywood star Shah Rukh Khan, are the defending 2025 champions.

stories.title: Supreme Court tells CBSE: students can't be forced into the Aadhaar-linked APAAR student ID — a clear opt-out is now mandatory
stories.what_happened: The Supreme Court said it will direct the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) to enforce, nationwide, an Orissa High Court ruling that had already found the APAAR ID must be voluntary. The Court's direction requires CBSE to build an explicit opt-out option into every APAAR consent form and to examine the underlying data-privacy concerns raised by petitioners, who said students were being effectively compelled to enrol because the ID was increasingly demanded during exams and other academic processes.
key_points: Supreme Court says it will direct CBSE to add a clear opt-out option to APAAR consent forms nationwide
APAAR is a 'lifelong' academic ID linked to Aadhaar for every student, launched in 2023
Government called it voluntary, but students say they were pressured to enrol to sit exams
The ruling leans on the 2019 Puttaswamy privacy judgment, which barred mandatory Aadhaar for children

depth.background: APAAR ('Automated Permanent Academic Account Registry') is a Ministry of Education scheme launched in 2023 under the 'One Student, One ID' plan — a single, lifelong academic ID for every student in India, from school through university, linked to their Aadhaar (India's biometric national ID). The government always described enrolment as voluntary. But petitioners argued that in practice, schools and boards were making it a de facto requirement to sit board exams or access other academic services, which they said violated the Supreme Court's landmark 2019 Puttaswamy ruling — the judgment that first established a constitutional right to privacy in India and specifically restricted making Aadhaar mandatory for children's access to education and welfare.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay's plan for direct Cauvery water talks with Karnataka draws backlash, including from DMK's Stalin
stories.what_happened: Tamil Nadu has received only 3.5 TMC (thousand million cubic feet) of Cauvery water since June 1 against an entitlement of 31 TMC under the Supreme Court's release schedule — a severe shortfall for farmers downstream. On July 22, the CWMA declined to order an immediate release and instead referred the matter to the Cauvery Water Regulatory Committee (CWRC), which meets on July 28. In response, new Tamil Nadu CM Vijay proposed holding direct, bilateral talks with Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar, with a visit planned for August 3, to try to resolve the shortfall outside the usual statutory process.
key_points: TN got only 3.5 TMC of water against its 31 TMC entitlement since June 1
New CM Vijay proposes bilateral talks with Karnataka CM, visit set for Aug 3
Farmers' groups, PMK and rival DMK's Stalin all criticize the plan
Statutory water body (CWRC) meets July 28 on a pro-rata sharing formula

depth.background: The Cauvery river flows from Karnataka into Tamil Nadu, and the two states have fought over sharing its water for over a century — it's one of India's most sensitive inter-state disputes because millions of farmers in both states depend on it. The Supreme Court has laid down a fixed release schedule, policed by statutory bodies like the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA), specifically so the states don't have to negotiate the issue from scratch each time there's a shortfall. C. Joseph Vijay, the actor-turned-politician who leads the TVK party, became Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister after his party won the state's 2026 assembly election, unseating the DMK.

stories.title: ED tells court Kerala CM's daughter was paid because of family ties, not real work, in CMRL case
stories.what_happened: The ED told India's Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) Adjudicating Authority that CMRL's former managing director, in a recorded statement, admitted that payments to Veena Vijayan were made because of her relationship with the then-chief minister — not for services rendered. The ED has frozen about ₹29 crore in assets linked to 12 accused individuals and entities, and is now seeking to formally attach Veena Vijayan's properties.
key_points: ED cites ex-CMRL MD's statement: payments to Veena Vijayan were about her father's position
Case centers on ₹2.78 crore paid to Veena's firm, Exalogic, for little apparent service
ED has already frozen roughly ₹29 crore in assets tied to the case
ED is now seeking court attachment of Veena Vijayan's properties

depth.background: The case involves CMRL (Cochin Minerals and Rutile Ltd), a Kerala-based company, and Exalogic Solutions — an IT consultancy owned by Veena Vijayan, daughter of Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan. The Enforcement Directorate (ED), India's financial-crime investigator, has been probing since 2024 whether CMRL's payments to Exalogic were disguised political favors rather than payment for genuine consulting work.

stories.title: 33.84 lakh Haryana voters set to be left off the draft electoral rolls as a contentious nationwide recount rolls on
stories.what_happened: With Haryana's SIR enumeration phase complete, the Election Commission says about 33.84 lakh electors will not appear in the draft electoral roll due for publication on July 31 — because they could not be traced, verified, or did not submit the required enumeration forms during the door-to-door drive. Voters who believe they were wrongly excluded can file claims and objections between July 31 and August 30, before a final roll is published on October 3, 2026.
key_points: Draft electoral rolls for Haryana, due July 31, will exclude about 33.84 lakh (3.38 million) registered electors
The exclusions come from the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), a door-to-door re-verification of every voter
Claims and objections can be filed July 31 to August 30; final rolls come out October 3
The exercise follows a similar, politically explosive SIR drive in Bihar last year

depth.background: The Election Commission of India (ECI) periodically re-verifies voter rolls to remove duplicate, deceased, or shifted voters and register new ones. A Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is a more thorough version of this — booth-level officers go door-to-door to re-confirm every single voter's details, rather than just updating records on request. When the ECI ran an SIR in Bihar in 2025, it became highly controversial: opposition parties alleged it was being used to quietly strike out genuine voters (especially from poorer or minority communities) ahead of elections, while the ECI maintained it was a purely administrative accuracy exercise.

stories.title: Haas boss says an inconsistent car is clouding Ocon's case, as the team weighs its 2027 driver lineup
stories.what_happened: Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu said the team's VF-26 car has been inconsistent enough this season that it's difficult to fairly judge Esteban Ocon's true performance level, even though Ocon has been outqualified by teammate Oliver Bearman 3 times to 11 and trails him 3 points to 18 in the standings. The comments come as Haas ponders its driver lineup for 2027 and as the team gives reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa an FP1 outing in Bearman's car this weekend, ahead of the sport's summer break.
key_points: Team principal Ayao Komatsu says the VF-26's inconsistency makes Esteban Ocon hard to judge fairly
Ocon has been outqualified 3-11 by teammate Oliver Bearman this season, scoring 3 points to Bearman's 18
Haas is weighing whether to keep Ocon or promote Bearman-paired talent for 2027
Comes as Haas hands Bearman's car to reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa for Friday practice this weekend

depth.background: Formula 1 teams typically decide their next season's driver lineup by mid-to-late summer, comparing how each of their two drivers performs in the identical car — since a faster car can flatter a mediocre driver and a difficult car can bury a good one, teams try to judge drivers on how they perform relative to their own teammate, not the raw lap time. Haas's current car is the VF-26.

stories.title: Lovlina Borgohain becomes India's first confirmed medallist at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games
stories.what_happened: Tokyo Olympic bronze medallist Lovlina Borgohain received a direct bye into the women's 75kg boxing semifinal, which under Commonwealth Games rules guarantees her at least a bronze medal — making her India's first confirmed medallist of these Games. Para-powerlifter Jhandu Kumar had already won bronze to close out Day 1, and boxer Jadumani Singh Mandengbam won his men's 55kg bout on points to advance further into the draw.
key_points: Borgohain gets a bye straight into the women's 75kg boxing semifinal — guaranteeing at least bronze
Para-powerlifter Jhandu Kumar also won bronze to close out Day 1
Boxer Jadumani Singh advanced to the men's 55kg pre-quarterfinals
India now has confirmed medals as the Games enter Day 3

depth.background: We previously reported India was opening its medal account at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, with weightlifter Mirabai Chanu chasing a historic third straight gold. Boxing has traditionally been one of India's strongest medal sports at the Commonwealth Games.

thread.previously: We reported India was opening its Commonwealth Games medal account, with Mirabai Chanu chasing a third straight weightlifting gold.
thread.changed: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain has now become India's first confirmed medallist via a semifinal bye, with para-powerlifter Jhandu Kumar also winning bronze.

prev_ref.title: India opens its Commonwealth Games 2026 medal account as Mirabai Chanu chases a historic third gold

stories.title: Welsh Fire Women thump MI London Women by 60 runs in the Hundred
stories.what_happened: At Sophia Gardens in Cardiff, Welsh Fire Women batted first and posted 177 for 4, built on a 49-run opening stand between Georgia Voll and Ella McCaughan before Sophie Devine (52) and Georgia Wareham (43 not out) took over. In reply, MI London Women were restricted to 117, with bowler Lucy Potts taking 3 wickets to break the back of the chase. Welsh Fire won by 60 runs.
key_points: Welsh Fire posted 177/4, their third-highest total in competition history
Sophie Devine (52) and Georgia Wareham (43*) led the batting
MI London were bowled out for just 117 in reply
Backs up a strong turnaround after finishing bottom last season

depth.background: The Hundred is England's short-form franchise cricket tournament — each innings is 100 balls instead of the usual 120 — with men's and women's competitions run side by side since 2021. Welsh Fire's women's team finished with the wooden spoon (last place) last season, so a big win this early in the group stage is a notable turnaround.

stories.title: Oman's Iran shuttle diplomacy pays off — US pauses strikes as talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz advance
stories.what_happened: Iranian and Omani deputy foreign ministers met on Friday and Saturday (July 24-25) to negotiate 'common principles and operational mechanisms' for keeping ships safe as they pass through the Strait of Hormuz and each country's territorial waters. Regional officials say President Trump deliberately paused US airstrikes on Iran during the talks so as not to derail them — the first day in two weeks without a new US strike. Diplomats caution a final deal isn't done yet.
key_points: Omani and Iranian deputy foreign ministers held two days of talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz
The US paused its nightly bombing campaign on Iran for the first time in two weeks
Daily ship crossings through the strait are down 70% — from 45 a day to just 13
A full deal isn't signed yet; diplomats say it needs 'more time'

depth.background: The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow shipping lane between Iran and Oman that roughly a fifth of the world's oil and gas physically passes through — it's the ocean equivalent of a single-lane bridge. In mid-2026 a US-Iran conflict over Iran's nuclear program escalated into direct strikes: the US bombed Iranian targets, Iran fired on tankers and US bases across the Gulf, and a ceasefire/memorandum that had briefly calmed things broke down in mid-July. Oman — a neutral Gulf state with historically good relations with both Washington and Tehran — has repeatedly stepped in as the go-between.

thread.previously: Oman sent a diplomatic delegation to Tehran on July 24 to try to negotiate safe passage for ships through the Strait of Hormuz, after weeks of Iran-US strikes had turned the waterway into a war zone.
thread.changed: The talks have now visibly progressed: Iranian and Omani deputy foreign ministers met on back-to-back days to hash out concrete 'operational mechanisms' for safe shipping, and the US paused its nightly bombing of Iran for the first time in two weeks specifically so as not to disrupt the diplomacy.

prev_ref.title: Oman sends a delegation to Tehran to try to keep ships moving safely through the Strait of Hormuz

stories.title: Carlos Sainz eyes an Audi escape from struggling Williams — but Audi's own drivers say their seats aren't up for grabs
stories.what_happened: With Williams mired in ninth place in the constructors' standings and battling an overweight car under the new 2026 rules, reports say Carlos Sainz is weighing his options for 2027 and has identified Audi as a potential destination. But Audi's current driver Gabriel Bortoleto pushed back on the speculation, saying 'my future with Audi is already decided... I will remain with the team for many years. I have a multi-year contract.' Teammate Nico Hulkenberg has similarly dismissed doubts about his own seat.
key_points: Williams sits ninth in the constructors' championship with an overweight, uncompetitive car
Sainz is reportedly exploring a 2027 move to Audi (Sauber's future factory team)
Audi driver Gabriel Bortoleto says his own seat is locked in for 'many years'
Teammate Nico Hulkenberg has also dismissed doubts about his own future

depth.background: Carlos Sainz, a race-winning veteran previously at Ferrari, joined Williams for the 2026 season hoping to help rebuild the historic team. Formula 1 changed its technical rules for 2026 (new engines and aerodynamics), which reshuffled the competitive order — some teams that were strong under the old rules, like Williams, have struggled to adapt. Audi is entering F1 as a full factory manufacturer team by absorbing the existing Sauber team, a project it has been building toward for several years with heavy investment, currently fielding Bortoleto and Hulkenberg.

stories.title: Bangladesh's parliament speaker set to become acting president as Hasina reveals a December return plan
stories.what_happened: Bangladesh's government reportedly urged Shahabuddin to resign because of his longstanding ties to Hasina, after she signaled she intends to return from exile. Under Bangladesh's constitution, Parliament Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed is expected to take over as acting president until lawmakers elect a successor. Separately, Hasina told Reuters directly that she and senior party colleagues plan to return to Bangladesh and surrender to authorities around December.
key_points: Sources say Shahabuddin was pushed to resign over his old ties to ousted PM Sheikh Hasina
Parliament Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed is constitutionally next in line to become acting president
Hasina told Reuters she plans to return from exile in India and surrender around December
She was sentenced to death in absentia last November over the deadly 2024 protest crackdown

depth.background: Sheikh Hasina fled to India in 2024 after a mass student-led uprising ended her 15-year rule, following a violent crackdown on protesters. An interim government led by Muhammad Yunus has run Bangladesh since, and Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia last November for ordering that crackdown — a charge she denies. President Shahabuddin, a former Hasina ally, had remained in the largely ceremonial presidency throughout the transition.

thread.previously: We reported that President Mohammed Shahabuddin, 76, resigned citing health issues just as pressure was mounting over ousted PM Sheikh Hasina's plans to return to Bangladesh from exile in India.
thread.changed: Reuters sources now say the resignation was really about Shahabuddin's old ties to Hasina, not just health. Parliament Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed is set to become acting president under the constitution, and Hasina herself has told Reuters she plans to return to Bangladesh and surrender to authorities around December.

prev_ref.title: Bangladesh's President Shahabuddin resigns citing health, as pressure grows over Hasina's planned return

stories.title: India eye a T20I series-sealing win in Zimbabwe today, buoyed by Sooryavanshi's record fifty
stories.what_happened: India head into the second T20I of their three-match series against Zimbabwe in Harare today holding a 1-0 series lead, after winning the opener by 7 wickets on the back of Sooryavanshi's record-breaking fifty. A win today would give India an unbeatable 2-0 lead with one match to spare.
key_points: India lead the three-match T20I series 1-0 after a 7-wicket win in the opener
Teenager Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's 19-ball fifty powered that win, a men's T20I record
India can seal the series today with a win in the 2nd T20I at Harare
The series opener had ended a four-month winless run for India in the format

depth.background: India had gone winless in T20Is for four months before this tour, making the series opener's dominant win — and the emergence of 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, fast-tracked into international cricket as part of India's push to blood young talent — a notable turnaround.

thread.previously: We reported India snapped a four-month T20I losing streak by beating Zimbabwe comfortably in the series opener, with 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi smashing a 19-ball fifty to become the youngest player ever to score a men's T20I half-century.
thread.changed: India now play the second T20I in Harare today with a chance to go 2-0 up and seal the three-match series with a game to spare.

prev_ref.title: India end a four-month T20I losing streak with a comfortable win over Zimbabwe

stories.title: Pakistan Women post 273 and push for a series-sealing win over Sri Lanka in the 2nd ODI
stories.what_happened: Pakistan Women won the toss and batted first in the second ODI at Hambantota, posting 273/5. In reply, Sri Lanka Women reached 127/1 by the latest available update, needing 147 more runs to win. The match was still in progress as of this report. Pakistan enter the day already 1-0 up in the three-match series after their opening win.
key_points: Pakistan Women batted first at Hambantota and posted 273/5
Sri Lanka Women were 127/1 in reply, needing 147 more runs at the latest update
A win today would give Pakistan an unassailable 2-0 lead with one match left
Pakistan already lead the series 1-0 after chasing down 211 in the opener

depth.background: This series is part of the ICC Women's Championship, a multi-year league whose results feed directly into qualification for the next ODI Women's Cricket World Cup — so these matches carry weight well beyond the bilateral series itself.

thread.previously: We reported Pakistan Women opened their Sri Lanka tour by chasing down 211 with seven overs to spare, taking a 1-0 lead in the three-match ODI series.
thread.changed: In the second ODI at Hambantota today, Pakistan Women batted first and posted 273/5. As of the latest available update, Sri Lanka Women were 127/1 in reply, needing 147 more runs — with Pakistan well placed to seal the series 2-0 with a match to spare.

prev_ref.title: Pakistan Women chase down Sri Lanka to open their ODI tour with a win

stories.title: Théo Nael wins a chaotic Formula 3 Sprint Race at the Hungarian Grand Prix weekend
stories.what_happened: In the F3 Sprint Race at the Hungarian Grand Prix weekend, reverse-grid pole-sitter Kanato Le lost the lead into the first corner as Gerrard Xie jumped ahead from fourth on the grid. Théo Nael then pushed past both to take the lead and controlled the race from there for a dominant win, with Le and Rivera completing the podium. It followed a qualifying session in which Tuukka Taponen denied Freddie Slater pole position.
key_points: Nael fought through a chaotic start to win the F3 Sprint Race in Hungary
Reverse-grid pole-sitter Kanato Le lost the lead at turn one to Gerrard Xie
Nael then passed both to take the lead and controlled the race from there
Le and Rivera completed the podium; Tuukka Taponen had denied Freddie Slater pole in qualifying

depth.background: Formula 3 is one rung below Formula 2 on the ladder that feeds Formula 1, and races as a support category on Grand Prix weekends — including this one in Hungary. Its Sprint Race uses a partial reverse-grid format, where some of qualifying's top finishers start further back, deliberately mixing up the field to produce closer, more unpredictable racing.

stories.title: UN chief Guterres lands in Damascus — the first visit by a UN Secretary-General since before Syria's civil war
stories.what_happened: António Guterres landed at Damascus International Airport on Saturday, greeted by Syria's foreign minister Asaad al-Shaibani, for a three-day visit running into Monday. He is scheduled to meet President al-Sharaa and senior officials to reaffirm UN support for Syria's transition, address the country's new transitional parliament, meet civil-society and women's-rights groups, and visit the UN force that has monitored the Syria-Israel ceasefire line in the Golan Heights since 1974.
key_points: Guterres arrived in Damascus for a 3-day visit — the first by a UN chief since 2009
He'll meet President Ahmed al-Sharaa, the former rebel leader who took power after Assad fell
Trip includes talks with civil society and a stop at the Golan Heights ceasefire monitors
Comes 18 months after al-Sharaa's government replaced five decades of Assad family rule

depth.background: Syria's civil war began in 2011 and killed hundreds of thousands of people over more than a decade. Bashar al-Assad, whose family had ruled Syria since 1971, was finally overthrown in late 2024 by a rebel coalition led by Ahmed al-Sharaa. Since then Syria has been in a fragile political transition — writing new governing rules, trying to fold former rebel factions into a national army, and seeking the foreign investment and sanctions relief it needs to rebuild. No UN Secretary-General had set foot in the country since Ban Ki-moon in 2009, largely because Assad's government was treated as illegitimate by much of the world during the war.

stories.title: India's Jadumani Singh dominates Scotland's Aaron Cullen 5-0 to reach Commonwealth Games boxing pre-quarterfinals
stories.what_happened: At the SEC Hall in Glasgow, Jadumani Singh Mandengbam dictated the fight from the start against Scotland's Aaron Cullen, dominating with pace, accuracy, and control. All five judges scored it 30-27 in his favour, giving him a clean 5-0 unanimous decision and a place in the Round of 16, where he'll meet Pakistan's Rehman on July 26.
key_points: Jadumani wins the men's 55kg Round of 32 bout 5-0, on identical 30-27 scorecards
All five judges gave Jadumani every round of the fight
He advances to face Pakistan's Rehman in the Round of 16 on July 26
Comes a day after Lovlina Borgohain was already guaranteed a medal via a bye

depth.background: Commonwealth Games boxing is a straight knockout draw — win and advance, lose and you're out. A round of 32 opener is the first hurdle for most boxers, and Indian boxing has historically been one of the country's most reliable sources of Commonwealth Games medals.

stories.title: Lahore Qalandars crush Desert Vipers to complete a perfect start to the Global Super League
stories.what_happened: Lahore Qalandars beat Desert Vipers by 38 runs in Guyana on Thursday, posting 176/4 before bowling Desert Vipers out for 138/9. Leg-spinner Usama Mir took 4/23, while Michael Bracewell's unbeaten 46 off 23 balls earned him Player of the Match. The result gives Qalandars two wins from two games in the league's first-ever season.
key_points: Lahore Qalandars beat Desert Vipers by 38 runs at Providence Stadium, Guyana
Qalandars posted 176/4; Vipers were bowled out for 138/9
Usama Mir took 4/23; Michael Bracewell (46* off 23) was Player of the Match
It's Qalandars' second win in as many games in the brand-new tournament

depth.background: The Global Super League is a brand-new T20 franchise tournament launched this year, bringing together city-franchise teams (several backed by IPL owners) to play in the Caribbean during the traditional cricket off-season. We reported yesterday that Lahore Qalandars were chasing a second straight win to open their campaign.

thread.previously: We reported Lahore Qalandars were chasing a second straight win to open the brand-new Global Super League in Guyana.
thread.changed: They completed it — beating Desert Vipers by 38 runs to go 2-0, with Usama Mir taking 4/23 and Michael Bracewell winning Player of the Match.

stories.title: SpaceX's Starship completes its most successful test yet, deploying 20 next-gen Starlink satellites
stories.what_happened: SpaceX launched Starship's 13th test flight from Starbase, Texas, at 10:51pm UTC on July 24. The Super Heavy booster separated about two minutes into flight and made a controlled splashdown in the Gulf. The Starship upper stage carried 20 next-generation 'V3' Starlink satellites — the first time this Starship version carried a real operational payload — deployed them successfully, and then splashed down under control in the Indian Ocean as planned. SpaceX confirmed it made contact with all 20 satellites afterward.
key_points: Starship's 13th test flight launched from Texas at 10:51pm UTC Friday
The Super Heavy booster made a controlled splashdown in the Gulf
Starship deployed 20 upgraded 'V3' Starlink satellites — its first real payload
The ship itself splashed down under control in the Indian Ocean as planned

depth.background: Starship is SpaceX's giant, fully-reusable next-generation rocket — the vehicle NASA plans to use to land astronauts on the Moon later this decade, and the one SpaceX eventually wants to send to Mars. Earlier test flights had mixed results, including several that ended in explosions, as SpaceX iterates fast and learns from failures in public view rather than testing quietly for years first.

stories.title: Indian sailor killed as a commercial ship is attacked in the Black Sea; India summons Russia's envoy
stories.what_happened: The MV Omorfi came under attack while navigating the Black Sea. Of its ten crew members, three were Indian nationals; one was killed and two survived unharmed. India's Ministry of External Affairs condemned the strike on a civilian commercial vessel and summoned Russia's ambassador to formally protest.
key_points: The MV Omorfi, a Marshall Islands-flagged bulk carrier, was attacked in the Black Sea
One of its three Indian crew members was killed; the other two are reported safe
India's foreign ministry condemned the attack and summoned Russia's top envoy in New Delhi
The attack reportedly happened in or near Russian territorial waters

depth.background: The Russia-Ukraine war has made the Black Sea one of the world's most dangerous shipping lanes, with both sides accused of striking vessels tied to the other. Indian sailors, who crew a large share of the world's commercial shipping fleet, have repeatedly been caught in conflict-zone attacks in recent years — from Houthi strikes on Red Sea tankers to incidents near Iraq — even on ships with no military role.

stories.title: A parasite outbreak tied to Taco Bell lettuce spreads to 9 US states, nearly 2,000 sick
stories.what_happened: The CDC confirmed cyclospora — a parasite that causes long bouts of watery diarrhea, cramping and fatigue — has now sickened 1,947 people who ate at Taco Bell across nine US states (Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, West Virginia, plus newly added Illinois, Kansas, Oklahoma and Pennsylvania). Investigators traced the likely source to iceberg lettuce grown by Taylor Farms de Mexico. Illnesses began June 22 and continued through July 20. It's one of two active cyclospora outbreaks the CDC is tracking; nationally, almost 12,000 cases have been confirmed or are suspected across 41 states this summer, with at least 308 people hospitalized.
key_points: CDC says 1,947 people across 9 states fell ill after eating at Taco Bell
Contaminated iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms de Mexico is the likely source
Illinois, Kansas, Oklahoma and Pennsylvania were just added to the outbreak zone
Nationally, almost 12,000 cases of the same parasite are active across 41 states this summer

depth.background: Cyclospora is a microscopic parasite that lives in contaminated water and spreads when produce like lettuce is irrigated or rinsed with it, then eaten raw. The US sees seasonal outbreaks most summers, usually tied to imported fresh produce, because the parasite doesn't show up in routine food-safety checks and can take weeks to trace back to a single farm.

stories.title: China and Philippines clash for a third time in a week at Scarborough Shoal
stories.what_happened: On July 24-25, China Coast Guard ships repeatedly fired water cannon at Philippine government vessels — including one carrying a CNN crew — that were delivering fuel and food to Filipino fishermen near Scarborough Shoal. The Philippine Coast Guard said a Chinese vessel sprayed the ship BRP Cape San Agustin from close range while being shadowed by at least six Chinese coast guard and militia vessels. It was the third clash in five days, following an earlier incident at Second Thomas Shoal in which Manila said a sailor was struck and injured.
key_points: China Coast Guard fired water cannon at a Philippine vessel near Scarborough Shoal
Third confrontation between the two countries in five days
Comes as ASEAN foreign ministers meet in Manila; China warned of 'bitter consequences'
Beijing says it showed 'restraint'; Manila disputes that account

depth.background: Scarborough Shoal is a fishing ground in the South China Sea that sits within the Philippines' internationally recognized exclusive economic zone but has been under de facto Chinese control since a 2012 standoff. A 2016 international tribunal ruling rejected China's broader claims to the sea, but Beijing has never accepted it.

stories.title: A magnitude-6.0 earthquake rattles Vanuatu — no tsunami threat, but a reminder of the Pacific's most dangerous fault lines
stories.what_happened: A magnitude-6.0 earthquake struck the Coral Sea about 75-82 km southwest of Sola in Vanuatu's Torba Province on the morning of Saturday, July 25 local time (21:37 UTC July 24), at a shallow depth of roughly 45 km. The US Geological Survey and the European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre both recorded the quake; people near the epicenter reported feeling it, but there are no reports so far of significant damage or casualties, and no tsunami warning was issued.
key_points: M6.0 quake struck 75-82km southwest of Sola, Vanuatu, at a shallow depth of about 45km
USGS and regional monitors confirm no tsunami warning or threat
People near the epicenter felt shaking; no major damage or injuries reported so far
Vanuatu sits directly on the Pacific 'Ring of Fire,' one of the world's most earthquake-prone zones

depth.background: Vanuatu is a chain of islands in the South Pacific that sits directly on the boundary where the Australian and Pacific tectonic plates grind past each other — part of the Pacific 'Ring of Fire,' the horseshoe-shaped belt around the Pacific Ocean where most of the world's earthquakes and volcanic eruptions happen. The country experiences frequent, usually minor-to-moderate quakes because of this.

stories.title: Cabinet approves ₹3,030-crore chemical-parks scheme and a rail line doubling to cut India's import dependence
stories.what_happened: The Union Cabinet approved the 'BHAVYA-Rasayan' scheme to set up three chemical parks in India, with an outlay of ₹3,030 crore — ₹3,000 crore for shared infrastructure and utilities inside the parks, and ₹30 crore for administration, running for five years through 2030-31. Separately, the Cabinet cleared ₹1,264 crore to double the railway line between Guntakal and Ballari — adding a third and fourth track over 46km spanning Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, including a major bridge over the Vedavathi River — expected to take three years to complete. Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and PM Modi both said the moves would boost industrial connectivity in the region.
key_points: BHAVYA-Rasayan scheme funds three new chemical parks with ₹3,030 crore, running through 2030-31
₹1,264 crore approved to double (add 3rd/4th tracks) the Guntakal-Ballari rail line — 46km across Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh
Rail project adds capacity for freight and connects ~99 villages with about 7 lakh people
Part of a broader ₹2.19-lakh-crore package of projects the Cabinet has cleared this month, including the Semicon 2.0 chip-manufacturing plan

depth.background: India has been trying to reduce its reliance on imports across strategic industries — chips, chemicals, urea — while also building out infrastructure to support that manufacturing push. Earlier this month the Cabinet approved the ₹1.27-lakh-crore 'Semicon 2.0' semiconductor plan; this week's chemicals and rail approvals are part of the same broader economic push.

stories.title: Union minister Ravneet Bittu resigns from Modi's cabinet as his Rajya Sabha term lapses, eyes a Punjab comeback
stories.what_happened: President Droupadi Murmu accepted Bittu's resignation as Union Minister of State for Railways and Food Processing Industries on July 24, with immediate effect. He steps down because his Rajya Sabha term had already lapsed on June 21 — a minister without a seat in either house of Parliament cannot continue for more than six months, so the resignation formalizes an exit already set in motion.
key_points: President Murmu accepted Bittu's resignation as Minister of State for Railways with immediate effect
He lost his seat because his Rajya Sabha term technically ended June 21
A Congress defector turned BJP MP, he's a three-time Lok Sabha winner who lost his 2024 seat
Seen as gearing up to contest the 2027 Punjab Assembly election

depth.background: Ravneet Singh Bittu, grandson of former Punjab Chief Minister Beant Singh, was a three-time Congress Lok Sabha MP from Punjab before defecting to the BJP in 2024. He lost his own Lok Sabha re-election bid that year but was still made a Union Minister of State (a junior minister rank) and given a seat in the Rajya Sabha (Parliament's upper house, whose members are elected by state legislatures rather than voters directly) to keep him in government despite the electoral loss.

stories.title: Zelensky says Russia has 'readied missiles' for a massive strike within 48 hours, warns of a huge autumn draft
stories.what_happened: President Volodymyr Zelensky said on July 24 that Ukrainian intelligence and Western partners have information that Russia has readied missiles for a fresh massive attack, which could hit within the next 48 hours. He separately said intelligence points to Russia preparing a 'significant' new wave of mobilization for the autumn — Ukraine's Centre for Countering Disinformation has put the expected number at around 500,000 personnel, some to be sent to the front quickly and others trained to potentially open a new front.
key_points: Ukrainian intelligence says Russia has missiles ready for a new mass attack
Strike could land within 48 hours of Zelensky's Friday warning
Russia is reportedly prepping a call-up of ~500,000 more troops for autumn
Comes a day after a Russian missile killed 10 at a Kyiv arms fair

depth.background: Russia has spent the war firing waves of missiles and drones at Ukrainian cities and power infrastructure, timed to maximize damage before Ukraine's air defenses can intercept everything. Ukraine, in turn, has built an intelligence-sharing network with Western partners that often gives Kyiv advance warning of these barrages. Manpower is Russia's other constraint: it relies on periodic mobilization waves, which are politically unpopular at home, to keep replacing soldiers lost at the front.

thread.previously: We reported a Russian ballistic missile strike killed at least 6 people in the Kyiv region, a day after Zelensky had hosted Raytheon (maker of the Patriot air-defense system) to discuss bolstering Ukraine's defenses.
thread.changed: Zelensky is now warning of a far bigger strike — missiles Ukraine says Russia has already 'readied' — within 48 hours, plus intelligence pointing to a major autumn mobilization wave of roughly 500,000 troops.

prev_ref.title: Russian ballistic missile strike kills at least 6 in Kyiv region — a day after Zelenskyy hosted Patriot-maker Raytheon

stories.title: Wall Street's 'Magnificent Seven' shed $797 billion in a day on AI-spending fears — then claw back some ground as a volatile week closes
stories.what_happened: On Thursday, the Magnificent Seven index fell 4.8%, erasing $797 billion in value in a single session as investors reacted to fresh disclosures of surging AI capital expenditure from the group, layered on top of oil near $100 a barrel and war-driven risk aversion. Tesla dropped nearly 15% despite reporting record revenue; Alphabet fell over 7%. The S&P 500 fell 1.2% and the Nasdaq 100 sank 1.9% that day. By Friday's close, the Nasdaq Composite dipped a further 0.64% but the Dow gained 0.46% and the S&P 500 was roughly flat, as the week ended without a full-blown rout.
key_points: The 'Magnificent Seven' megacap tech index fell 4.8% Thursday, its worst one-day drop since April 2025's tariff shock
Tesla plunged nearly 15%, Alphabet fell more than 7%, wiping out $797 billion in combined market value
Trigger: investor worry that Big Tech's ballooning AI spending has an unclear payoff, compounded by the Iran war clouding the macro outlook
Friday: Nasdaq slipped further but the Dow and S&P 500 recovered, closing a rocky week roughly flat

depth.background: The 'Magnificent Seven' — Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Nvidia, Meta and Tesla — have driven most of the US stock market's gains since 2023, largely on excitement about AI. Those same seven companies have also been ploughing hundreds of billions of dollars a year into AI data centers and chips. For most of that run, investors rewarded the spending; lately, they've started asking when — or whether — it turns into profit.

stories.title: Modi government overhauls the NTA and sacks 47 officials as NEET paper-leak protests keep building
stories.what_happened: The Ministry of Education announced sweeping changes to the National Testing Agency (NTA) — the body that conducts NEET and other national exams — at a scheduled 8pm briefing on Friday. The NTA sacked 47 officials as part of the shake-up. A high-level reforms committee will be set up to review the agency's structure, examination process, transparency and data-security protocols, with the government aiming to resolve NTA-related issues within one to two months. The Cabinet is standing behind Pradhan and has ruled out his resignation, while officials say the government is positively considering compensation for the families of students who died by suicide after the leak, and is going easy on peaceful protesters at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.
key_points: Education Ministry announces a major NTA shake-up at 8pm amid student protests
47 National Testing Agency officials sacked
A high-level committee will review NTA's structure, security and transparency
Government rules out minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation but weighs compensation for suicide victims' families

depth.background: The NEET-UG 2026 medical entrance exam paper leak has triggered weeks of student protests, with demonstrators demanding Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, accountability, and ₹1 crore compensation for families of students who died by suicide after the leak. Earlier this week the Union Cabinet approved a tougher anti-paper-leak law with fast-track courts, and Mumbai police banned protests over the leak through August 6 as disruption spread to trains and Parliament.

thread.previously: We reported the Union Cabinet approved a tougher anti-paper-leak law with fast-track courts as protests kept building, a day after Mumbai's trains ground to a halt amid a protest ban tied to the NEET leak.
thread.changed: The government has now gone further than legislation — announcing a full NTA overhaul, sacking 47 officials, and weighing compensation for the families of students who died by suicide.
