stories.title: Netanyahu's toughest challenger yet: ex-army chief Eisenkot now polls ahead of Likud
stories.what_happened: A new Times of Israel/Zman poll puts Yashar at a record 25 Knesset seats, four ahead of Likud — up from a 2-seat lead the week before. A separate Maariv poll conducted July 22–23 has Eisenkot leading Netanyahu 46% to 40% on the question of preferred prime minister. Israel's national election is set for October 27.
key_points: Gadi Eisenkot's new Yashar party has overtaken Netanyahu's Likud in seat projections
One poll gives Yashar a record 25 seats to Likud's low
Eisenkot leads Netanyahu 46%-40% as preferred PM in another poll
Israel votes October 27 — but the opposition still can't form a majority alone

depth.background: Gadi Eisenkot is a former Israeli military chief of staff who lost his son and two nephews fighting in Gaza. He resigned from Netanyahu's war cabinet in 2024, accusing the prime minister of lacking a strategy in Gaza, and has since built a new centrist party, Yashar ('Straight'), positioning himself as the main alternative to Israel's longest-serving prime minister.

stories.title: McLaren brings a new floor to Hungary — but only fits it to Norris' car, leaving Piastri to play catch-up
stories.what_happened: McLaren arrived at the Hungaroring with a new floor and associated components designed to improve the MCL40's performance under braking and through corner entry. The parts were fitted only to Lando Norris' car during Friday practice. Oscar Piastri, meanwhile, had already lost FP1 to a mandatory rookie-driver session for his team and so had only an hour of track time all day — running the previous-specification car. He finished FP2 eighth, over 1.3 seconds off Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and nearly nine tenths behind Norris. Piastri called Friday 'very, very challenging'; both drivers said they wanted to stay cautious about the upgrade's real impact before qualifying.
key_points: McLaren's upgraded floor and related parts fitted only to Norris' car in Friday practice
Piastri also lost FP1 entirely to a mandatory rookie test, leaving him just one hour of running
Piastri finished FP2 eighth, 1.372s off pace-setter Hamilton; Norris was third
Piastri: 'very, very challenging'; both drivers cautious about how much the upgrade actually helps

depth.background: McLaren has led the constructors' championship for most of 2026, with Norris and Piastri as title rivals to each other as much as to Ferrari and Mercedes. Teams often introduce upgrades unevenly across a garage — fitting new parts to one car first to manage risk and understand the change — but doing so right before a race weekend can leave one driver at a real disadvantage.

stories.title: India wins its first medals at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow
stories.what_happened: India collected its first confirmed medals of the Glasgow 2026 Games on day two. Boxer Lovlina Borgohain, an Olympic medallist, advanced straight into the women's 75kg semifinals on a bye and is guaranteed at least bronze under Commonwealth Games boxing rules, which award bronze to both losing semifinalists rather than holding a third-place bout. Separately, Bihar's Jhandu won bronze in men's heavyweight para powerlifting, successfully lifting 181kg and 190kg before narrowly missing a Games record on a 196kg attempt. India finished the day joint-ninth on the overall medal table with one confirmed bronze.
key_points: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain secures at least a bronze in the women's 75kg category
Para-powerlifter Jhandu wins bronze with a 190kg lift in the men's heavyweight event
India stood joint-ninth on the medal table after day two
Games boxing rules award bronze to every losing semifinalist

depth.background: The Commonwealth Games is a multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from Commonwealth nations (mostly former British territories), similar in format to a smaller Olympics. India traditionally performs strongly in shooting, wrestling, boxing, weightlifting and badminton at the Games. The 2026 edition is being held in Glasgow, Scotland.

stories.title: President Murmu makes India's first presidential visit to Romania in three decades, signs three MoUs
stories.what_happened: Murmu visited Bucharest from July 23-25 at the invitation of Romanian President Nicusor Dan, holding talks with Romanian PM Ilie Bolojan on trade, clean energy, connectivity and technology cooperation, and addressing the India-Romania Business Forum. Three MoUs were signed covering science and technology collaboration, sports cooperation, and a new 'Chair of Indian Studies' at the University of Bucharest. The two countries agreed to double bilateral trade within three years, expand cooperation in pharmaceuticals, renewable energy and agriculture, and mark 2028 — the 80th anniversary of diplomatic ties — as an 'India-Romania Year of Innovation.'
key_points: First visit by an Indian head of state to Romania in 30 years
Three MoUs signed: science & tech cooperation, sports, and an Indian Studies chair at the University of Bucharest
India and Romania set a target to double bilateral trade within three years
Comes just after the India-EU Free Trade Agreement, as India courts Central/Eastern European partners

depth.background: President Droupadi Murmu is India's ceremonial head of state. Romania is a NATO and EU member bordering Ukraine and the Black Sea. India has been expanding its diplomatic outreach to the EU following the recent conclusion of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement, a deal cutting tariffs and trade barriers between India and the 27-nation bloc.

stories.title: Aston Martin unveils its biggest 2026 upgrade in Hungary — Alonso gives cautious thumbs-up
stories.what_happened: In Friday practice at the Hungaroring, Aston Martin rolled out a sweeping upgrade package touching almost every part of the AMR26 for both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll — big enough that insiders are calling it a B-spec car. The team flew in spare components to make sure both drivers kept the full package for qualifying and the race. Alonso said the car 'felt good' and that the numbers on track matched what the team predicted beforehand, which he called encouraging both for the rest of this year and for next year's all-new car.
key_points: Aston Martin brought roughly 16 new parts — its largest single upgrade of 2026
Effectively a 'B-spec' car for both Alonso and Stroll
Team flew in spare parts so both cars could run it through the weekend
Alonso: real-world numbers matched simulation, 'very encouraging'

depth.background: Aston Martin started 2026 with high hopes but has slipped down the order, fueling questions about the team's development direction and Fernando Alonso's long-term future there. Under F1's cost cap, teams only get a limited budget for new parts, so a major mid-season overhaul like this is a real gamble on where to spend it.

stories.title: Trump says a 'massive attack' on Iran 'may not be necessary,' floats negotiations as US strikes hit a 13th straight night
stories.what_happened: A day after threatening an unprecedented 'massive attack,' Trump told reporters on Friday afternoon that it 'may not be necessary,' saying Iran wants to negotiate but isn't yet ready to make a deal. Even as he left the door open to talks, US strikes on Iran continued for a 13th straight night, and Iran kept up retaliatory attacks on US-linked targets in the Gulf.
key_points: Trump: the massive strike he threatened a day earlier 'may not be necessary'
Says Iran wants a deal but 'isn't ready' to sign one yet
US bombing campaign continued into a 13th consecutive night
Some Gulf allies reportedly losing patience with the daily escalation

depth.background: The US-Iran war reignited weeks ago after a fragile ceasefire collapsed, and Washington has since carried out nightly strikes on Iranian military and nuclear-linked sites while Iran has hit back at US bases and shipping across the Gulf and Red Sea. On Thursday, Trump said he was 'considering a massive attack, bigger than ever before' and 'close to making a decision,' telling Iran it 'hasn't received enough pain yet.' The US House had already voted a second time, in a rare bipartisan rebuke, to try to end Trump's war powers over the conflict.

thread.previously: On Thursday, Trump said he was considering a 'massive attack, bigger than ever before' on Iran and was 'close to making a decision,' warning Tehran it 'hasn't received enough pain yet.'
thread.changed: By Friday afternoon, Trump softened that to the massive attack 'may not be necessary,' saying Iran wants to negotiate — even as US strikes continued for a 13th straight night and Gulf allies show signs of losing patience.

stories.title: Joe Root reportedly set to return as England's Test captain after Ben Stokes' retirement
stories.what_happened: According to a report from The Athletic, Joe Root is set to be reappointed England's Test captain, with the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) expected to make it official soon. His second stint would begin with the Pakistan series at Headingley on August 19, and he's tipped to continue at least through next summer's Ashes against Australia. Assistant coach Marcus Trescothick is expected to take interim charge of the team for the Pakistan series.
key_points: Report says Root will be reappointed England Test captain, starting the Pakistan series at Headingley on August 19
It would be Root's second stint as captain after he first held the role from 2017-2022
He's expected to stay in charge through the winter tours and into next summer's home Ashes
Marcus Trescothick is set to take interim charge of coaching for the Pakistan series

depth.background: Ben Stokes announced his retirement from international cricket about a month ago, stepping down as England's Test captain, a role he had held since 2022 after taking over from Root. England have needed to name a successor before their next Test assignment, a three-match home series against Pakistan starting in August, and have also been searching for a permanent head coach since Brendon McCullum's departure.

stories.title: India rejects Pakistan's claim it deliberately flooded the Chenab, citing Pakistan's own flood data
stories.what_happened: Pakistani media reports accused India of deliberately releasing water from upstream dams to cause flooding in Pakistan's Punjab province. India's government formally rejected the claim, saying the rise in the Chenab's water level between July 20–23 was 'entirely' the result of heavy monsoon rainfall over Jammu and its catchment areas — and noted that Pakistan's own Flood Forecasting Division in Lahore had already attributed the flooding to the same rainfall before the 'deliberate release' allegation surfaced.
key_points: Pakistani media alleged India deliberately released upstream water to flood Punjab province
India calls the claim 'baseless and technically untenable'
Points out Pakistan's own Lahore flood forecasting office already blamed heavy monsoon rain
India says it remains willing to share flood data with Pakistan 'on humanitarian grounds'

depth.background: India and Pakistan share the Indus river system under the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty, which governs how the two countries use rivers like the Chenab that flow from Indian into Pakistani territory. Water has long been a flashpoint between the two countries, and any suggestion that India is using river flows as a weapon is politically explosive in Pakistan, especially given recent India-Pakistan tensions.

stories.title: Jos Buttler overtakes Chris Gayle for 2nd on cricket's all-time T20 run-scoring list
stories.what_happened: England wicketkeeper-batter Jos Buttler scored 16 off 11 balls, including a four and a six, for Manchester Super Giants against London Spirit in the Hundred at Lord's, taking his career T20 run tally to 14,572 — one more than Chris Gayle's 14,562 — and moving him into 2nd on the all-time list.
key_points: Buttler passed Gayle during a Hundred match at Lord's
His career T20 tally: 14,572 runs, edging past Gayle's 14,562
Kieron Pollard still holds the all-time record, set in June 2026
Buttler needed just a four and a six to get there

depth.background: T20 is cricket's shortest major format — 20 overs (120 balls) a side — and the format behind fast-growing leagues like the IPL and the Hundred. 'Career T20 runs' counts every run a player has scored across all T20 cricket, international and franchise leagues combined. Chris Gayle, nicknamed the 'Universe Boss', was long the format's most prolific run-scorer; Kieron Pollard broke Gayle's record in June 2026 during Major League Cricket.

stories.title: Manchester Super Giants edge London Spirit at Lord's despite a Livingstone masterclass in the Hundred
stories.what_happened: In the men's Hundred opener at Lord's, London Spirit captain Liam Livingstone put in a stand-out all-round performance — scoring 69 off just 40 balls and taking 2 wickets for 14 runs — but it wasn't enough to get his team over the line. Manchester Super Giants got a first-ever Lord's innings of 67 from Tim Seifert, and young bowler Sonny Baker held his nerve to defend just 12 runs in the final five balls and complete the win.
key_points: Liam Livingstone hit 69 off 40 balls and took 2-14, but London Spirit still lost
Tim Seifert made 67 on his first-ever appearance at Lord's for Manchester
Young Sonny Baker defended just 12 runs in the final over to seal it
This is the men's opener at Lord's — separate from the earlier women's fixture there

depth.background: The Hundred is English cricket's 100-balls-per-innings franchise tournament, running men's and women's competitions in parallel each summer at the same host grounds, including the historic Lord's ground in London. London Spirit and Manchester Super Giants are two of the eight franchise teams.

stories.title: Oil rockets past $100 a barrel after Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers, then eases back — why the Middle East keeps moving crude prices
stories.what_happened: Houthi militants struck two Saudi Arabian oil tankers in the Red Sea, setting one ablaze while the crew was reported safe. The attack, alongside a separate strike disrupting Kazakhstan's Caspian Pipeline exports, pushed Brent crude above $100 a barrel — a level not seen since May and roughly 40% higher than a month earlier. Several Saudi tankers reportedly reversed course in the Red Sea after the Houthis declared a maritime blockade on Saudi ports. Prices have since eased to around $97–98 a barrel as of July 24.
key_points: Iran-backed Houthi rebels attacked two Saudi Arabian oil tankers (Encelia and Layla) in the Red Sea; one caught fire, crew were unharmed
Brent crude — the global oil benchmark — jumped above $100 a barrel for the first time since May, before easing to around $97–98
Separately, Kazakhstan lost roughly 80% of its oil exports after tanker attacks forced a halt to loadings at its Caspian Pipeline terminal
Goldman Sachs warns Brent could climb past $120 a barrel by year-end if the disruptions continue

depth.background: The Houthis are an Iran-aligned armed group controlling much of Yemen; they've intermittently attacked Red Sea shipping for a couple of years, usually tied to the Israel-Gaza war, but these strikes specifically targeted Saudi Arabia's own tankers. The Red Sea and the nearby Strait of Hormuz sit on some of the world's most important oil-shipping routes, so any threat there worries energy markets even before any oil is actually lost.

stories.title: Paramount agrees to delay its Warner Bros. Discovery buyout until mid-2027 as state lawsuits threaten to kill the deal
stories.what_happened: Paramount said in a Friday afternoon court filing that it will not complete the merger until either an antitrust trial takes place or June 1, 2027, whichever is sooner. This came just days after a federal judge had already ordered the two companies to pause the deal for at least two weeks while a legal challenge from a coalition of state attorneys general plays out. The Writers Guild of America filed its own separate lawsuit making similar antitrust arguments.
key_points: Paramount won't close the Warner Bros. Discovery deal until a court rules on an antitrust challenge, or June 1, 2027 — whichever comes first
A federal judge had already ordered a 2-week halt to the merger earlier in the week
12 state attorneys general, led by California's Rob Bonta, are suing to block it outright
The Writers Guild of America filed a separate suit, saying the merger would mean lower pay and fewer jobs for writers

depth.background: Paramount (owner of CBS and Paramount Pictures) agreed to buy Warner Bros. Discovery (owner of HBO, CNN, and Warner Bros. studios) in one of the largest media mergers in Hollywood history — combining two major studios, two streaming services, and a stack of TV networks into one company. Big mergers like this need antitrust approval because regulators worry about one company controlling too much of an industry, which can mean higher prices and fewer choices for consumers.

stories.title: FIA lets Verstappen off, warns Sainz, after their tense Hungarian GP practice near-miss
stories.what_happened: The stewards ruled that Sainz had positioned himself on the racing line to deliberately warm up his brakes, without radio contact with his team after a cable came loose — so he never heard warnings that Verstappen was approaching on a fast lap. They accepted that explanation but still judged Sainz should not have been on the racing line without communication, issuing him a warning. Verstappen was found to have taken no action that further endangered anyone, and the stewards closed the case against him with no penalty.
key_points: Stewards ruled Verstappen faces no further action over the Turn 12 incident
Sainz gets a formal warning instead, despite explaining a radio failure
Sainz's race engineer's warnings about Verstappen never reached him — his radio cable was loose
Stewards said Sainz shouldn't have been on the racing line warming his brakes without radio contact

depth.background: In Friday's first practice session for the Hungarian Grand Prix, Max Verstappen came upon a slow-moving Carlos Sainz on the approach to Turn 12 while on a fast lap, and appeared to react by briefly slowing on the corner exit — holding up both Sainz and Gabriel Bortoleto's Audi behind him. The FIA stewards summoned both drivers to explain themselves, opening a formal investigation into the incident.

thread.previously: Stewards opened a formal investigation Friday after Verstappen appeared to slow deliberately in front of Sainz near Turn 12 during FP1.
thread.changed: The verdict is in: Verstappen faces no penalty at all, while Sainz gets a warning for being on the racing line without radio contact with his team.

prev_ref.title: Stewards summon Carlos Sainz and Max Verstappen after a tense traffic incident in Hungarian GP practice

stories.title: Adrian Newey tells Christian Horner: Aston Martin is 'very happy' with its current management, dodging renewed return rumours
stories.what_happened: Asked directly about the renewed Horner-to-Aston-Martin rumours, Newey said 'I keep hearing these rumours about Christian' but added he 'can't comment further' and that the team is 'very happy' with 'the personnel we have at AMR.' Aston Martin owner Lawrence Stroll has previously stated Horner will not be joining the team in any capacity, and earlier reports this year suggested Newey himself had blocked an earlier attempt to bring Horner in.
key_points: Newey says Aston Martin is 'very happy' with its senior management team
Comes amid fresh rumours linking former Red Bull boss Christian Horner to an Aston Martin role
Horner was ousted from Red Bull about a year ago and remains free to work in F1
Newey previously worked with Horner for two decades at Red Bull before an acrimonious split

depth.background: Christian Horner ran Red Bull's F1 team for nearly two decades before being removed roughly a year ago following controversy, including accusations of controlling behaviour toward a female colleague. Since then he has repeatedly been linked with a return to the sport, most persistently with Aston Martin — a team owned by billionaire Lawrence Stroll that has been aggressively spending to catch the front-runners. Adrian Newey, F1's most decorated car designer, left Red Bull in the wake of the Horner controversy and now leads Aston Martin's technical operation.

stories.title: Europe's wildfires explode: 200,000+ flee France and Spain as Madrid declares its first national emergency
stories.what_happened: The fires tore out of control on Friday. In France, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 40,000 people were evacuated from the Gironde department and 23,000 from Landes, with authorities ordering a total evacuation of the Cap Ferret peninsula, a coastal tourist area. President Emmanuel Macron ordered the military to mobilize as the fires threatened villages and approached Bordeaux. In Spain, the government declared a national wildfire emergency for the first time, with roughly 60,000 people evacuated or told to shelter indoors around Madrid and Ávila. Total evacuations across both countries topped 200,000, with some residents escaping by boat.
key_points: Evacuations jump from 44,000 to over 200,000 people in a day
Spain declares a national wildfire emergency for the first time ever
Macron orders the French military to mobilize as fires near Bordeaux
Croatia, Portugal, Czechia, Slovakia, Italy and Greece are all sending aircraft and crews

depth.background: Southwestern France and central Spain have been battling wildfires for about a week amid an intense heatwave, with a story yesterday putting the evacuation count at roughly 44,000 people as the EU sent in firefighting planes under its joint disaster-response mechanism. Spain's largest active fire, near Guadalajara north of Madrid, had already burned about 32,000 hectares over the prior week.

thread.previously: We reported roughly 44,000 people had fled wildfires in France and Spain as the EU rushed in firefighting planes.
thread.changed: The evacuation count has jumped past 200,000, Spain has declared its first-ever national wildfire emergency, and Macron has mobilized the French military as fires approach Bordeaux.

prev_ref.title: Wildfires force 44,000 to flee in France and Spain as the EU rushes in firefighting planes

stories.title: F1 design legend Adrian Newey says his overhauled Aston Martin has found 'seconds' of pace
stories.what_happened: Newey said Friday that Aston Martin's newly introduced upgrade package for the Hungarian Grand Prix has found 'seconds' worth of lap time, a major step after what he described as a 'complete nightmare' start to the season. Fernando Alonso set the 13th fastest time in Friday's second practice session, closing a gap that had been as wide as four seconds to the front of the field earlier in 2026. Newey said it is 'very early days' in understanding the new package, with further upgrades planned for the Monza and Baku races, and said he expects Alonso — who has been the subject of retirement speculation — to remain with the team.
key_points: Newey says the AMR26's big Hungary upgrade has 'unlocked seconds' of lap time
Fernando Alonso set 13th fastest in Friday practice — a big step up from a 4-second gap earlier this season
Newey calls the season so far 'a complete nightmare' but sounds optimistic now
He expects double champion Alonso to stay at Aston Martin

depth.background: Adrian Newey is one of the most successful car designers in F1 history, behind championship-winning cars at Williams, McLaren and Red Bull; he joined Aston Martin in 2025 to help turn around a team that has struggled for competitiveness. Aston Martin has trailed the F1 field for most of 2026, prompting persistent doubts about the team's project and speculation over Alonso's future.

stories.title: Lahore Qalandars chase a second straight win as the brand-new Global Super League gets going in Guyana
stories.what_happened: In the tournament's third match, Lahore Qalandars batted first at Providence Stadium in Guyana and posted 176/4 in their 20 overs. Desert Vipers, chasing, were 121/7 after 17.3 overs when the match was last updated. Qalandars arrive with momentum after beating Perth Scorchers by 16 runs in the tournament opener, while Desert Vipers — led by Pakistan's Shadab Khan and featuring South African hitters Rilee Rossouw and Andries Gous — are playing their first game of the competition.
key_points: Lahore Qalandars posted 176/4 batting first against Desert Vipers in Providence, Guyana
It's only the tournament's 3rd-ever match — the Global Super League (GSL) launched this year
Qalandars opened their campaign with a 16-run win over Perth Scorchers
Desert Vipers, led by Shadab Khan, field a star-studded squad including Rilee Rossouw

depth.background: The Global Super League is a brand-new T20 franchise tournament launched in 2026, joining an already crowded calendar of T20 leagues (IPL, The Hundred, PSL and more). It brings together franchise teams with roots in different established leagues — Lahore Qalandars from Pakistan's PSL, Perth Scorchers from Australia's Big Bash, and Desert Vipers from the UAE's ILT20 — to play each other in a new, standalone competition based in the Caribbean.

stories.title: Modi's Cabinet approves ₹3,030 crore scheme to build three new chemical parks
stories.what_happened: The Union Cabinet on Friday approved the Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana — Rasayan (BHAVYA) scheme, allocating ₹3,030 crore to build three chemical parks between FY 2026-27 and FY 2030-31. Of that, ₹3,000 crore covers common infrastructure and utilities inside the parks, with ₹30 crore for administration. The Centre will grant up to ₹1,000 crore per park, conditional on the relevant state government putting in at least ₹500 crore. Each park must have a minimum contiguous, encumbrance-free area of 8 sq km (about 2,000 acres). Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced the decision after the Cabinet meeting.
key_points: The 'BHAVYA' Rasayan scheme funds three dedicated chemical parks across five years
Centre gives up to ₹1,000 crore per park; states must chip in at least ₹500 crore each
Each park needs a minimum of 2,000 acres of encumbrance-free land
Parks offer 'plug-and-play' infrastructure so chemical companies can set up faster

depth.background: India's chemical industry is a major manufacturing sector but has long complained about the time and cost of building basic infrastructure — land, power, water, effluent treatment — before a single factory can even start construction. Dedicated industrial parks, where the government builds that shared infrastructure upfront, are meant to remove that bottleneck, the same model India has used for textile and pharma parks.

stories.title: Intel blows past earnings estimates — and its stock falls anyway, as the chip-stock rally cracks
stories.what_happened: Intel reported Q2 2026 results after markets closed Thursday that beat Wall Street on every major line: adjusted profit of 42 cents a share against an expected 21 cents, and $16.1 billion in revenue against an expected $14.42 billion. Gross margin, the share of revenue left after production costs, recovered to 42% from a razor-thin 2.5% a year earlier, which Intel credited to selling more, higher-margin chips at greater scale. Despite that, the stock climbed only briefly after the report before falling through Friday's trading, down roughly 4% on the day and about 28% for the month.
key_points: Intel posted adjusted EPS of $0.42 vs $0.21 expected, and revenue of $16.1 billion vs $14.42 billion expected
Revenue grew 25% — Intel's fastest growth in almost 15 years — and gross margin jumped to 42% from just 2.5% a year ago
Shares still fell through Friday's session, extending a 28% slide this month that makes Intel one of the S&P 500's worst July performers
Broadcom and AMD also slipped, and the semiconductor ETF (SMH) pulled back, as investors rotate out of this year's AI-chip winners

depth.background: Intel has spent the last two years trying to convince investors it can rebuild after losing ground to Nvidia and AMD in the AI-chip race, while also fixing its own manufacturing business. Its stock had rocketed 278% in the first half of 2026 on hopes that AI-driven server-chip demand would keep growing and that its factories were finally turning a corner. That made the stock unusually vulnerable: after a run that big, even genuinely good news can disappoint if it doesn't clear an even higher bar the market had already set.

stories.title: Sonam Wangchuk ends his 26-day hunger strike after government intervention, vows to keep fighting for Ladakh statehood
stories.what_happened: Wangchuk began his hunger strike in early July 2026 to press the central government on Ladakh's status. After 26 days, he ended the fast on Friday, July 24, in the presence of Union Ministers Jitendra Singh and JP Nadda, doctors, family, and supporters, following what he described as extended negotiations. He said dozens of members of parliament from different parties had appealed to him to stop, and he promised to detail the conditions of his decision in a video soon.
key_points: Climate activist and engineer Sonam Wangchuk broke his 26-day fast on Friday
Two Union ministers, doctors, and his family were present as he ended it
He was fasting to demand statehood and constitutional protections for Ladakh
He says the fight for those protections continues despite ending the fast

depth.background: Ladakh became a Union Territory directly ruled by the central government in 2019, when the government revoked Jammu and Kashmir's special status and split the region. Unlike a full state, a Union Territory has far less local self-government and weaker legal protection for land and local jobs. Wangchuk — the engineer-educator whose real-life work inspired a Bollywood film — has spent years campaigning for Ladakh to get statehood, or at least 'Sixth Schedule' protections, a constitutional provision that gives tribal-majority regions like parts of India's northeast strong control over their own land and resources so it can't be bought up or industrialized by outsiders.

stories.title: Verstappen throws a towel from his cockpit mid-practice — and Red Bull gets an FIA warning for it
stories.what_happened: During second practice, Red Bull's mechanics left a rag inside Verstappen's car after making setup changes. Once on track between Turns 3 and 4, Verstappen threw the towel out of the cockpit, explaining afterward to stewards that he judged it safer to discard it there than risk it interfering with his pedals on the drive back to the pits. The FIA investigated Red Bull for an alleged breach of the rule against releasing a car in an unsafe condition, and ultimately issued the team a warning rather than a harsher penalty.
key_points: Verstappen tossed a white rag/towel out of his Red Bull on track during FP2
Team had left it in the car after a setup change; Verstappen says removing it was the safer option
FIA investigated Red Bull for releasing the car in an unsafe condition, then issued a warning
A quirky but real regulatory footnote during an already tense practice day for Red Bull

depth.background: F1's sporting regulations (specifically Article 34.14(c)) require teams to send cars out of the pits in a safe condition — covering everything from wheel nuts to loose objects that could interfere with the driver or fall onto the track. Red Bull has already had a difficult run of practice sessions this season, including known reliability and setup issues, and Verstappen himself has been dealing with a car whose rear wing was flagged as 'super dangerous' earlier this year after causing two of his crashes.

stories.title: Trump says he's 'close to' ordering a 'massive attack' on Iran — bigger than any strike so far
stories.what_happened: In an interview with Axios published July 24, President Trump said he is 'close to making a decision' on a new, larger campaign against Iran, saying Tehran 'hasn't received enough pain yet.' He said any new operation would be bigger than Operation Epic Fury and that Israel 'would join in two minutes' if asked. The comments come as the US confirms a 13th consecutive night of strikes on Iran, with Tehran having rejected an Iraq-brokered ceasefire proposal.
key_points: Trump tells Axios he's considering an attack 'bigger than ever before'
Would eclipse Operation Epic Fury, the Feb-April 2026 campaign
Comes amid a 13th straight night of US strikes on Iran
Sticking point remains who controls the Strait of Hormuz

depth.background: The US and Israel have been at war with Iran since early 2026, when Iran's nuclear and missile programs triggered a first round of strikes known as Operation Epic Fury. A June 17 memorandum of understanding was meant to wind the conflict down, but it left the fate of the Strait of Hormuz — the narrow waterway roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes through — unresolved, and fighting has continued in fits and starts since.

thread.previously: This week, Trump said the US would destroy one Iranian bridge or power plant every time Iran fired on a ship in the Strait of Hormuz — a fixed, automatic retaliation policy tied to Hormuz incidents.
thread.changed: Trump has now gone further, telling Axios he's 'close to' ordering one much larger 'massive attack' on Iran — not tit-for-tat strikes tied to Hormuz incidents, but a single campaign he says would be bigger than the earlier Operation Epic Fury.

prev_ref.title: Trump vows to bomb an Iranian bridge or power plant every time Iran fires on a ship in the Strait of Hormuz

stories.title: Lewis Hamilton and Ferrari crush Mercedes in Hungarian GP practice, boosting his title hopes
stories.what_happened: In Friday's second practice session at the Hungaroring, Hamilton set the fastest lap at 1:18.729s, half a second clear of McLaren's Norris and 0.148s ahead of Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc. Mercedes' George Russell was almost a second slower in fifth — a striking gap for the team that has won the most races this season. Hamilton said afterwards he 'really believes' he can still fight for the title, while admitting he needs to 'step it up.'
key_points: Hamilton topped FP2 with Leclerc 0.148s behind — a Ferrari one-two
Mercedes' George Russell was nearly a full second off Hamilton's pace, down in 5th
McLaren's Lando Norris was third, half a second back
Hamilton trails championship leader Kimi Antonelli by 45 points going into this weekend

depth.background: Lewis Hamilton joined Ferrari after a difficult first season adjusting to the team, while Mercedes — now led on-track by 18-year-old rookie Kimi Antonelli — has been the car to beat for most of 2026. This is the last race before Formula 1's summer break, so every team wants to head into the shutdown with momentum.

stories.title: Supreme Court bars anyone from posting or monetizing courtroom video clips without official permission
stories.what_happened: A three-judge bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, along with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana, passed an interim order stating there shall be no extraction, editing, dissemination, posting, reposting, uploading, or monetization of audio-video recordings of court proceedings on social media or any digital platform without prior permission from the Secretary General of the Supreme Court or the Registrar General of the relevant High Court. The bench also asked High Courts to report back on what rules they already have for regulating livestreamed hearings. The Court clarified this does not restrict ordinary news reporting.
key_points: Interim order bans posting, editing, or monetizing live-streamed court footage on social media
Prior permission is now needed from the Supreme Court's Secretary General or the relevant High Court's Registrar General
Order came on a plea by journalist Harshita Grover over misuse of court livestreams
News reporting of court proceedings is explicitly NOT affected

depth.background: India began live-streaming select Supreme Court and High Court hearings in recent years to boost transparency. But that footage has increasingly been clipped, edited out of context, and reposted on YouTube and social media — sometimes to sensationalize exchanges between judges and lawyers, or to monetize clips through ad revenue. A journalist, Harshita Grover, filed a public interest litigation asking the Court to set clear rules for how livestreamed proceedings can be used.

stories.title: Wall Street shrugs off Iran-war oil jitters as blockbuster earnings offset a chip-stock slide
stories.what_happened: US stocks closed a mixed but resilient session on Friday. The S&P 500 — a basket of America's 500 largest public companies and the market's main health gauge — edged up just 0.05% to 7,411.98. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which tracks 30 big industrial and blue-chip firms, gained 235.60 points (0.46%) to a record 51,947.25. The Nasdaq Composite, heavy with tech and chip stocks, fell 0.64% to 24,975.82. Investors were weighing a stronger-than-expected start to second-quarter earnings season against oil prices surging past $100 a barrel after Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers widened the Iran war's reach.
key_points: S&P 500 ended nearly flat Friday at 7,411.98; the Dow rose 235 points to a record 51,947.25
The Nasdaq fell 0.64% to 24,975.82, dragged down by chip stocks
Q2 corporate earnings are beating Wall Street forecasts by a wide margin so far
Oil's surge past $100 a barrel on the Iran war is the main headwind investors are weighing

depth.background: Every stock's price reflects two competing forces right now: how much money companies are actually making (strong this earnings season) and how worried investors are about the Middle East war disrupting oil supply and the wider economy. When the two pull in opposite directions, as they did Friday, the market can end up barely moving even though a lot happened underneath.

stories.title: Franco Colapinto's Alpine slams the barriers backwards, red-flagging Hungarian GP practice
stories.what_happened: Colapinto lost the rear of his Alpine at the final corner of the Hungaroring during FP2, spinning and hitting the barriers backwards, which tore off the back of the car. He had actually been setting personal-best times in the first two sectors before losing control, with officials pointing to strong gusts of wind combining with a dusty, low-grip track surface. The session was red-flagged just before its halfway point and resumed with 26 minutes remaining, as a queue of cars rushed out to complete their qualifying-simulation runs on soft tyres before time ran out.
key_points: Colapinto spun and hit the barriers rear-first at the final corner during FP2
The crash destroyed the back of his car and stopped the session with a red flag
Gusty wind and a dusty, low-grip track surface were behind the loss of control
The session resumed with 26 minutes left, disrupting cars' qualifying-simulation runs

depth.background: Franco Colapinto is a 23-year-old Argentine driving for Alpine, a team that has struggled for competitiveness this season. Friday practice sessions are when teams and rookies fine-tune their cars for qualifying, and losing running time to a red flag is especially costly for a struggling team trying to close the gap to rivals.

stories.title: Sensex and Nifty slide to a one-month low as surging oil prices squeeze Indian stocks
stories.what_happened: India's benchmark stock indices fell on Friday, July 24, with the Sensex down 332 points (0.43%) to 76,060 and the Nifty 50 down about 0.4% to 23,770 — both one-month lows. The decline tracked a sharp rise in crude oil prices driven by escalating Middle East tensions, which pushes up India's import costs and pressures the rupee. Bajaj Finance and Mahindra & Mahindra were among the top losers; HCL Tech, ITC and Reliance Industries bucked the trend.
key_points: India's Sensex fell 332 points (0.43%) to close at 76,060; the Nifty 50 fell about 0.4% to 23,770 — both their lowest in over a month
The trigger: crude oil jumping on Middle East tensions (Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers, US-Iran strikes), which raises India's oil-import bill and pressures the rupee
Bajaj Finance and Mahindra & Mahindra led the losses; HCL Tech, ITC and Reliance Industries were among the few gainers

depth.background: India imports the vast majority of the crude oil it uses, so global oil-price spikes hit it harder than most large economies — both by raising fuel and import costs directly, and by weakening the rupee, since India has to spend more dollars buying the same amount of oil. Indian stocks, especially import-heavy and rate-sensitive sectors, tend to wobble when oil jumps.

stories.title: Sensex falls for a 5th straight session as oil nears $100 and the rupee stays pinned near record lows
stories.what_happened: India's benchmark indices fell for a fifth straight session on July 24 — the Sensex closing at 76,059.77 (down 0.43%) and the Nifty at 23,767.45 (down 0.43%) — as Brent crude oil climbed toward $96–100 a barrel on fears that the Iran war could disrupt Middle East shipping lanes. The rupee stayed pinned near record lows against the dollar. Auto, metal and energy stocks — the sectors most exposed to oil costs — led the declines, while IT and media stocks were relative gainers.
key_points: Sensex closed at 76,059.77, down 331.62 points — its fifth consecutive losing day
Nifty fell to 23,767.45, down 102.15 points
Brent crude oil pushed toward $100 a barrel on Iran-war shipping fears
Auto, metal and energy stocks led the losses; IT and media stocks held up better

depth.background: Indian markets import most of their oil, so a rising crude price directly squeezes companies' fuel costs and India's trade balance, and it tends to weaken the rupee as more dollars flow out to pay for oil. This selloff comes on top of an already-tense global backdrop: the Iran war has raised fears that a key Middle East shipping route could be disrupted, and foreign investors have been pulling money out of Indian stocks (FII selling) as global risk appetite has soured.

stories.title: Hindustan Zinc's profit more than doubles on record zinc and silver prices
stories.what_happened: For the April-June 2026 quarter (Q1 of FY27, India's financial year running April-March), Hindustan Zinc reported consolidated net profit of ₹5,469 crore, up 144.81% from ₹2,234 crore a year earlier, on revenue up roughly 72% to about ₹13,033 crore. CEO Arun Misra said the company delivered its highest-ever first-quarter mined metal production of 268 KT (thousand tonnes) for the fifth straight year, crediting cost discipline and strong global zinc and silver prices even as production volumes typically dip in this quarter for seasonal reasons.
key_points: Q1 FY27 net profit up 144.81% year-on-year to ₹5,469 crore
Revenue rose about 72% to ₹13,033 crore on higher metal prices
Highest-ever first-quarter mined metal output: 268,000 tonnes, 5th year running
Result beats Street expectations of a strong but smaller jump

depth.background: Hindustan Zinc is the world's second-largest integrated zinc-lead-silver producer, mining and smelting in Rajasthan. It was privatised in stages from 2002, with Vedanta Ltd now the majority owner and the Indian government still holding a roughly 29.5% stake, so results also matter for public dividend income.

stories.title: Nifty closes below 24,000 for the first time in weeks, as US strikes on Iran push oil higher and foreign investors keep selling
stories.what_happened: On Friday, the Sensex closed at 76,391.39, down 0.47%, while the Nifty fell 0.53% to 23,869.60 — slipping below the psychologically important 24,000 level. Rising crude oil prices, persistent FII selling, a weaker rupee, and continued West Asia tensions all weighed on sentiment, extending a losing run that started earlier in the week as US airstrikes on Iran continued.
key_points: Sensex closed at 76,391.39 (down 0.47%); Nifty at 23,869.60 (down 0.53%) — below 24,000
Extended the week's losing streak, driven by rising crude, a weaker rupee, and FII selling
US strikes on Iran and Strait of Hormuz tensions are keeping oil prices elevated
Oil-import-dependent India is especially exposed to this kind of Gulf-driven price shock

depth.background: The Sensex (30 large companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange) and the Nifty (50 large companies on the National Stock Exchange) are India's two headline stock market gauges. Indian markets had already been sliding through the week as the US-Iran conflict escalated and crude oil pushed past $100 a barrel for the first time since May. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) — overseas funds that buy and sell large blocks of Indian shares — had already been pulling money out, adding to the pressure.

thread.previously: Sensex and Nifty had fallen for a fourth straight session as Gulf tensions pushed oil prices higher, with persistent FII selling and a weak rupee adding to the pressure.
thread.changed: The slide continued into Friday's close, with the Nifty dropping below the psychologically important 24,000 level for the first time in weeks (23,869.60, -0.53%) and the Sensex closing at 76,391.39 (-0.47%), as the US-Iran conflict escalated further and crude climbed higher still.

prev_ref.title: Sensex and Nifty fall for a fourth straight day as Gulf tensions push oil prices higher

stories.title: Lando Norris tops both Hungarian GP practice sessions as McLaren dominates Friday
stories.what_happened: In first practice on Friday, Norris set the fastest lap, just 0.019 seconds quicker than Piastri, with the pair well clear of the rest of the field. In second practice later the same day, Norris again beat Piastri, this time by a bigger 0.291-second margin, with a best lap of 1:15.624. McLaren finished both sessions in a clean one-two.
key_points: Norris fastest in FP1 by 0.019s, then FP2 by 0.291s — both ahead of teammate Piastri
McLaren looks like the car to beat heading into Saturday qualifying at the Hungaroring
Comes right after Mercedes' Antonelli extended his championship lead with a Spa win
Sets up a genuine three-way fight (McLaren, Mercedes, Ferrari) for Hungary's race pace

depth.background: The Hungaroring is a tight, twisty circuit that rewards a car with strong aerodynamic grip through slow-to-medium corners rather than raw straight-line speed, which historically suits different cars than power-hungry tracks like Spa or Monza. McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri have been in a close intra-team fight for form all season, while Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli arrives in Budapest fresh off winning at Spa-Francorchamps to extend his championship lead.

stories.title: Government tells NEET protesters Education Minister Pradhan will not resign, sets Saturday deadline for a final word
stories.what_happened: On Friday, July 24, Union Ministers J.P. Nadda and Jitendra Singh held a nearly two-hour second round of talks with CJP spokespersons at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. Nadda said CJP presented '3 main demands and 5 suggestions.' Government sources said the Centre has agreed in principle to two of the three demands — ₹1 crore compensation for the families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide, and withdrawing legal cases against protesters — but on CJP's core demand that Pradhan resign, the government says there is 'no question' of that happening, arguing 'resignation equates to running away.' The government asked for time until Saturday afternoon to give a final answer. This followed the sacking of 47 National Testing Agency (NTA) officials on Friday, including its former Director-General, as part of a broader shake-up.
key_points: Govt agrees in principle to ₹1 crore compensation for NEET aspirants who died by suicide, and dropping cases against protesters
But it flatly rules out Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation — the protest group CJP's central demand
47 NTA officials were sacked Friday, including the former Director-General, as part of the exam body's overhaul
Government has set itself a Saturday deadline to give its final answer on the resignation demand

depth.background: NEET-UG is India's single national entrance exam for medical college admission, taken by about 2 million students every year. A leaked question paper before the May 3, 2026 exam triggered a month-long protest movement led by a youth group called CJP, later joined by veteran activist Sonam Wangchuk, who began a hunger strike. Congress had used the scandal to demand the resignations of both Home Minister Amit Shah and Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, repeatedly disrupting Parliament over it.

thread.previously: Congress had repeatedly disrupted Parliament demanding Home Minister Amit Shah and Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resign over the police crackdown on NEET paper-leak protesters.
thread.changed: The government held direct talks with the CJP protest group, agreed in principle to compensation and dropping legal cases, but explicitly ruled out Pradhan's resignation — setting itself a Saturday deadline to give a final answer.

stories.title: FIA clears Verstappen, warns Sainz over their Hungarian GP practice incident
stories.what_happened: The stewards ruled Sainz should not have been braking on the racing line as Verstappen closed in on a push lap, and issued him a warning. They accepted Sainz's explanation that a disconnected radio cable meant he didn't hear his engineer's repeated warnings that Verstappen was approaching. Verstappen, despite an angry in-the-moment radio message saying Sainz 'even slammed on the brakes,' told stewards he wasn't endangered and didn't consider the incident dangerous — so he was cleared with no action taken.
key_points: Stewards take 'no further action' against Verstappen
Sainz gets a warning for braking on the racing line
Sainz says a disconnected radio cable meant he missed his engineer's warnings
Verstappen said the incident wasn't dangerous despite an angry radio message

depth.background: Verstappen and Williams driver Carlos Sainz were summoned to the stewards after a tense moment during Friday's first practice session at the Hungarian Grand Prix, when Sainz was on the racing line as Verstappen approached on a fast lap.

thread.previously: We reported that stewards had summoned Carlos Sainz and Max Verstappen after a tense traffic incident during Hungarian GP practice.
thread.changed: The stewards have now ruled: Sainz gets a warning, Verstappen is cleared with no action taken.

prev_ref.title: Stewards summon Carlos Sainz and Max Verstappen after a tense traffic incident in Hungarian GP practice

stories.title: Guyana Amazon Warriors edge San Francisco Unicorns by 3 wickets on DLS in Global Super League opener
stories.what_happened: In the tournament's second match at Providence Stadium, Guyana Amazon Warriors chased down San Francisco Unicorns' total, winning by 3 wickets with the result determined by the DLS (Duckworth-Lewis-Stern) method, used to adjust targets when a match is shortened, typically by weather. Hammad Azam scored 61 and Tim Robinson 38 to lead the chase, while Hassan Khan took 2 wickets for San Francisco.
key_points: Hammad Azam top-scores with 61 for Guyana
Tim Robinson adds 38 as the chase gets over the line
Hassan Khan takes 2 wickets for San Francisco Unicorns
Result decided by the DLS method

depth.background: The Global Super League is a new T20 franchise tournament held in the Caribbean (Providence, Guyana), part of a wave of T20 leagues launching worldwide as cricket boards chase the format's global audience and broadcast money. Guyana Amazon Warriors is an established Caribbean Premier League franchise; San Francisco Unicorns represents the growing US market for T20 cricket.

stories.title: US measles cases hit a 35-year high as vaccination rates keep sliding
stories.what_happened: The CDC said Friday that confirmed US measles cases have reached 2,318 this year, more than the 2,289 recorded in all of 2025 — the highest count in 35 years. Officials logged 35 distinct outbreaks in 2026, with the largest clusters in South Carolina, Utah and Arizona sickening hundreds of people. The CDC says 93% of this year's cases are in people who were unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown.
key_points: CDC confirms 2,318 measles cases in 2026 — already above all of 2025's total
93% of cases are in people who were never vaccinated
35 separate outbreaks reported this year, with the worst in South Carolina, Utah and Arizona
Measles was declared 'eliminated' in the US in 2000 — this is the second record year running

depth.background: The US wiped out measles as a native disease in 2000 through decades of high childhood vaccination coverage with the MMR (measles-mumps-rubella) shot, which is about 97% effective after two doses. Since then, cases have only ever arrived from travelers bringing it in from abroad. But vaccine hesitancy — parents skipping or delaying the MMR shot — has been rising for several years, especially in pockets of a few states, which lowers 'herd immunity' (the protection a community gets when enough people are immune that the virus can't find new hosts to spread through).

stories.title: Pakistan batter Abdullah Fazal ruled out of West Indies and England Tests with a back injury
stories.what_happened: The Pakistan Cricket Board confirmed on July 24 that top-order batter Abdullah Fazal, 23, will miss the Test series against West Indies and the following tour of England after suffering a lower-back injury during a training session on July 23 at the Brian Lara Cricket Academy Ground in Tarouba, Trinidad. An MRI scan and assessment by the team's medical panel confirmed he needs a period of rehabilitation. His absence is expected to open the door for the experienced Imam-ul-Haq to return at the top of the order, or for uncapped batter Awais Zafar to make his Test debut.
key_points: 23-year-old top-order batter Abdullah Fazal will miss both the West Indies and England Test series
He suffered a lower-back injury in training in Trinidad on July 23
An MRI and medical panel confirmed he needs a rehabilitation period
His absence likely opens the door for Imam-ul-Haq's return or a debut for Awais Zafar

depth.background: Pakistan's Test tour of the West Indies is the first assignment of the newly reinstated Babar Azam era as captain, with the squad also looking ahead to a subsequent tour of England. A settled, in-form top order is exactly what a team wants heading into back-to-back away Test series against strong opposition.

stories.title: Government moves to give 'Vande Mataram' the same legal shield as the National Anthem
stories.what_happened: The Minister of State for Home Affairs, Nityanand Rai, introduced a Bill in the Rajya Sabha on Friday, July 24, to amend the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 so that 'Vande Mataram' gets the same legal protection as the national anthem. Under the proposed amendment, intentionally insulting, obstructing, or disrupting the singing of the song would become a punishable offence carrying up to three years in prison — mirroring the existing penalty for insulting the anthem.
key_points: A new Bill would extend the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 to cover the national song
Intentionally insulting or disrupting it could carry up to 3 years in prison — matching the anthem's penalty
Union minister Nityanand Rai tabled it in the Rajya Sabha this Friday afternoon
Congress calls it the government's 'jail first' instinct; BJP frames it as protecting national symbols

depth.background: 'Vande Mataram' — written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in his 1882 novel Anandmath — was adopted as India's national song (distinct from the national anthem, 'Jana Gana Mana') in 1950. It has a politically loaded history: some Muslim organisations have historically objected to lyrics that personify the nation as a Hindu goddess, while the BJP has long pushed to elevate its status. Parliament marked the song's 150th anniversary with a special Rajya Sabha discussion in December 2025.

stories.title: McLaren tests its long-awaited 'Macarena' rear wing in Hungary practice — then pulls it after one session
stories.what_happened: McLaren brought a new floor and a version of the 'Macarena' rear wing to Friday practice at the Hungaroring, aiming to improve braking and corner-entry performance at a track known for tight, high-downforce corners. The floor closely follows the direction of Ferrari's SF-26 design. The team tested the wing on both Lando Norris's car and Oscar Piastri's, driven in FP1 by reserve Leonardo Fornaroli as part of a mandatory rookie practice session, but removed it after the session and does not currently plan to race it this weekend or at the next race after the summer break.
key_points: New floor and rear-wing package debuts in FP1, echoing ideas from Ferrari's SF-26
The flip-up 'Macarena' wing, already raced by Ferrari and Red Bull, was removed after Friday's running
Not expected to race this weekend or at the next race after the summer break
Reserve driver Leonardo Fornaroli ran Piastri's car with the upgrade during a mandatory rookie session

depth.background: In F1, teams bring new aerodynamic parts, called upgrades, to specific races to try to close performance gaps to rivals. A 'Macarena' wing is a nickname for a rear wing whose main flap flips upside-down on the straights to cut drag, a concept Ferrari and Red Bull already race. McLaren leads the constructors' championship but has trailed Mercedes and Ferrari in high-downforce corners, which is what this upgrade targets.

stories.title: Lance Stroll's Aston Martin breaks down in a suspected suspension failure, undercutting the team's big Hungary upgrade
stories.what_happened: During Friday's first practice session for the Hungarian Grand Prix, Lance Stroll's overhauled Aston Martin suffered what he described as a rear-left suspension failure on the exit of Turn 2, spinning him around. He kept the car away from the barriers and was unhurt, but the session was red-flagged for about six minutes while the car was recovered.
key_points: Stroll spun out between Turns 2 and 3 in FP1 after 11 laps in Aston Martin's new B-spec car
He reported a suspected rear-left suspension failure; he was unhurt
The stoppage cost the session about six minutes under red flag
Ironic timing: Aston Martin had rolled out a 16-part upgrade package that same morning

depth.background: Aston Martin has struggled for competitiveness this season and brought a major mid-season overhaul — a 'B-spec' car with 16 new parts — to the Hungarian Grand Prix, hoping to close the gap to the front-runners. Reliability problems on brand-new parts are a common risk when teams introduce big upgrades mid-season, since components haven't been tested under full race-weekend conditions yet.

stories.title: Russian ballistic missile strike kills at least 6 in Kyiv region — a day after Zelenskyy hosted Patriot-maker Raytheon
stories.what_happened: Russia fired a ballistic missile at the Kyiv region on Friday, killing at least 6 people and injuring dozens more, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The attack came a day after Zelenskyy met in Kyiv with senior representatives of Raytheon, the US defense contractor that manufactures the Patriot missile-defense system, to discuss producing Patriots jointly on Ukrainian soil. That meeting followed Trump's pledge, made in recent weeks, to license Ukraine to build the systems domestically. Trump and Zelenskyy are scheduled to meet in person at a NATO summit in Turkey the following Tuesday and Wednesday.
key_points: A Friday Russian ballistic missile attack on the Kyiv region killed at least 6 people and injured dozens, Zelenskyy said
The strike came one day after Zelenskyy met Raytheon representatives in Kyiv to discuss jointly producing Patriot air-defense systems inside Ukraine
It follows Trump's recent pledge to license Patriot production to Ukraine — part of a warmer recent tone toward Kyiv
Trump and Zelenskyy are due to meet at a NATO summit in Turkey next Tuesday and Wednesday

depth.background: Patriot systems are the US-made missile shields Ukraine relies on to intercept Russian ballistic missiles — the kind of weapon that just hit Kyiv. Ukraine has always had to import them fully built, which is slow and limited by how many the US and allies can spare. Trump has shifted noticeably warmer toward Ukraine in recent weeks after a period of tension, including floating letting Ukraine build Patriots domestically instead of only receiving finished units — a move that would give Kyiv a steadier, more independent supply of its own air defense.

stories.title: Aston Martin's revamped AMR26 breaks cover in Hungary — then Lance Stroll's car suffers a suspension failure
stories.what_happened: The upgraded AMR26 made its track debut in Hungarian GP practice, featuring a lighter chassis and a comprehensively redesigned front end. But the session was overshadowed when Stroll's car suffered a sudden left-rear suspension collapse exiting a corner, sending him spinning into the barriers. The failure struck a component the team believed was structurally sound, and a shortage of spare parts meant his car couldn't run in the next session.
key_points: Aston Martin rolled out a 16-part aerodynamic upgrade — its biggest of the season — for the Hungarian GP
The car got a lighter chassis, a redesigned nose, and reworked front and rear aerodynamics
Just 11 laps into first practice, Stroll's left-rear suspension suddenly failed, spinning him across the track
The car couldn't be repaired in time for second practice because the team lacked spare parts

depth.background: Aston Martin has struggled to match its ambitions in 2026 despite hiring F1 design legend Adrian Newey to lead a car overhaul. We reported yesterday that Newey said the reworked car had found 'seconds' of lap time in development — this weekend was the upgrade's first real on-track test.

thread.previously: Adrian Newey said his reworked Aston Martin design had found 'seconds' of lap time in development.
thread.changed: The upgrade made its real on-track debut in Hungary practice — but Lance Stroll's car suffered a sudden suspension failure just 11 laps in, denying the team a clean first look at the new package.

prev_ref.title: F1 design legend Adrian Newey says his overhauled Aston Martin has found 'seconds' of pace

stories.title: McLaren hands its F2 champion reserve a real F1 audition in Hungary
stories.what_happened: McLaren swapped Piastri out of FP1 at the Hungarian Grand Prix and put Fornaroli in the car instead, fulfilling the team's young-driver quota. Fornaroli trialled McLaren's version of Ferrari's upside-down rear wing design, with his race engineer reporting it performed well during the session.
key_points: Oscar Piastri sat out FP1; McLaren reserve Leonardo Fornaroli drove the MCL40 instead
It's Fornaroli's second F1 practice outing — he finished an impressive 5th on his Barcelona debut
He tested McLaren's own upside-down rear wing design, which his engineer said 'worked well'
F1 rules require every team to give young/rookie drivers at least 4 practice sessions a year

depth.background: F1 mandates that every team run a 'young driver' — someone with two or fewer Grand Prix starts — in at least four practice sessions each season, precisely so teams can properly test junior talent in a real car rather than just simulators. Leonardo Fornaroli, the reigning Formula 2 champion, is McLaren's official reserve and development driver, using these sessions to build his case for a race seat as the 2027 grid takes shape.

stories.title: F1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli sits out Hungarian GP practice — then struggles once he's back in the car
stories.what_happened: Mercedes used its Hungarian GP FP1 rookie obligation to give Fred Vesti the wheel instead of Antonelli, and Vesti finished a credible 7th in the session. When Antonelli returned for FP2 in the afternoon, he struggled to find a balance with the car and ended up only 13th fastest — a poor showing for a driver leading the standings.
key_points: Mercedes benched points leader Antonelli for FP1, handing the seat to reserve driver Fred Vesti
Vesti finished 7th in his session — a solid reserve-driver outing
Antonelli returned for FP2 but could only manage 13th, well off the pace
Part of F1's rule requiring teams to give rookies FP1 track time

depth.background: F1 rules require every team to give an F1-inexperienced driver track time in at least two Free Practice 1 sessions each season, which is why regular race drivers sometimes sit out Friday mornings for reserves or juniors. Antonelli is Mercedes' young driver currently leading the championship; Vesti is the team's reserve and test driver.

stories.title: Charles Leclerc tops Hungarian GP practice despite a scary mechanical scare — 'something broke'
stories.what_happened: Leclerc set the pace on soft tyres in FP1 at the Hungaroring, but with seven minutes left in the session reported a technical issue — 'something broke' — while upshifting on a flying lap. Replays suggested a possible power-related fault, and Ferrari's crew used a fire extinguisher as a precaution while monitoring high brake temperatures; Leclerc got the car to the pit lane but had to be pushed the rest of the way to the garage. He still held onto P1 for the session. In the afternoon's FP2, Lewis Hamilton beat him to fastest time by 0.148 seconds.
key_points: Leclerc set the fastest FP1 lap, 1:19.075, nearly half a second clear of Verstappen and Hamilton
With 7 minutes left, he reported 'something broke' after an upshift on a flying lap
Team used a fire extinguisher near the brakes as a precaution; the car had to be pushed back to the garage
Hamilton then beat him in FP2, setting up a tight qualifying battle

depth.background: Friday practice sessions (FP1 and FP2) exist so teams can test setups before Saturday's qualifying and Sunday's race — being fastest on Friday matters far less than being reliable and quick when points are actually on the line. Ferrari and Leclerc are chasing a title fight this season against Red Bull's Verstappen and a resurgent Hamilton/Ferrari teammate pairing.

stories.title: Stewards summon Carlos Sainz and Max Verstappen after a tense traffic incident in Hungarian GP practice
stories.what_happened: During Friday's first practice session for the Hungarian Grand Prix, Carlos Sainz and Max Verstappen were summoned by the FIA stewards after an on-track traffic incident, with both drivers noted for erratic driving. Separately, Sainz locked all four tyres approaching Turn 1 and narrowly avoided the barriers. Verstappen finished the session second-fastest, half a second behind Charles Leclerc's benchmark time.
key_points: The pair were called in following an on-track incident during FP1 at the Hungaroring
Sainz also locked all four tyres into Turn 1, narrowly missing the barriers
Stewards noted both drivers for erratic driving
Verstappen ended FP1 second fastest, half a second off Leclerc's pace

depth.background: Formula 1's stewards review any on-track incident that could be dangerous or unsporting, even in a practice session where the results don't count for the championship — because near-misses in practice can turn into real accidents once qualifying and the race are underway and stakes are higher.

stories.title: Fernando Alonso sits out Hungarian GP first practice with back injury, returns for FP2
stories.what_happened: Aston Martin confirmed Alonso would sit out first practice (FP1) at the Hungaroring on Friday to continue treatment on a back muscle injury carried over from Belgium, with reserve driver Felipe Drugovich stepping into the car instead. Drugovich finished the session 16th fastest, about three tenths of a second slower than Alonso's teammate Lance Stroll. After further treatment and a medical check, Alonso was cleared by the FIA (motorsport's governing body) and returned to his car for second practice (FP2) alongside Stroll.
key_points: Alonso skips FP1 to manage a lumbar (lower back) muscle injury
Injury dates back to last weekend's Belgian Grand Prix
Reserve driver Felipe Drugovich fills in, finishes FP1 16th
Alonso medically cleared by FIA, returns alongside Stroll for FP2

depth.background: Fernando Alonso, a two-time world champion now driving for Aston Martin, picked up a muscular injury in his lower back at last weekend's Belgian Grand Prix. Formula 1 rules allow teams to swap in a reserve driver for a practice session without penalty, which is why Aston Martin could call on its reserve, Felipe Drugovich, rather than lose Alonso's track time entirely.

stories.title: India confirmed among nations hit by Trump's new 10% 'forced-labour' tariff as the old US trade deadline expires
stories.what_happened: The US rolled out new tariffs on roughly 60 economies overnight Thursday into Friday, using Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 — a law letting the president tax imports from countries found to engage in 'unjust' trade practices — to replace the temporary 10% emergency tariff that expired at midnight. India is among about 10 countries the US designated as having 'forced-labour' trade practices, and will face a 10% tariff on exports to the US, the same rate as the UK and Canada. This landed the same day India's own interim tariff deal with the US expired with no agreement signed.
key_points: The US replaced its temporary global tariff with a new permanent regime on roughly 60 economies
India is one of about 10 countries hit with a 10% tariff, justified under a 'forced-labour' trade rule
The move lands the same day India and the US failed to sign an interim trade pact before its deadline
Other partners face different rates: UK and Canada also 10%; EU and Taiwan under 10%; Switzerland and Japan up to 12.5%

depth.background: Since April, Trump had kept most countries under a temporary 'reciprocal' emergency tariff while negotiating individual deals; that emergency legal authority was struck down by the Supreme Court in February, forcing the administration to find a new legal basis. India and the US had also been separately negotiating their own interim trade pact, due to expire this week without an agreement.

thread.previously: We reported that India's interim tariff deal with the US was set to expire with no pact signed, as talks went down to the wire.
thread.changed: The deadline has now passed without a deal, and India has been confirmed as one of about 10 countries hit with a new 10% permanent US tariff under a forced-labour trade designation.

stories.title: Indian racer Kush Maini storms to his second Formula 2 pole of the season in Hungary
stories.what_happened: Kush Maini claimed pole position for the Formula 2 Hungarian Grand Prix on Friday, setting a lap of 1 minute 28.896 seconds around the Hungaroring to beat championship contender Rafael Câmara (Invicta Racing) by just over a tenth of a second, with Campos Racing's Noel León third. It's Maini's second F2 pole of the 2026 season.
key_points: Kush Maini (ART Grand Prix) took pole for Sunday's F2 Hungarian GP feature race
He set a 1:28.896 lap, beating title contender Rafael Câmara by over a tenth
It's his second F2 pole of the 2026 season
Maini is one of the highest-profile Indian drivers on the current F1 support bill

depth.background: Formula 2 is the main feeder series just below Formula 1 — most current F1 drivers came through it — and races on the same weekends and tracks as the F1 calendar. Kush Maini, from Bengaluru, has raced in Europe's junior single-seater ladder for years and is one of the highest-profile Indian drivers currently competing on the F1 support bill.

stories.title: Lance Stroll's Aston Martin suffers a suspension failure on its big upgrade debut
stories.what_happened: Lance Stroll's rear suspension appeared to fail on the exit of Turn 2 during Friday's first practice session in Hungary, sending his upgraded Aston Martin into a 360-degree spin. The team didn't have enough time to repair the damage before the second session began, so Stroll missed all of FP2 while teammate Fernando Alonso continued running the new upgrade.
key_points: Stroll spins 360 degrees in FP1 after his rear suspension appears to buckle
He misses the entire second practice session while the car is repaired
The failure came on the very session Aston Martin's heavily upgraded 'B-spec' AMR26 debuted
Teammate Fernando Alonso's future in F1 is tied to this upgrade actually working

depth.background: Aston Martin has struggled for competitiveness this season and brought a major mechanical and aerodynamic overhaul to their AMR26 car — often called a 'B-spec' — to the Hungarian Grand Prix, hoping to close the gap to the midfield. Suspension is the system of arms and springs connecting a car's wheels to its body; a failure there can send a car into a sudden, uncontrollable spin.

stories.title: England seamer Em Arlott signs three-year deal to leave Warwickshire for Yorkshire
stories.what_happened: England seamer Em Arlott has signed a three-year contract with Yorkshire and will leave Warwickshire at the end of the 2026 season, the clubs confirmed on July 24. Arlott, who has ten international caps since debuting in 2025 and last played for England at the Women's ODI World Cup, said she wanted a new challenge.
key_points: Arlott, capped 10 times by England, joins Yorkshire from 2027
Move comes as Yorkshire builds up its Tier One women's programme
Warwickshire's head coach says she leaves 'with our blessing'
Latest sign of growing investment in England's women's domestic game

depth.background: English domestic women's cricket restructured in 2025 into a tiered county system, with clubs investing seriously in players for the first time at anything approaching the scale of the men's game. Yorkshire has been building up its women's programme as it moved into the new Tier One.

stories.title: BCCI raises the reserve price for Team India's jersey sponsorship to ₹4.9 crore per match
stories.what_happened: The BCCI raised the reserve — the minimum floor price a bidder must clear — for Team India's title sponsorship to ₹4.9 crore (about $590,000) per home international match, up from ₹4.2 crore under the outgoing IDFC FIRST Bank deal, as it opened bidding for the 2026–28 commercial cycle running through March 2028 and covering roughly 35 home matches, worth an estimated minimum of ₹171 crore. Reserve prices for associate sponsorship slots were also raised, to ₹95 lakh from ₹82 lakh per match.
key_points: New floor price for India's title sponsorship rights is up over 15% from the outgoing deal
Bidding opens for the 2026–28 commercial cycle, covering roughly 35 home matches
Deal is worth an estimated minimum of ₹171 crore over its term
Associate-sponsor reserve prices were also raised, from ₹82 lakh to ₹95 lakh per match

depth.background: The logo on the front of the Indian cricket team's jersey is one of the most valuable pieces of advertising space in Indian sport, given the team's massive following. The rights are auctioned periodically by the BCCI (India's cricket board) to the highest bidder, with the outgoing sponsor being IDFC FIRST Bank.

stories.title: Sergio Perez says Cadillac 'hasn't developed enough' and fears Aston Martin will close the gap
stories.what_happened: Ahead of Hungarian GP practice, Cadillac driver Sergio Perez said the rookie team 'hasn't developed the car as much as we would have liked' this season, and that he's concerned Aston Martin's new Hungary-spec upgrade package will erode whatever competitive edge Cadillac currently holds. His teammate Valtteri Bottas struck a more optimistic tone about the team's trajectory.
key_points: Perez admits Cadillac's in-season development pace has fallen short of the team's own hopes
He's specifically worried about Aston Martin's new Hungary upgrade closing Cadillac's current edge
The upgrade is tied to design legend Adrian Newey's overhaul of the Aston Martin car
Teammate Valtteri Bottas gave a more upbeat view of the team's progress

depth.background: Cadillac is a brand-new entrant to Formula 1 in 2026 — the first new constructor added to the grid in years — and how quickly a rookie team can develop its car during its debut season is one of the sport's classic tests. Aston Martin, meanwhile, has been investing heavily in a technical rebuild led by renowned designer Adrian Newey, whose past cars have dominated multiple eras of F1.

stories.title: Russian missile hits a Kyiv arms fair, killing 10, as Ukraine unleashes its biggest strike on Russia this year
stories.what_happened: On Friday, a Russian ballistic missile struck an arms exhibition in Kyiv, killing at least 10 people and injuring around 100 — one of the deadliest single strikes on the Ukrainian capital in months. Hours later, Ukraine answered with what analysts called one of its biggest strikes on Russia all year: drones and missiles hit a missile factory and, for the fifth time in a week, warehouses belonging to Wildberries, Russia's largest e-commerce company, sparking a major fire in St Petersburg. Russia said its air defenses shot down 571 Ukrainian drones overnight across 15 regions plus occupied Crimea and the Black Sea. President Zelenskyy warned Russia is readying an even larger strike within the next 48 hours.
key_points: A Russian ballistic missile hit a Kyiv defense-industry exhibition, killing at least 10 and injuring about 100
Zelenskyy says Russia is preparing an even bigger strike within 48 hours
Ukraine answered with one of its largest attacks of the year, hitting a missile plant and e-commerce giant Wildberries' warehouses
Russia says it shot down 571 Ukrainian drones overnight across 15 regions, Crimea and the Black Sea

depth.background: Russia and Ukraine have been locked in near-daily missile-and-drone exchanges for months: Russia targeting Ukrainian cities and infrastructure, Ukraine hitting back at military-industrial and logistics targets deep inside Russia. This runs in parallel with the separate US-Israel war against Iran that has drawn in the region's oil and shipping routes.

thread.previously: We reported a Russian ballistic missile strike killed at least 6 people in the Kyiv region, a day after Zelenskyy hosted Raytheon, the maker of the Patriot air-defense system.
thread.changed: A new, separate Kyiv strike on an arms exhibition has killed at least 10 and injured about 100, and Ukraine has hit back with one of its largest strikes on Russia this year, while Zelenskyy warns of an even bigger Russian strike within 48 hours.
