stories.title: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak becomes the fastest-spreading in recorded history, with the death toll passing 1,000
stories.what_happened: DRC health authorities reported 1,033 deaths and 2,536 confirmed cases as of July 23-24, with 506 people recovered and 738 still in isolation. The outbreak crossed 1,000 confirmed deaths within just 40 days of the response being activated — a speed of spread health officials say is unprecedented in Ebola's recorded history. A U.S. citizen aid worker who tested positive was medically evacuated to a hospital in Frankfurt, Germany on July 13 and is in stable condition; a second American was also evacuated, and seven U.S. aid workers were quarantined in Kenya as the virus reached remote parts of Ituri.
key_points: Confirmed cases have topped 2,500, with 1,033 deaths as of July 24
It crossed 1,000 deaths within just ~40 days of the response starting — the fastest fatal surge in Ebola's history
It's now the third-largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded, trailing only 2014-16 West Africa
Two American aid workers have been medically evacuated; no vaccine exists for this Ebola strain

depth.background: Ebola is a severe, often fatal viral hemorrhagic fever first identified in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) in 1976, spread through contact with bodily fluids of infected people or animals. This outbreak, declared on May 15, 2026 in DRC's eastern Ituri Province, is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of the virus — a rarer cousin of the Zaire strain that killed roughly 11,000 people in West Africa's 2014-16 epidemic. Ituri is a remote, conflict-affected region, which has made contact tracing and treatment delivery difficult from the start.

stories.title: Josh de Caires outbowls and outbats his father Michael Atherton's List A best in a Middlesex romp
stories.what_happened: In a One-Day Cup Group B match at Southampton on July 24, Middlesex beat Hampshire by 160 runs. Middlesex posted 284 for 8 in their 50 overs, with de Caires opening the batting for 75 and half-centuries from Sam Robson and Ben Geddes. Hampshire then collapsed to 124 all out in 31.2 overs, with de Caires — an off-spin bowler — taking 6 for 35, including a spell of 5 for 14 in 27 balls.
key_points: De Caires scored 75 then took 6 for 35 as Middlesex thrashed Hampshire by 160 runs
His bowling figures beat his father Michael Atherton's List A career-best of 4 for 42
It's Middlesex's best List A bowling in the 21st century outside one other performance
De Caires, a genuine all-rounder, has previously been called up to the England Lions

depth.background: List A cricket is the official name for professional one-day (50-over) matches below full international level — in England, the domestic top tier is the Metro Bank One-Day Cup. Josh de Caires plays for Middlesex and is the son of Michael Atherton, a former England Test captain now a leading Sky Sports commentator; Atherton also played List A cricket in his career.

stories.title: Haas boss Ayao Komatsu says F1's 2026 rules hide true driver performance from fans — but calls it fixable
stories.what_happened: Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu told Autosport that fans currently 'don't get a true picture of driver performance,' because much of a lap's pace now depends on software managing energy deployment based on subtle throttle inputs — differences a driver can't fully see or control, worth several tenths of a second especially in qualifying. He said, 'I think we're trying to simplify the sport... currently it's just too complicated.' F1 already tightened related rules starting from the Miami Grand Prix, part of a mid-season 'six fixes' package addressing side effects of the new hybrid rules, including 'lift and coast' driving and closing-speed safety concerns around slower cars.
key_points: Komatsu says hidden software managing battery deployment can be worth several tenths of a lap
He avoids calling resulting mistakes 'driver error' — says even drivers can't track every variable
F1 already tightened rules from the Miami GP as part of a mid-season 'six fixes' package
Bigger changes, including a new 60/40 engine-to-electric power split, are planned for 2027

depth.background: F1's 2026 rules brought the biggest power-unit shake-up in years, moving to a near-50/50 split between traditional combustion power and electric power from the hybrid system, compared to a much smaller electric share before. That's made software that manages how and when the car uses its battery a much bigger factor in lap time than in previous years.

stories.title: Oil holds near $100 a barrel as traders weigh whether the Houthi Red Sea blockade threat will actually bite
stories.what_happened: Brent crude futures rose about 7% to settle above $100 a barrel, and US benchmark WTI crude climbed about 6% to roughly $92 — both hitting levels not seen since May. The move followed the Houthis' claim that they will target Saudi, Israeli and US-linked tankers passing through the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the narrow gateway between the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean.
key_points: Brent crude jumped past $100 a barrel this week for the first time since May
Houthi rebels say they've blockaded Saudi oil shipments through the Bab el-Mandeb strait
That chokepoint carries 12-15% of global sea trade — worth more than $1 trillion a year
Analysts are split on whether the blockade threat sticks or fades like past ones have

depth.background: Iran's Houthi allies in Yemen struck two Saudi oil tankers, Encelia and Layla, in the Red Sea this week, and declared a naval blockade on Saudi oil shipments — opening a new front in the Iran war days after Iran itself moved to restrict the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation for US and Israeli strikes.

thread.previously: Houthi rebels struck two Saudi tankers in the Red Sea and declared a blockade, opening a new front in the Iran war alongside Iran's own move against the Strait of Hormuz.
thread.changed: That threat has now moved markets directly — Brent crude has crossed $100 a barrel for the first time since May, and traders are debating whether the blockade will actually hold up.

prev_ref.title: Houthi rebels strike two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, opening a new front in the Iran war

stories.title: Trump says a 'massive' Iran attack 'may not be necessary' as Tehran gets 'serious' about a deal
stories.what_happened: Speaking to reporters on Friday, Trump said he has not decided whether to launch the 'massive' strikes on Iran he had threatened, saying Tehran is now 'being by far the most serious that we've seen' in talks — 'but that doesn't mean we get there.' He said Iran faces a choice between a deal or a 'much higher level' of strikes. Despite the softer tone, US Central Command carried out its 13th consecutive night of strikes on Iran early Friday, targeting military command centers, drone facilities and communications networks.
key_points: Trump says he hasn't decided on major new strikes as Tehran turns 'serious' in talks
The 13th straight night of US strikes hit Iran even as the diplomatic track stays open
VP JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are now directly involved in the back-channel talks
Pakistan is separately pushing to help restart the ceasefire process that collapsed this month

depth.background: A US-brokered ceasefire from a June memorandum of understanding fell apart in early July, and Washington has since carried out nightly strikes on Iran. The war has widened fast this week: Iran fired drones at US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan, and its Houthi allies in Yemen struck two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea. Yesterday Iran rejected an Iraq-brokered ceasefire proposal, and Trump said he was weighing a bigger escalation in response.

thread.previously: Iran rejected an Iraq-brokered ceasefire proposal, and Trump said he was weighing a bigger escalation against Tehran in response.
thread.changed: A day later, Trump struck a softer tone — saying a 'massive' attack 'may not be necessary' because Tehran is 'getting serious' in talks — even as nightly US strikes continued.

prev_ref.title: Iran rejects an Iraq-brokered ceasefire proposal as Trump weighs a bigger escalation

stories.title: AI-spending anxiety spreads: chip stocks slide 6% this month as Wall Street braces for Meta, Microsoft and Amazon earnings
stories.what_happened: Chip stocks have fallen into a rough patch after a blistering first-half rally — the MSCI World Semiconductor Index is down 6% in July as investors lock in profits and grow warier of rising spending forecasts. The trigger: Alphabet raised its 2026 capital-spending forecast to between $195 billion and $205 billion, and even with strong results (Google Cloud revenue up 82%), its stock came under pressure. Meta has similarly lifted its planned 2026 capex to $125–145 billion. Now attention turns to Microsoft and Meta, which report earnings on July 29, and Amazon, which reports July 30 — all facing the same question of whether AI revenue is catching up to AI spending.
key_points: The MSCI World Semiconductor Index has fallen 6% in July on profit-taking
Alphabet just raised its 2026 spending plan to $195–205 billion, and got punished for it
Meta already lifted its 2026 capex guidance to $125–145 billion
Microsoft, Meta and Amazon report next week — investors want proof this spending is paying off

depth.background: For over two years, Big Tech has poured hundreds of billions of dollars into data centers and AI chips, betting that AI would eventually generate revenue big enough to justify the spending. Across Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft, that AI infrastructure spending is on track to hit roughly $725 billion in 2026 alone. Wall Street cheered this for a while, but is now increasingly asking a harder question: where's the return?

stories.title: Stanford scientists find a natural body molecule that curbs appetite like Ozempic — without the nausea
stories.what_happened: Stanford Medicine researchers used an AI model called Peptide Predictor to scan thousands of small protein fragments the human body naturally produces, looking for ones that might act like hunger hormones. They found BRP (short for BRINP2-related peptide), a tiny 12-amino-acid molecule that acts directly on the hypothalamus — the brain region that governs hunger and metabolism — rather than acting broadly across the body the way GLP-1 drugs do. In mice, a single dose cut food intake by up to 50% within an hour, with none of the nausea, food aversion or muscle loss seen with existing drugs.
key_points: An AI tool sifted 2,600+ tiny protein fragments to find one your body already makes
The molecule, called BRP, cut animal appetite by up to 50% within an hour
No nausea, no food aversion, no muscle loss in the animal tests — Ozempic's biggest complaints
Still years from a human drug — no clinical trials in people yet

depth.background: Ozempic, Wegovy and similar drugs (called GLP-1s) triggered a weight-loss revolution by mimicking a gut hormone that tells your brain 'you're full.' They work, but many users report nausea, vomiting and loss of muscle along with fat. Drugmakers and scientists have spent years hunting for something that gets the appetite-suppressing benefit without those side effects.

stories.title: Jhandu Kumar, son of a vegetable vendor, wins India's first medal of the 2026 Commonwealth Games
stories.what_happened: Jhandu Kumar, who has been affected by polio since birth and comes from a family of modest means (his father is a vegetable vendor), won bronze in the men's heavyweight para powerlifting final with a best lift of 190kg and a combined score of 130.9 points — India's first medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games. Nigeria's Riluwan Idris took gold (132.8) and England's Matthew Harding silver (131.0). Kumar began as a para-athletics competitor in shot put and discus before switching to powerlifting in 2017, setting a national record of 206kg earlier this year at the Khelo India Para Games.
key_points: Jhandu Kumar took bronze in men's heavyweight para powerlifting in Glasgow
He lifted 190kg for a 130.9-point total, India's first medal of these Games
Polio-affected since birth, he switched from para athletics to powerlifting in 2017
Set national records this year (206kg) before qualifying for the Games

depth.background: The Commonwealth Games 2026 opened in Glasgow on July 23, with India's flag carried by weightlifter Mirabai Chanu and boxer Lovlina Borgohain carrying the baton. Para powerlifting was the first sport to hand out medals on Day 1. India has historically punched below its weight at multi-sport Games relative to its population, making early, feel-good medal stories like this one a big deal domestically.

stories.title: West Indies name their Test squad for Pakistan series — with a maiden call-up and an injury swap
stories.what_happened: Cricket West Indies announced its 15-player squad for the two-match home Test series against Pakistan, running from July 25 to August 6 in Tarouba and Port of Spain. Roston Chase captains the side with Jomel Warrican as vice-captain. Joshua Bishop, a left-arm orthodox spinner with 119 wickets in just 25 first-class matches, earns his maiden Test call-up. Kirk McKenzie returns to the squad in place of John Campbell, who was ruled out with a left hamstring strain. Pacer Anderson Phillip was dropped after his showing in the second Test against Sri Lanka.
key_points: West Indies picked a 15-man squad for their 2-match home Test series against Pakistan, starting July 25
Left-arm spinner Joshua Bishop gets his first-ever Test call-up after 119 first-class wickets at a 23.90 average
Kirk McKenzie returns to the squad, replacing John Campbell who's out with a hamstring strain
Roston Chase captains the side, with Jomel Warrican as vice-captain; pacer Anderson Phillip was dropped

depth.background: West Indies have been trying to rebuild a Test side capable of competing consistently, after years of struggling to match their historic strength in the format. Fresh faces earning maiden caps — like uncapped spinner Joshua Bishop here — are part of that rebuild, alongside recalls for players in good domestic form, such as Kirk McKenzie's 323 runs at an average of 64.60 in the latest West Indies Championship season.

stories.title: India's Ashok Malik finishes agonisingly fourth, missing Commonwealth Games' first para-powerlifting medal by inches
stories.what_happened: In the men's lightweight category, Ashok Malik lifted a personal-best 200kg for a total of 143.8 points, finishing fourth. England's Mark Swan took gold with a Games-record 222kg lift (153.9 points), Nigeria's Roland Ezuruike won silver with 185kg, and Malaysia's Bonnie Bunyau Gustin claimed bronze with 153.5 points — narrowly ahead of Malik.
key_points: Ashok Malik lifted a personal-best 200kg but finished 4th in men's lightweight para-powerlifting
England's Mark Swan won gold with a Games-record 222kg lift
This was India's first-ever shot at a Commonwealth Games para-powerlifting medal
Malik's points total was just short of Malaysia's bronze medallist

depth.background: Para-powerlifting is a bench-press-only sport for athletes with physical disabilities, contested by weight class and scored on a points system that adjusts for bodyweight so lifters of different sizes can be compared fairly. India has been steadily expanding its investment in Paralympic and para-sport programs, and Glasgow 2026 marked the country's first entrants in Commonwealth Games para-powerlifting.

stories.title: India's monsoon turns deadly — cloudbursts and floods kill dozens, displace thousands
stories.what_happened: Cloudbursts (sudden, extremely intense, localized rainfall), flash floods and landslides hit a large stretch of India this week, killing dozens and forcing mass evacuations. The India Meteorological Department said nearly a third of the country's states received rainfall 60% above the long-period average on July 23 alone, with the Himalayan states and the west coast among the hardest hit. Isolated pockets of Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Konkan and Goa are forecast to see extremely heavy rain into July 24.
key_points: Cloudbursts, flash floods and landslides have battered a wide swathe of India this week
Nearly a third of India's states got 60% more rain than normal on July 23 alone
Dozens are dead and thousands evacuated, from the Himalayan region to the west coast
IMD (weather department) warns more extremely heavy rain is likely through July 24

depth.background: India's economy and food supply depend heavily on the June-to-September monsoon, which normally arrives in predictable waves. But scientists have long warned that climate change is making monsoon rainfall more erratic — longer dry spells punctuated by sudden, extreme bursts — rather than steady seasonal rain. This week's disasters follow what had otherwise been described as a 'patchy' monsoon overall.

stories.title: Pakistan reinstates Babar Azam as Test captain, dumping Shan Masood after a brutal run
stories.what_happened: The Pakistan Cricket Board removed Shan Masood as Test captain and reinstated Babar Azam, announcing the change alongside the squad for a two-Test tour of the West Indies beginning July 25. Chief selector Aaqib Javed cited repetitive mistakes, poor over-rates and weak tactical decisions in key moments as reasons for the switch.
key_points: Babar Azam is Pakistan's Test captain again, replacing Shan Masood
Masood won just 4 of 16 Tests in charge — the worst start of any Pakistan captain on record
The switch was announced alongside the squad for two Tests in the West Indies, starting July 25
Babar previously led Pakistan to 10 wins in 20 Tests, including series sweeps in Bangladesh and Sri Lanka

depth.background: Pakistan cricket has a long history of swapping captains quickly when results sour. Babar Azam stepped down as Test captain around three years ago; Shan Masood then took over but struggled badly, losing 12 of his 16 Tests in charge — a worse record than every past Pakistan Test captain except Misbah-ul-Haq, who led far more matches. Pakistan now heads into back-to-back away tours of the West Indies and England.

stories.title: Trump swaps his global emergency tariff for a permanent 'forced-labour' tariff on 60 countries
stories.what_happened: The U.S. Trade Representative's office imposed new duties on 60 countries — covering 99.4% of all U.S. imports — as the temporary 10% global tariff expired on July 24. Rates range from 10% (for countries that have banned forced-labour imports) to 12.5% (for those that haven't). Canada, Mexico, India and the UK are among those facing the 10% rate; Brazil was hit with 12.5% and called the move 'arbitrary' and 'unjustified'.
key_points: New tariffs of 10-12.5% hit America's top 60 trading partners
Replaces a temporary tariff the Supreme Court had ruled illegal
Officially justified by forced-labour import bans, not trade balances
Brazil, Canada, the EU and others reject the reasoning as 'arbitrary'

depth.background: Since returning to office, President Trump used emergency economic powers to impose sweeping tariffs on nearly every country. In February 2026 the Supreme Court ruled he lacked the legal authority to declare a trade 'emergency' and tax imports that way, so the White House built a replacement using a different, narrower law — one that lets it tariff countries that fail to police forced labour in their supply chains.

stories.title: Sensex and Nifty fall for a fifth straight day as oil tops $100 on the Iran war
stories.what_happened: The Sensex closed at 76,059.77, down 331.62 points (0.43%); the Nifty 50 closed at 23,767.45, down 102.15 points (0.43%) — the fifth consecutive losing session for both indices. Auto, metal and energy stocks dragged the market down, while IT and media stocks gained.
key_points: Sensex fell 331 points, Nifty fell 102 points to close at 23,767
Fifth straight losing session for both indices
Auto, metal and energy stocks led the fall; IT and media held up
Driven by crude oil spiking past $100/barrel on the Iran war and Houthi attacks

depth.background: Yesterday we reported the Sensex and Nifty fell for a fourth straight day as Gulf tensions pushed oil higher. That selloff has now stretched to a fifth day as the region's violence escalates further — continued US strikes on Iran and fresh Houthi missile attacks on Saudi tankers — pushing crude oil, a major cost for import-dependent India, even higher.

thread.previously: We reported a fourth straight day of losses as Gulf tensions pushed oil prices higher.
thread.changed: The losing streak has extended to a fifth day, with oil now topping $100/barrel and auto, metal and energy stocks leading the decline.

prev_ref.title: Sensex and Nifty fall for a fourth straight day as Gulf tensions push oil prices higher

stories.title: Sonam Wangchuk ends his 26-day hunger strike after two ministers step in — but the protests don't stop
stories.what_happened: Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike on Friday, in the presence of two federal ministers, after what he called 'a long negotiation... in view of possible violence in the country.' His announcement followed a video message from PM Modi promising a tougher law against paper leaks and fast-track courts. Protest organizers said demonstrations will continue until Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns.
key_points: Wangchuk ends fast after 26 days, following talks with two federal ministers
PM Modi pledges a tougher anti-paper-leak law in a video address
Protesters vow to continue until the Education Minister resigns
His fast had become the rallying symbol of India's 'Cockroach' protest movement

depth.background: Sonam Wangchuk is a Ladakh-based education reformer and climate activist. He began a hunger strike over exam paper leaks, and yesterday we reported his health crisis was deepening, with a Delhi court ordering him moved to a private hospital. His strike became the anchor of the 'Cockroach' protest movement — a youth-led wave of demonstrations that began more than a month ago demanding education reforms after leaks in major competitive entrance exams.

thread.previously: We reported his hunger-strike health crisis deepening, with a Delhi court ordering him moved to a private hospital.
thread.changed: He has now ended the 26-day fast after direct intervention from two federal ministers and a PM Modi pledge on a tougher anti-paper-leak law, though protesters vow to continue until the education minister resigns.

prev_ref.title: Delhi High Court orders activist Sonam Wangchuk moved to a private hospital as his hunger-strike health crisis deepens

stories.title: Afghanistan hands Rahmat Shah the captaincy and rebuilds its pace attack for the Ireland ODI series
stories.what_happened: Afghanistan's cricket board named Rahmat Shah the new Test and ODI captain this week, with Rahmanullah Gurbaz as vice-captain, after Shahidi stepped down. On July 24, the board announced the ODI squad for Rahmat's first series in charge — a five-match tour of Ireland starting August 5 — bringing back fast bowler Fazalhaq Farooqi and pace options Yamin Ahmadzai and Saleem Safi, while senior all-rounder Mohammad Nabi was omitted.
key_points: Rahmat Shah named Afghanistan's new Test and ODI captain, replacing Hashmatullah Shahidi
Shahidi, who led Afghanistan's famous 2023 World Cup run, stepped down after 5 years
Squad for the Ireland ODI series overhauls the pace attack after a 3-0 loss to India
Fazalhaq Farooqi returns; veteran all-rounder Mohammad Nabi is left out

depth.background: Hashmatullah Shahidi had captained Afghanistan since 2021, including their standout 2023 World Cup run where they beat former champions England, Pakistan and Sri Lanka to finish sixth. Rahmat Shah, a 128-ODI, 12-Test veteran, has been his deputy since 2021. Afghanistan is coming off a heavy 3-0 ODI series defeat to India.

stories.title: England's Jacob Bethell ruled out of The Hundred with a knee injury — and his Pakistan Test spot is now in doubt
stories.what_happened: Bethell suffered a right knee injury during the India ODI series; a Monday MRI scan confirmed it was serious enough to rule him out of the entire Hundred tournament. Birmingham Phoenix has replaced him as captain with South African batter Donovan Ferreira for the rest of the competition. England's cricket board has not given a recovery timeline, so his fitness for the first Test against Pakistan at Headingley, starting August 19, is now uncertain.
key_points: Jacob Bethell out for the whole Hundred season with a right knee injury
Injury MRI-confirmed after England's ODI series against India
Birmingham Phoenix names Donovan Ferreira as replacement captain
His spot in England's Pakistan Test series, starting August 19, is now uncertain

depth.background: Bethell is a 22-year-old England all-rounder and one of the breakout stars of the domestic Hundred competition, retained by Birmingham Phoenix for £340,000 and named the team's captain this season. He had just finished playing in England's ODI series against India, where he was named player of the match in the series-deciding game at Lord's.

stories.title: Haas is quietly weighing whether to drop Esteban Ocon for a rookie next season
stories.what_happened: Reports from the Hungarian Grand Prix weekend say Haas is debating whether to keep Ocon alongside Bearman for 2027, or replace him with a rookie — either Rafael Camara, a Brazilian junior driver, or Leonardo Fornaroli, a back-to-back F3 and F2 champion getting FP1 running with McLaren this weekend. No decision has been announced.
key_points: Haas is debating replacing driver Esteban Ocon for 2027
Junior options in the frame: Rafael Camara and Leonardo Fornaroli
Bearman, Ocon's current teammate, has impressed; Ocon has struggled
No decision announced yet

depth.background: Esteban Ocon is a veteran French driver who joined Haas for 2025 after years at Alpine, where he won the team's only race so far. Haas is a smaller, independent team that often uses driver changes to try to climb the midfield. His young British teammate, Oliver Bearman, has been the team's brighter spot this year.

stories.title: American rookie Colton Herta gets his second Cadillac F1 outing — with a brakes fix the team badly needed
stories.what_happened: Herta drove Bottas's car in first practice at the Hungarian Grand Prix. Cadillac used the session to run an upgraded brakes package, which Bottas said was essential — the Hungaroring is unusually tough on brakes, and without the fix the team likely wouldn't have finished the race.
key_points: Colton Herta drives Cadillac's car in Hungary FP1, replacing Bottas
It's his second F1 practice session this year, after his Barcelona debut
Cadillac brings an upgraded brakes package — Bottas said without it they might not finish the race
Part of F1's rule requiring teams to give rookies practice running

depth.background: Cadillac is a brand-new F1 team debuting in the 2026 season, led by veteran drivers Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Pérez. F1 rules require every team to hand a rookie driver at least two practice sessions per season, which is how Colton Herta — an American F2 driver and former IndyCar racer — gets his seat time. He made his first Cadillac appearance in Barcelona.

stories.title: India's ₹5,000 crore highway-investment trust IPO closes today — its biggest InvIT listing bid yet
stories.what_happened: Cube Highways Trust's InvIT public offer, which opened July 22, closes today at a price band of ₹151-152 per unit, targeting roughly ₹5,000 crore. The entire issue is an offer-for-sale of about 32.9 crore units by existing unit-holders — the trust itself raises no fresh money from this sale. Qualified institutional buyers get 75% of the allocation and high-net-worth investors get the rest; ordinary retail investors have zero allocated quota. Units are set to begin trading on the NSE and BSE on July 29.
key_points: Cube Highways Trust's ₹5,000 crore public offer closes today, priced at ₹151-152 a unit
It's an offer-for-sale — existing owners cashing out, not new money for building roads
Institutional investors get 75% of the units; ordinary retail investors get none
Units list on the NSE and BSE on July 29

depth.background: An InvIT (Infrastructure Investment Trust) is a vehicle that owns income-generating infrastructure — in this case, operating toll roads — and passes most of the toll income straight through to unit-holders as regular payouts, similar to how a REIT works for buildings. Cube Highways, backed by global infrastructure investor I Squared Capital, owns a portfolio of operating toll highways across India.

stories.title: F1 eyes a surprise return to Malaysia's Sepang circuit to fill the hole the Middle East war left in its calendar
stories.what_happened: F1 is now in discussions with Malaysian organisers about staging a one-off race at Sepang, most likely around October 4 — fitting into a gap between the Azerbaijan Grand Prix (September 26) and the Singapore Grand Prix (October 11). Malaysia's government has confirmed it is formally studying the proposal. Sepang has emerged as the front-runner over other options like Portugal's Portimão largely because its circuit sits next to an international airport, making the fast turnaround F1 needs on short notice far more practical.
key_points: Sepang is the leading candidate for a stand-in race around October 4, slotted between Baku and Singapore
It would replace the Bahrain Grand Prix, cancelled back in March along with the Saudi Arabian round
Malaysia's government confirms it's assessing hosting a race — the country hasn't held an F1 round since 2017
Sepang's airport-adjacent location makes a quick-turnaround event more logistically realistic than rival option Portugal's Portimão

depth.background: F1's original 2026 calendar had 24 races, but the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix, both scheduled for mid-April, were scrapped in March as the conflict between the US, Israel and Iran escalated in the region — shrinking the season to 22 rounds. Sepang International Circuit, just outside Kuala Lumpur, hosted F1 every year from 1999 to 2017 before dropping off the calendar and has been rumoured as a comeback venue on and off ever since.

stories.title: West Bengal votes today to fill three Rajya Sabha seats vacated by TMC rebels — BJP is expected to sweep them all
stories.what_happened: Bypolls for the three vacated West Bengal Rajya Sabha seats are being voted on and counted today, July 24. With BJP holding 207 of the state assembly's 293 seats, the party is widely expected to win all three, since West Bengal's MLAs — not the general public — cast the votes.
key_points: Voting and counting happen today for 3 Rajya Sabha seats from West Bengal
Seats fell vacant after three sitting TMC MPs — Sukhendu Sekhar Roy, Sushmita Dev, and Prakash Chik Baraik — resigned in June
All three quit after publicly questioning TMC's leadership following the party's defeat in West Bengal's assembly election
BJP holds 207 of 293 West Bengal assembly seats, making it near-certain to win all three — since state MLAs, not the public, vote for these seats

depth.background: India's Parliament has two houses: the Lok Sabha, elected directly by voters, and the Rajya Sabha, whose members are instead elected indirectly by sitting state assembly MLAs — so a party's strength in a state assembly translates into seats in Delhi's upper house too, just with a delay. West Bengal recently held state assembly elections, which BJP won decisively; these three Rajya Sabha seats are the first concrete national payoff of that state win, after the sitting TMC MPs holding them resigned rather than stay loyal to a defeated state leadership.

stories.title: Parliament moves to permanently expand the Supreme Court from 33 to 37 judges, replacing a Modi government ordinance
stories.what_happened: Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal moved the Bill in the Lok Sabha for consideration and passing, seeking to convert May's temporary ordinance into permanent law and lock in the top court's new strength of 37 judges.
key_points: Lok Sabha takes up the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026 for final consideration and passing today
It raises the Supreme Court's sanctioned strength from 33 to 37 judges (excluding the Chief Justice of India)
It replaces an ordinance President Droupadi Murmu signed on May 16, after the Cabinet approved the expansion on May 5
It needs only a simple majority — Article 124 of the Constitution lets Parliament set judge numbers by ordinary law, not a constitutional amendment
It comes as Opposition members keep up protests over the NEET-UG paper-leak row and a Ram Mandir donation embezzlement case

depth.background: India's Supreme Court has a fixed, government-set number of judges, and a growing backlog of pending cases has long fuelled calls to add more. When Parliament isn't in session, the government can issue an ordinance — a temporary law with immediate effect — but it must get Parliament's approval within months or it automatically lapses. That's what forced this Bill onto the agenda now, during the Monsoon Session.

stories.title: Trent Rockets edge out Birmingham Phoenix by 6 wickets in a low-scoring Hundred thriller at Edgbaston
stories.what_happened: Birmingham Phoenix were restricted to 122 for 6 in their innings at Edgbaston. Trent Rockets chased the target down comfortably enough, finishing on 123 for 4, winning by 6 wickets.
key_points: Birmingham Phoenix posted 122/6 from their 100 balls
Trent Rockets chased the target down for the loss of just 4 wickets
It was the 4th match of The Hundred Men's Competition 2026
A tight, bowler-friendly Edgbaston pitch made the modest target harder to defend than it looked

depth.background: The Hundred is an English franchise cricket competition launched in 2021, where each side faces 100 balls per innings — slightly shorter than the 120-ball T20 format — designed to be fast-paced and easy for newcomers to follow. Eight city-based teams compete each English summer.

stories.title: Lewis Hamilton pays for skipping Ferrari's simulator — only Charles Leclerc gets to test the team's new rear wing in Hungary practice
stories.what_happened: At Friday practice for the Hungarian Grand Prix, Ferrari let only Leclerc run the team's new 'Macarena' rear wing, because he'd already built confidence with it on the simulator. Hamilton, who opted out of simulator work months ago, is sticking with the wing spec he raced at Spa last weekend instead.
key_points: Only Charles Leclerc trials Ferrari's updated 'Macarena' rear wing in first practice at the Hungaroring
Hamilton keeps running the older wing spec he used last weekend at Spa
Reason: Hamilton stopped using Ferrari's driving simulator ahead of May's Canadian GP, saying it can 'mislead' a driver more than it helps
Leclerc, by contrast, leans heavily on the simulator and had already logged laps with the new wing there
The Hungaroring's tight, high-downforce corners reward the new wing far more than Spa's high-speed layout did

depth.background: A rear wing shapes how much downforce (the force pushing a car onto the track, helping it corner faster) a car generates — teams constantly tweak the design and test changes in a simulator (a motion-and-screen rig that mimics a car's handling) before risking them in a real session. Hamilton has been skeptical of simulators since 1997, saying they can teach bad habits that don't match the real car; Leclerc uses Ferrari's simulator extensively to prepare.

stories.title: SpaceX tries again to launch Starship on its 13th test flight — this time carrying real satellites for the first time
stories.what_happened: SpaceX says it has fixed the issue behind last week's aborted launch, replacing several engines and updating the rocket's propulsion system. After slipping from July 23, the company is now targeting a liftoff around 6:45 p.m. ET today from Starbase, Texas. The flight's headline goal is to deploy 20 production Starlink V3 satellites — SpaceX's newest, higher-capacity internet satellites — the first time Starship has released real payloads rather than dummy simulators.
key_points: SpaceX is targeting Friday (today) for Starship's 13th test flight after a launch-pad abort last week
For the first time, Starship will try to deploy real payloads: 20 production Starlink V3 satellites
Engineers replaced several engines and reworked the propulsion system after the abort
Weather, not hardware, is now the main risk to today's launch window

depth.background: Starship is SpaceX's giant, fully reusable next-generation rocket, central to both its Mars ambitions and NASA's Artemis Moon-lander plans (which we covered separately). The program has flown a dozen prior test flights with mixed results, including explosions. On July 16, this 13th test flight was aborted less than a second before liftoff when several engines failed to ignite.

stories.title: Commonwealth Games 2026: India's para-lifters get their first real shot at a podium finish today
stories.what_happened: On day 2 of the Games, seven Indian para-powerlifters are competing in finals at the SEC Armadillo — India's first real shot at a para-powerlifting podium finish this edition. Separately, Olympian swimmer Srihari Nataraj lines up in heat 4 of the men's 50m backstroke, and India's boxing campaign proper begins with Jadumani Singh facing Scotland's Aaron Cullen in the men's 55kg round of 32.
key_points: Seven Indian para-powerlifters compete in finals at Glasgow's SEC Armadillo today
It's India's first genuine medal opportunity in the sport at these Games
Swimmer Srihari Nataraj also races in the men's 50m backstroke heats
India is already guaranteed one medal via Lovlina Borgohain's boxing bye

depth.background: The Commonwealth Games 2026 opened in Glasgow this week, with India sending a large contingent across boxing, swimming, weightlifting, gymnastics and more. Lovlina Borgohain has already secured India at least one medal via a bye straight to the semi-finals — but that's an automatic result, not a won contest.

stories.title: Israel bombs Gaza City after ordering residents to flee — the ceasefire's latest gap
stories.what_happened: Israel issued evacuation warnings for people in four separate areas of Gaza, including near the Bureij and Jabalia refugee camps, and then struck those same areas, killing at least two Palestinians according to medical sources. One strike on Gaza City started a large fire that Civil Defence crews were still working to extinguish. Al Jazeera's correspondent on the ground said the pattern — warning people to flee, then hitting the area they were told to flee to or from — has become a recurring and alarming feature of recent weeks.
key_points: Israel issued displacement orders for four areas of Gaza, then bombed them
At least two Palestinians were killed; a strike on Gaza City sparked a large fire
It's the latest in a pattern of strikes since the US-brokered ceasefire began in October 2025
Reporters note the warned-about areas were the ones actually hit

depth.background: A US-brokered ceasefire between Israel and Hamas took effect on 10 October 2025, meant to end nearly two years of war in Gaza. In practice, though, Israeli strikes, demolitions, and displacement orders have continued at a lower intensity ever since, and rights groups say the humanitarian situation in Gaza remains dire — the territory's population has repeatedly been ordered to move from one area to another as the fighting has continued in bursts.

stories.title: 18-year-old Kimi Antonelli is guaranteed to lead the F1 title race into the summer break — and says he's 'getting the confidence back'
stories.what_happened: Antonelli heads into the Hungarian Grand Prix already guaranteed to carry the championship lead into the summer break, regardless of this weekend's result, holding a 45-point cushion over Hamilton and 50 over his own teammate George Russell. He said he used the recent gap between races to rest and reset — doing things like driving his remote-control car — and that Friday's practice sessions left him 'getting the confidence back' with the Mercedes car.
key_points: Antonelli leads Hamilton by 45 points and teammate Russell by 50, with one race left before the break
At 18, he's the youngest points leader in F1 history
He says resting and doing hobbies helped him prepare mentally for this weekend
Friday practice in Hungary left him feeling he's 'getting the confidence back' in the Mercedes car

depth.background: Kimi Antonelli is a Mercedes rookie promoted into a race seat after Lewis Hamilton departed for Ferrari — and remarkably, he now leads the drivers' championship in his first full season. Because Hungary is the last race before F1's mandatory summer shutdown, whoever leads after this weekend is locked in as championship leader for a full month with no racing to change it.

stories.title: Modi's Cabinet clears a full anti-paper-leak Bill with fast-track courts, to be tabled in Parliament next week
stories.what_happened: The Union Cabinet met on Friday and finalized the contours of a Bill that provides for fast-track courts and stringent punishment for paper-leak offenders. Modi said the Bill will be introduced in Parliament next week and that the government will try to pass it as quickly as possible.
key_points: Union Cabinet finalizes a draft Bill with fast-track courts and stringent punishment for exam paper leaks
Modi says the government will try to pass it 'as early as possible' next week
Builds on his verbal fast-track-courts announcement from a day earlier
Comes as Parliament remains disrupted over the NEET paper-leak scandal

depth.background: India's NEET medical-entrance exam paper leak has fueled three weeks of protests by the 'Cockroach Janta Party' movement, demanding accountability and the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Yesterday, PM Modi announced the government would set up fast-track courts to punish paper-leak offenders swiftly — a first concession to the protest movement, though it stopped short of removing the minister. That announcement was a verbal commitment; today's Cabinet meeting is where the government had to turn it into an actual piece of draft legislation.

thread.previously: Yesterday, PM Modi verbally announced the government would set up fast-track courts to punish paper-leak offenders, as a first concession to three weeks of 'Cockroach Janta Party' protests over the NEET exam leak.
thread.changed: Today the Union Cabinet actually finalized a draft Bill with fast-track courts and stringent punishments, and Modi committed to introducing and trying to pass it in Parliament next week — turning yesterday's promise into a concrete legislative plan.

stories.title: Kuldeep Yadav signs with Yorkshire, becoming only the fifth Indian to play for the county
stories.what_happened: Kuldeep Yadav has signed an overseas deal with Yorkshire, one of English cricket's most storied county clubs. He'll play five One-Day Cup matches starting July 24, before leaving to join India's squad for their two-Test tour of Sri Lanka in August. He'll then return to Yorkshire in September to play the club's final three County Championship (first-class) matches of the season. He becomes only the fifth Indian to represent Yorkshire, following Sachin Tendulkar, Yuvraj Singh, Cheteshwar Pujara, and Mayank Agarwal.
key_points: Kuldeep joins Yorkshire as an overseas player for the One-Day Cup and County Championship
Plays five One-Day Cup matches from today before leaving for India's Sri Lanka Test tour
Returns in September for three more County Championship matches
Joins a short list of Indians for Yorkshire: Tendulkar, Yuvraj, Pujara, Mayank Agarwal

depth.background: India's left-arm wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav has recently found himself in and out of India's white-ball plans, missing out on some Team India selections. English county cricket has long been a place where international players — including a handful of high-profile Indians — sign short overseas stints to stay match-fit and sharpen their game between international assignments, playing in England's domestic first-class (County Championship) and one-day (One-Day Cup) competitions.

stories.title: Five drivers — including title contenders Antonelli and Piastri — sit out Hungary's first practice as F1 hands rookies the wheel
stories.what_happened: At Friday's first practice for the Hungarian Grand Prix, five regular drivers sat out in favour of younger or reserve drivers: McLaren handed Oscar Piastri's car to 21-year-old Leonardo Fornaroli, Mercedes gave championship leader Kimi Antonelli's car to reserve Frederik Vesti, and Cadillac put IndyCar convert Colton Herta in Valtteri Bottas's seat for his second F1 practice outing of the season. The regular drivers all return for the more representative FP2 session later Friday.
key_points: Championship leader Antonelli and McLaren's Piastri both skip FP1 at the Hungaroring
Their seats go to reserve/development drivers, including Fornaroli and Vesti
Colton Herta, the American IndyCar convert, gets his second Cadillac practice outing
F1 rules require every team to give young/reserve drivers track time twice a season

depth.background: F1 rules require every team to run a driver who has started two or fewer grands prix in at least two free-practice sessions across the season — a way of giving young talent real seat time in a current F1 car. Teams typically pick low-stakes sessions like FP1 (rather than the more important FP2, which sets up qualifying and the race) to fulfil this.

stories.title: Japan's 40-year bond yield jumps toward a record high as inflation fears mount
stories.what_happened: Japan's 40-year government bond yield led gains across all maturities on July 24, climbing 10 basis points to 4.01% — nearing the record 4.355% touched in May. The move tracked a rise in US Treasury yields, which climbed as higher oil prices (partly driven by the US-Iran conflict) fed bets that the US Federal Reserve may need to keep interest rates higher for longer to fight inflation.
key_points: Japan's 40-year government bond yield rose 10 basis points to 4.01%
That's closing in on its all-time high of 4.355% hit in May
The 5-year yield also hit its highest level since it was first issued in 2000
Rising US Treasury yields and higher oil prices are dragging Japanese yields up too

depth.background: A bond's 'yield' is the return an investor gets for lending money to a government — yields rise when investors demand more compensation, usually because they fear inflation will erode the value of fixed interest payments, or because they expect the central bank to raise interest rates. Japan spent decades with ultra-low, near-zero yields, so a 40-year yield above 4% is a historic shift for a market long known for rock-bottom rates.

stories.title: India opens its Commonwealth Games 2026 medal account as Mirabai Chanu chases a historic third gold
stories.what_happened: India's first medal of the Games came from para-powerlifter Jhandu Kumar, who won bronze in the men's heavyweight category on Day 1. India then had a quiet Day 2 without further medals, leaving the country tied for 10th in the overall table. Today, Mirabai Chanu contests the women's 48kg weightlifting final, aiming to become just the second Indian in the sport's Commonwealth history to win three straight golds.
key_points: Para-powerlifter Jhandu Kumar won India's first medal — a bronze — on Day 1
India sits joint-10th in the medal table after two days, behind medal leader Australia
Star weightlifter Mirabai Chanu goes for the women's 48kg gold today
A win would be Chanu's third straight Commonwealth gold, after 2018 and 2022

depth.background: The 2026 Commonwealth Games are being held in Glasgow, Scotland, running through early August. Mirabai Chanu is India's most decorated weightlifter — an Olympic silver medallist and two-time Commonwealth Games gold medallist (2018, 2022) — who missed this year's Asian Championships while recovering from a shoulder injury.

stories.title: Sensex slides for a fifth straight session as Brent crude tops $100 a barrel on the Iran war
stories.what_happened: India's Sensex fell for a fifth consecutive session, closing at 76,059.77 (down 0.43%), while the Nifty 50 slipped to 23,767.45. The selling was concentrated in auto, metal, and energy stocks, while IT and media shares partly offset the decline. The trigger was Brent crude oil crossing $100 a barrel for the first time since May, after Yemen's Houthi forces attacked Saudi Aramco's Jazan and Yanbu oil facilities in an escalation of the US-Iran conflict.
key_points: Sensex closed at 76,059.77, down 331.62 points (0.43%), its fifth losing session in a row
Nifty 50 fell 102.15 points (0.43%) to 23,767.45
Auto, metal and energy stocks led losses; IT and media stocks gained
Brent crude crossed $100/barrel for the first time since May after Houthi attacks on Saudi oil sites

depth.background: India imports roughly 85% of the crude oil it uses, making it one of the world's most oil-import-dependent large economies. When global oil prices rise, India pays more dollars for the same barrels, which widens its trade deficit (the gap between what it imports and exports), weakens the rupee, and pushes up domestic inflation — since fuel costs ripple through transport, manufacturing, and food prices. The Sensex and Nifty 50 are India's two benchmark stock indices, tracking its most valuable listed companies.

stories.title: India bars telecom infrastructure firms from storing or sharing network data outside the country
stories.what_happened: The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) notified a new authorisation framework requiring communication infrastructure providers — including cloud-hosted telecom network operators, mobile tower and internet exchange point providers, and satellite earth station gateway operators — to store all telecommunication data, logs and related information exclusively within India. No copies can be routed, shared, or made available outside the country. The notification is dated July 20 and applies to companies seeking authorisation under the new framework.
key_points: New DoT authorisation framework covers cloud telecom networks, mobile towers, satellite gateways
All telecom data, logs and information must now be stored inside India
No copies may be routed, shared, or made accessible outside India
Part of a shift from telecom licensing to a regulatory framework under the Telecommunications Act, 2023

depth.background: India has been steadily tightening rules on where digital and telecom data can physically sit, arguing that keeping sensitive infrastructure data inside the country protects national security and gives regulators direct oversight. The Telecommunications Act, 2023 replaced decades-old colonial-era telecom law and gave the government power to set up new regulatory frameworks like this one, moving away from case-by-case licensing toward standing rules that apply to a whole category of company.

stories.title: AIADMK's Palaniswami to meet PM Modi on July 26 as strain shows in the BJP alliance ahead of Tamil Nadu's 2026 election
stories.what_happened: Palaniswami is set to meet Prime Minister Modi on July 26 in Tiruchirapalli during Modi's visit to the state — their first meeting since the alliance came back together in 2025. The meeting comes amid visible tension inside the alliance: AIADMK has been saying it expects to form a majority government on its own if the alliance wins in 2026, while senior BJP leaders, including Home Minister Amit Shah, have publicly said any win would produce a coalition government with the BJP playing an integral role.
key_points: AIADMK chief Palaniswami meets Modi in Tiruchirapalli on July 26 — their first since the alliance reformed
Under their March seat-sharing deal, AIADMK contests 178 seats, BJP 27, allies the rest
AIADMK says it will form the government alone; BJP leaders insist it'll be a coalition
Palaniswami has grown 'more assertive' publicly on the power-sharing question in recent weeks

depth.background: The AIADMK (All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam) is one of Tamil Nadu's two dominant regional parties, historically trading power with the DMK. It split from the BJP-led national alliance in 2023-24 but the two parties patched things up and announced a fresh alliance for Tamil Nadu's 2026 assembly election, with a seat-sharing agreement finalized in March: AIADMK gets 178 of the seats to contest, BJP 27, with smaller allies splitting the rest. Palaniswami (often called EPS) is a former Tamil Nadu chief minister and AIADMK's general secretary.

stories.title: Parliament moves to make disrupting Vande Mataram a criminal offence, just like insulting the national anthem
stories.what_happened: The government introduced the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026 in the Rajya Sabha on July 24, moved by Minister of State for Home Affairs Nityanand Rai. It seeks to make intentionally obstructing or disturbing the singing of Vande Mataram a criminal offence, bringing it under the same legal protection the 1971 Act already gives the National Anthem. The bill's introduction was passed by voice vote despite loud opposition objections in the House.
key_points: Government introduces a bill giving India's national song the same legal shield as the anthem
Passed introduction stage in the Rajya Sabha by voice vote amid noisy protest
Opposition says it risks criminalizing free speech and political expression
Comes during 2026, the 150th anniversary year of Vande Mataram's composition

depth.background: India has two distinct patriotic songs: 'Jana Gana Mana,' the National Anthem, and 'Vande Mataram,' the National Song, first written in the 1870s and adopted as a symbol of the independence movement. Only insults to the Anthem are currently a criminal offence under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 — Vande Mataram has cultural but not equivalent legal protection. 2026 marks the song's 150th anniversary, which the government has used as a platform for events and, now, this legislation.

stories.title: NEET protests: government offers compensation and drops FIRs, but still won't remove minister Pradhan as Saturday deadline arrives
stories.what_happened: In a second round of talks, the Centre gave in-principle approval to two of the protesters' demands: compensating the families of students who died by suicide over the leak, and withdrawing FIRs and cases against protesting students. But it held firm on refusing to remove Pradhan, which the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) — the group leading the protests — has called non-negotiable. A third round of talks is scheduled for Saturday.
key_points: A third round of talks between the CJP-led protesters and the Centre is set for Saturday (today)
Government has agreed in-principle to compensate families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide
It has also agreed to withdraw FIRs and legal cases filed against protesting students
Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation — the protesters' central demand — remains off the table

depth.background: Protests erupted after a leak in the NEET medical-entrance exam, and have grown into one of India's largest youth-led movements in years. This week we reported the government told protesters Pradhan would not resign but promised to fix problems at the National Testing Agency (NTA), and set Saturday as the deadline for a 'final word' — a deadline that arrives today.

thread.previously: We reported that the government told protesters Pradhan would not resign, promised to resolve NTA-related issues instead, and set Saturday as the deadline for a final word.
thread.changed: In a further round of talks, the government went beyond process fixes — offering compensation for victims' families and agreeing to withdraw FIRs against students — but it still refused Pradhan's resignation, with the real test coming in today's third round of talks.

prev_ref.title: Government tells NEET protesters Education Minister Pradhan will not resign, sets Saturday deadline for a final word

stories.title: Sonam Wangchuk ends his 26-day hunger strike as the government agrees to compensate NEET-leak victims' families
stories.what_happened: After 26 days without food, Wangchuk ended his hunger strike following fresh government assurances: compensation for the families of students who died by suicide linked to the paper leak, and no legal action against the protesters. Delhi Metro shut 17 stations this week as crowds around Jantar Mantar swelled, and the government has asked for until tomorrow to decide whether Pradhan will resign.
key_points: Wangchuk ends a 26-day fast at Jantar Mantar after government assurances
The Centre agrees to compensate families of students who died by suicide over the NEET paper leak
Government won't pursue legal action against protesters, but wants a day to decide on Education Minister Pradhan's resignation
Delhi Metro had shut 17 stations this week as the protests swelled

depth.background: The Cockroach Janta Party-led protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar began on June 6 over the 2026 NEET-UG medical entrance exam paper leak and alleged CBSE on-screen marking irregularities. Ladakh-based education reformer and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk — known for earlier hunger strikes over Ladakh's statehood demand — joined the students' fast on June 28 in solidarity, demanding Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and broader reform of how national exams are run.

thread.previously: Parliament was adjourned twice this week as Congress demanded Amit Shah and the education minister resign over police action against NEET-leak protesters, while Mumbai's trains were disrupted and police banned further protests through August 6.
thread.changed: The standoff's most prominent figure, Sonam Wangchuk, has now ended his 26-day hunger strike after the government agreed to compensate victims' families and hold off legal action — with a decision on the minister's resignation still pending.

prev_ref.title: Parliament twice adjourned as Congress demands Amit Shah and the education minister resign over police action on protesting students

stories.title: Bajaj Finance's profit jumps 22% to ₹4,765 crore, showing India's consumer-lending engine is still humming
stories.what_happened: For the quarter ending June 2026, Bajaj Finance reported consolidated net profit of ₹4,765 crore, up 22% from a year earlier, on net interest income of ₹10,227 crore, also up 22%. At the same time, the amount it set aside for loans that might go bad rose even faster, 26%, to ₹2,120 crore.
key_points: Net profit up 22% year-on-year to ₹4,765 crore in Q1 FY26
Net interest income (its core lending margin) rose 22% to ₹10,227 crore
But loan-loss provisions grew even faster — up 26% to ₹2,120 crore
Results land the same week Sensex and Nifty are sliding on oil and global jitters

depth.background: Bajaj Finance is India's largest NBFC (non-banking financial company) — a lender that isn't a bank but still issues loans, here mostly for consumer goods, personal credit, and small businesses. Because so much of the Indian middle class borrows through it, its results are widely watched as a bellwether for how confident Indian consumers feel about spending and borrowing.

stories.title: Parliament twice adjourned as Congress demands Amit Shah and the education minister resign over police action on protesting students
stories.what_happened: On the third day of Parliament's monsoon session, Congress MPs wore black in protest and disrupted proceedings, demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the continuing paper-leak crisis and of Home Minister Amit Shah over the police response to the July 20 student march. Both houses were adjourned as the opposition pressed for a full discussion on the police action, while the government has separately introduced a tougher anti-paper-leak bill this week.
key_points: Both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha adjourned for a third straight day amid opposition protests
Congress MPs dressed in black, demanding Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation
The protests stem from police using lathi charges, water cannons and tear gas on students at a July 20 march
Opposition also wants Home Minister Amit Shah to make a statement in Parliament on the police action

depth.background: The protests trace back to India's recurring exam paper-leak scandal, which has fueled student anger for weeks and already forced out the Higher Education Secretary. On July 20, students marched on Parliament ('Chalo Sansad') demanding accountability; opposition parties and student groups say police responded with disproportionate force, including lathi (baton) charges and detentions, and several students were hospitalised.

stories.title: Verstappen escapes penalty, Sainz warned after tense brake-test standoff in Hungary practice
stories.what_happened: During Friday practice for the Hungarian Grand Prix, Williams driver Carlos Sainz was warming his brakes on the racing line on the straight between Turns 11 and 12 when Max Verstappen's Red Bull arrived and had to take avoiding action. Verstappen then appeared to retaliate by deliberately slowing on the exit of Turn 13, blocking both Sainz and Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto. Sainz told stewards he had lost radio contact with his team and hadn't heard warnings that Verstappen was approaching. Stewards ruled Sainz should not have been on the racing line regardless, and issued him a formal warning; Verstappen was not punished, partly because Sainz said Verstappen's slowing hadn't actually affected him.
key_points: Sainz was warming his brakes on the racing line with a broken team radio
Verstappen had to swerve to avoid him, then appeared to retaliate by slowing deliberately
Stewards handed Sainz a warning; Verstappen faced no further action
Set the tone for a chaotic, penalty-filled Hungarian GP weekend

depth.background: F1 cars often 'warm' their brakes and tyres in specific zones during practice, usually off the racing line so faster cars can pass safely. The Hungaroring is a tight, low-speed circuit where cars run close together and overtaking room is scarce, which makes incidents like this more likely.

stories.title: Le Mans winner Ryo Hirakawa gets a second F1 outing for Haas in Bearman's car
stories.what_happened: Ryo Hirakawa, a 2022 Le Mans 24 Hours winner and Haas's test and reserve driver, took over Bearman's car for the first practice session at the Hungarian Grand Prix — his second FP1 appearance this year after one in Austria that was disrupted by a red flag and aerodynamic testing. The Hungary outing gave him a fuller opportunity to run representative laps and hand engineers useful data.
key_points: Hirakawa drove Ollie Bearman's Haas in first practice (FP1) at the Hungarian Grand Prix
It was his second FP1 outing of the season, after Austria
He's Haas's official test/reserve driver while racing for Toyota in endurance racing
The session helps Haas gather setup data on its VF-26 car

depth.background: F1 rules require teams to give rookie or reserve drivers a certain number of practice-session outings each season, using one of the two race drivers' cars for that session only. We've reported that Haas is weighing Ollie Bearman against Esteban Ocon for its 2027 driver lineup, with Bearman currently outperforming Ocon on track.

stories.title: Ferrari sweeps both Friday practice sessions in Hungary, and Mercedes' Russell says their worst fears are confirmed
stories.what_happened: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc set the fastest FP1 time (1:19.075 on soft tyres), and teammate Lewis Hamilton topped FP2 with a 1:18.729, 0.148 seconds quicker than Leclerc, with Lando Norris third for McLaren nearly half a second off the pace. Ferrari was fastest on both the soft and medium tyre compounds across the day at the Hungaroring.
key_points: Charles Leclerc topped FP1 with a 1:19.075, Lewis Hamilton topped FP2 with a 1:18.729
Hamilton beat Leclerc by 0.148s in FP2; Norris was third for McLaren, half a second back
Ferrari was quickest on both soft and medium tyres across the day
Mercedes' George Russell said it confirmed the team's fears about Ferrari's raw pace

depth.background: Friday practice sessions (FP1 and FP2) are a team's first real look at how their car behaves on a given track before the following day's qualifying and Sunday's race — teams use them to test tyre performance, fuel loads, and setup changes rather than chase outright lap times, but a team that's clearly fastest on both tyre compounds is sending a genuine signal about race pace, not just a one-lap sprint.

stories.title: Carlos Sainz calls Williams' 2026 season 'incredibly frustrating' after a reversal from a strong 2025
stories.what_happened: Speaking at Thursday's Hungarian Grand Prix media day, Carlos Sainz gave a blunt assessment of Williams' 2026 campaign, calling it 'incredibly frustrating and very disappointing' compared to the team's strong 2025. He pointed to the new FW48 chassis arriving overweight and behind schedule — Williams was the only team on the grid that failed to complete a single lap during pre-season testing in Barcelona. Both Sainz and teammate Alex Albon finished outside the points at last week's Belgian Grand Prix.
key_points: Sainz says Williams' 2026 results are 'incredibly frustrating and very disappointing'
New FW48 car arrived overweight and badly delayed
Williams was the only team that failed to complete a lap during pre-season testing in Barcelona
Both Sainz and teammate Albon finished outside the points at last week's Belgian GP

depth.background: Williams enjoyed a genuine resurgence in 2025 after years in the midfield doldrums, which raised expectations heading into 2026 — a season where F1 also introduced a major new set of technical rules that reshuffled the competitive order across the whole grid. How a team handles that kind of rules reset often determines its fortunes for years afterward.

stories.title: Birmingham Phoenix loses Mustafizur Rahman to injury before his first-ever Hundred appearance
stories.what_happened: Bangladesh pace bowler Mustafizur Rahman, who had signed with Birmingham Phoenix for £100,000 and was set to become the first Bangladeshi cricketer to play in The Hundred, has been ruled out for at least four weeks after suffering a grade-1 hamstring tear during Bangladesh's first ODI against Zimbabwe while on international duty. Birmingham Phoenix have brought in Australian left-arm pacer Ben Dwarshuis as his replacement — his second stint with the franchise after playing one match for them in 2022 — following a strong run of 16 wickets in 8 matches for Washington Freedom in Major League Cricket.
key_points: Mustafizur Rahman, signed for £100,000, would have been the first Bangladeshi to play in The Hundred
He's ruled out at least 4 weeks with a grade-1 hamstring tear suffered during an ODI against Zimbabwe on international duty
Birmingham Phoenix have signed Australian pacer Ben Dwarshuis as his replacement
Dwarshuis returns to Phoenix after one match in 2022, fresh off 16 wickets in 8 Major League Cricket matches

depth.background: The Hundred is England's short-format domestic competition that draws overseas stars for a few weeks each English summer; signing a country's first-ever representative in the tournament, as Phoenix had done with Mustafizur, is a genuine box-office and cricketing milestone for a franchise. Losing that player to injury before he even takes the field is a significant blow to both the player's individual milestone and the team's plans.

stories.title: Trent Rockets bowl out Birmingham Phoenix Women for just 64 — the joint-second lowest total in Hundred history
stories.what_happened: Birmingham Phoenix Women collapsed to just 64 all out against Trent Rockets at Edgbaston — the joint-second lowest total in the women's competition's history — with debutant Samantha Bates (3 for 10) and Georgia Elwiss (3 for 13) combining for 6 wickets for just 23 runs. Trent Rockets knocked off the target with 69 balls to spare, led by Sophia Dunkley's unbeaten 43 off 17 balls.
key_points: Birmingham Phoenix Women collapse to 64 all out at Edgbaston
Samantha Bates (3/10, on Hundred debut) and Georgia Elwiss (3/13) share 6 wickets for 23 runs
Trent Rockets chase it down for a 9-wicket win, with 69 balls to spare
Sophia Dunkley finishes unbeaten on 43 off just 17 balls

depth.background: The Hundred is England's short-format cricket competition where each team faces 100 balls per innings (rather than the usual 120-ball T20 over count), with men's and women's tournaments running in parallel each summer — designed to be fast, high-scoring, and easy for newcomers to follow.

stories.title: West Indies pace bowler Alzarri Joseph 'declines selection' for the Pakistan Tests — coach Sammy calls it a big loss
stories.what_happened: Cricket West Indies initially said Alzarri Joseph was 'unavailable for selection due to personal reasons' when it announced the Test squad for the home series against Pakistan. Head coach Darren Sammy later clarified that Joseph had, in fact, 'declined selection' — a more pointed admission that the player chose not to be picked rather than being unavailable. Sammy called it a 'big loss' given Joseph's six wickets in the recent two-Test series win over Sri Lanka, and said the question of how the board handles contracted players declining selection is a decision for CWI's directors, not him.
key_points: Joseph took 6 wickets in 2 Tests against Sri Lanka but won't play the Pakistan series
Cricket West Indies first cited 'personal reasons'; coach Darren Sammy later confirmed he 'declined selection'
Sammy says the decision on how contracted players can decline selection is 'beyond his head'
West Indies' pace attack for Pakistan now leans on Shamar Joseph, Kemar Roach and Jayden Seales

depth.background: Alzarri Joseph is one of West Indies' senior fast bowlers and had been in good recent form, including a key role in a Test series win over Sri Lanka. West Indies players are centrally contracted through Cricket West Indies (CWI), which is meant to give the board control over player availability for international duty — but the system still allows disputes over pay, workload or personal circumstances to occasionally lead a contracted player to step away from a series, which is what's happened here ahead of the Pakistan Tests, starting in Trinidad.

stories.title: Bumrah ruled out of full training until July 30 as selectors weigh his fitness for the Sri Lanka Tests
stories.what_happened: Scans on July 24 found continued soreness in Bumrah's left knee, and doctors gave him an anti-inflammatory injection to manage it. India's team management has advised him to rest completely until July 30, after which he'll travel to the National Cricket Academy's Centre of Excellence for rehabilitation and a final fitness clearance from the medical board. The two-Test series in Sri Lanka starts August 15 in Colombo; the squad is due there by August 4 for an acclimatisation match, leaving a tight but workable window for Bumrah to prove his fitness before the squad is finalised this week.
key_points: Bumrah's left knee, hurt fielding in the England ODI series, showed fresh soreness on July 24 scans
Team management has told him to rest completely until July 30, then start rehab
India's two-Test series in Sri Lanka begins August 15; the squad reaches Colombo by August 4
Bumrah and Ravindra Jadeja are still expected to return to the Test squad if fitness clears

depth.background: Jasprit Bumrah is India's premier fast bowler and has become central to India's Test bowling attack, but has also dealt with recurring back and workload issues in recent years that have forced the team to manage his bowling carefully. He originally hurt his left knee fielding during the second ODI against England on July 17; he played on through that match, but swelling developed overnight and ruled him out of the third ODI. He and all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja were then rested entirely for India's one-off Test against Afghanistan to protect them for the bigger series ahead.

stories.title: Israel launches a major West Bank military operation after deadly settler-Palestinian clashes near Nablus kill six
stories.what_happened: On July 24, a group of Israeli settlers raided the Palestinian village of Tal near Nablus. A confrontation turned into a shootout after a Palestinian resident seized a settler's weapon, leaving four Palestinians and two Israelis dead. The killings triggered a wave of settler reprisal attacks on nearby Palestinian villages, and Israel's government announced a sweeping 'counterterrorism operation,' reinforcing troops in the area. Some Israeli officials publicly called for the destruction of Palestinian homes and villages in response.
key_points: Israeli settlers raided the Palestinian village of Tal near Nablus, sparking a shootout
Four Palestinians and two Israelis were killed in the July 24 clash
Israel's military is reinforcing troops for a 'major counterterrorism operation'
Human Rights Watch warns the West Bank is a 'powder keg' at risk of mass atrocities

depth.background: The West Bank is Palestinian territory Israel has militarily occupied since 1967; roughly 500,000 Israeli settlers now live there in communities most of the world considers illegal under international law, alongside about 3 million Palestinians. Settler attacks on Palestinian communities have been rising sharply since October 2022, and spiked further this year during the US-Israel war with Iran, with monitoring group Yesh Din recording 170 separate violent incidents in just the first 17 days after Israel's initial strikes on Iran.

stories.title: Supreme Court bars posting or monetizing live-streamed court hearings without permission, cracking down on viral clips
stories.what_happened: The Supreme Court directed that no live-streamed court proceedings can be extracted, edited, posted, reposted, circulated, monetized, or uploaded to social media or other digital platforms without prior permission from the Secretary General of the Supreme Court or the Registrar General of the relevant High Court. The order was framed as a direct response to courtroom moments being turned into viral entertainment content.
key_points: Top court says no more extracting, editing or reposting live-streamed hearings without permission
The rule covers social media and any platform, including monetized content
Permission must come from the Supreme Court's Secretary General or the relevant High Court's Registrar General
The court said flatly: 'there can't be 24x7 courtroom entertainment'

depth.background: India's Supreme Court began live-streaming select high-profile hearings in recent years specifically to make justice more transparent and accessible to the public. Since then, clips of dramatic courtroom exchanges have gone viral on YouTube and social media — sometimes edited or taken out of context, and sometimes monetized by channels with no connection to the case.

stories.title: HCLTech and Sarvam sign a ₹14,257 crore deal to build India's first Sovereign AI data center in Odisha
stories.what_happened: HCLTech, Sarvam and the Government of Odisha signed a memorandum of understanding to build an AI data center inside a new Odisha Sovereign AI Park, with a planned capital outlay of ₹14,257 crore. The signing was held in the presence of Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, along with senior state officials and executives from both companies.
key_points: HCLTech and Indian AI startup Sarvam will build a large AI data center in Odisha
The ₹14,257 crore (roughly $1.4 billion) project sits inside a new 'Odisha Sovereign AI Park'
Odisha CM Mohan Charan Majhi hosted the MoU signing with HCLTech and Sarvam executives
It's part of India's push to build home-grown AI computing power instead of relying on foreign clouds

depth.background: Almost all the powerful computing infrastructure that trains and runs today's AI models — including for Indian users and companies — sits in data centers owned by a handful of US and Chinese cloud giants. 'Sovereign AI' is the push by countries like India to build and control their own AI compute and data infrastructure domestically, both for economic reasons (capturing the investment and jobs) and strategic ones (not depending on foreign chip and cloud policy). Sarvam is one of India's homegrown AI startups building large language models tuned for Indian languages.

stories.title: US to resume Mexican cattle imports after a year-long ban, in a bid to bring down record beef prices
stories.what_happened: The US Department of Agriculture said it will begin a phased reopening of Mexican cattle imports, starting with the Douglas, Arizona port of entry on August 24, with two New Mexico ports following later, contingent on Mexico sticking to a screwworm-control plan. The move comes even though the screwworm the ban was meant to block was still detected on Texas and New Mexico farms in June — meaning the year-long closure did not fully succeed at keeping the parasite out.
key_points: US will phase in Mexican cattle imports starting Aug 24, over a year after halting them
The ban was meant to stop New World screwworm, a flesh-eating livestock parasite
It failed anyway — screwworm was found on Texas and New Mexico farms in June
Beef prices hit record highs partly because the ban cut US cattle supply

depth.background: The US suspended imports of live cattle from Mexico more than a year ago to try to keep out the New World screwworm — a parasite whose larvae burrow into and feed on the living flesh of livestock, and which had been spreading north through Central America. Mexican cattle are a meaningful part of the supply that feeds US feedlots, so cutting that off shrank the pool of cattle available to US ranchers and packers at the same time as beef demand stayed strong, pushing consumer beef prices to records and putting political pressure on the Trump administration to act.

stories.title: Monsoon floods swamp 400+ villages in Uttar Pradesh as four major rivers cross danger levels
stories.what_happened: Uttar Pradesh's disaster authorities issued a red alert for districts along the Hindon river (Baghpat, Gautam Buddh Nagar/Noida), the Ganga (Budaun), the Ghaghara (Ayodhya, Ballia), and the Gandak (Kushinagar), all of which are flowing above their warning marks. More than 400 villages have been swamped and over 4,000 hectares of farmland submerged. At least 12 people died in the last 24 hours from rain-related causes including lightning strikes, drowning, and snakebites. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed officials to visit affected areas and ensure compensation reaches affected families within 24 hours.
key_points: The Hindon, Ganga, Ghaghara and Gandak rivers are all flowing above their danger marks
More than 400 villages are flooded and 4,000+ hectares of farmland submerged
At least 12 people died in 24 hours from lightning, drowning, and snakebites
The state government has ordered compensation for affected families within 24 hours

depth.background: India's monsoon season (roughly June to September) brings the bulk of the country's annual rainfall, but also regularly triggers destructive flooding as rivers swell beyond their banks. This year's monsoon has already caused serious flooding in India's northeast, including in Assam, where the toll has climbed past 40 dead and hundreds of thousands affected.
